en.title: National Bank gives money to auditors' conference
en.body: National Bank of Malawi gave K5 million to help the Institute of Internal Auditors hold a big conference. The conference will be in Mangochi from 7 to 13 September. The bank said good governance is very important. Governance means leaders and rules that help an organization work well.
en.body_more:
The head of internal audit at National Bank, Noel Tomoka, said the bank gave money because trust is very important in banking. "We look after people's money. People must trust us," Tomoka said. He said National Bank has a long history with the Institute. Two of the people who started the Institute worked at National Bank.

The conference will bring together more than 600 people. They work in audit, risk management, and compliance. Compliance means following the rules. The conference theme is "The Currency of Trust: Governance as Strategy, Assurance as Proof." The conference will be at Sunbird Nkopola Lodge and Sun 'n' Sand Holiday Resort in Mangochi.

Albert Dambula is the chief executive of the Institute of Internal Auditors. He said thank you to National Bank. "The K5 million will help us pay for the conference," Dambula said. He said the conference will help organizations improve their controls and manage risks better.

The Institute will also host a big international conference in 2027. It will be in Lilongwe from 23 to 29 May. This will be the 13th African Federation of Institutes of Internal Auditors Conference. It will be at Bingu Wa Mutharika International Convention Centre.

en.title: Police and Magalasi disagree about charges
en.body: Police arrested Collins Magalasi on Monday. Magalasi was the chief of the Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority. The arrest is linked to the Amaryllis Hotel scandal. Police say they are still investigating. But Magalasi says he has been charged.
en.body_more:
Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwawula told reporters that Magalasi has NOT been formally charged yet. She said police officers are still working on the investigation. Chiwawula also refused to say where Magalasi is being held. She said telling reporters the location could harm the investigation.

But Magalasi told journalists a different story. Media workers found him at Area 3 Police Station after his arrest. He said: "I have been formally charged this morning." He added that police told him he would go to court the next day. Magalasi said he could give no more details about the charges.

Magalasi revealed he has been moved between three police stations. Police took him first to Lumbadzi Police Station. Then they moved him to Kanengo Police Station. Finally, they brought him to Area 3 Police Station. This is where journalists met him and heard his version of events.

The two accounts create confusion. Police say Magalasi is still under investigation and has not been charged. Magalasi says he was charged in the morning and will appear in court. This basic disagreement raises a key question: has Magalasi been formally charged with a crime, or is he still being investigated? The answer is not yet clear.

en.title: Army Soldier Gets 20 Years for Child Sexual Abuse
en.body: Diof Simaone, a 36-year-old soldier at Kamuzu Barracks in Lilongwe, was sentenced to 20 years in prison. He was found guilty of defiling a 15-year-old girl. The girl became pregnant. Senior Resident Magistrate Bracious Kondowe handed down the sentence on September 1, 2026.
en.body_more:
Simaone had sexual intercourse with the girl on four separate occasions. These happened between April and August 2025. Three times the abuse happened at a guest house in Area 44. One time it happened at his home. The girl became pregnant and gave birth to a baby boy in January 2026.

Simaone told the girl's mother about the pregnancy. The mother works as a cleaner at Kamuzu Barracks. He promised to give money to help support the girl and her child. But he did not give the money. The mother then went to the police at Area 23 Police Unit and reported what happened. Simaone was arrested and charged with defilement. Defilement means having sexual contact with a child under 16 years old.

During the trial, Simaone said he was not guilty. The court heard evidence from four witnesses from the government side. After the trial, the court found him guilty on August 28, 2026. When the judge gave the sentence, Simaone asked for forgiveness. He said going to prison would make it hard for him to help the girl and her baby. He said sorry to the girl, her mother, the court and the nation. But the judge said no. The prosecutor asked for a harsh sentence because Simaone was a soldier and should have protected the girl, not hurt her. The judge said the 20-year sentence is a warning to all people in positions of power that they cannot abuse children.

en.title: Malawi's Navicha reaches Beauty With a Purpose top 24
en.body: Ireen Navicha, Malawi's representative at Miss World 2026, has made the top 24 finalists in the Beauty With a Purpose challenge. She is one of the top six contestants from Africa. The competition is taking place in Vietnam. Navicha now has a chance to reach the top 40 of the main pageant if she wins this category.
en.body_more:
The Beauty With a Purpose challenge gives winners an automatic place in the top 40. Navicha presented a project called 'When a Mother is a Child'. This project helps young mothers return to school.

Through her work with the Greynavies Foundation, Navicha has helped 432 girls go back to school. She gives them support like school fees, learning materials and a place to stay. She visits villages across Malawi to find girls who left school because of early marriage or teenage pregnancy. She talks to them and encourages them to come back to learning.

Stephen Mdala is the public relations officer for Miss Malawi Organisation. He said Navicha's selection in the top 24 is good news for Malawi. He said it gives her another chance to reach the top 40. Mdala explained that Navicha did not make the final stages in some other challenges. These challenges were Head to Head, Top Model, Top Chef, Sports and Talent.

The final of the Miss World competition will take place on September 5 in Nha Trang, Vietnam. Many people in Malawi have praised Navicha for her confidence and her work to help young girls. She speaks English well and has shown she can represent Malawi on a world stage.

en.title: Malawi banks earn big profits in first half of 2026
en.body: Malawi's eight banks earned a total of K524 billion profit in the first half of 2026. Centenary Bank made K5.6 billion profit after tax for the six months ended 30 June 2026. CDH Investment Bank earned K41 billion profit, more than double its earnings from the same time last year.
en.body_more:
Centenary Bank's profit rose from K3.6 billion in the first half of 2025. The bank said more customers left money with them, which helped the bank lend more money to people. Assets grew to K274.9 billion. Money earned by the bank climbed to K32.7 billion, up from K20.9 billion one year before.

CDH Investment Bank's chief, Thoko Mkavea, said the bank worked hard and got good results. He said the bank will keep helping Malawi's economy grow. CDH's profit jumped 124 percent, which was the fastest growth among all banks.

Standard Bank made K67.5 billion profit. FDH Bank earned K86.418 billion. First Capital Bank got K67.5 billion profit. National Bank of Malawi earned K133.97 billion, the highest of all eight banks. NBS Bank made K90.23 billion profit. Ecobank Malawi earned K31.7 billion before tax.

Economist Marvin Banda said the banks' strong profits are good news. But he warned that the profits may come from high interest rates and money the banks invest in government bonds, not from lending to businesses. The wider economy still faces big problems. Prices rose 21.1 percent in June 2026. The country also has less foreign money to buy goods from outside. Banks said the second half of 2026 will stay hard.

en.title: Minister Phiri goes to China for training in governance
en.body: Minister of Local Government and Rural Development Dr Ben Phiri will spend the whole month of September in China. He will train at Peking University in Beijing. The training is about governance and public administration. Leaders from 48 countries will join him. Phiri said knowledge is very important for good government work.
en.body_more:
Phiri wrote on Facebook that he wanted to learn from the Chinese government. He said the month-long training will teach him about policy, leadership, local governance and development. He called this a big investment in his own knowledge. "Knowledge is power," Phiri wrote. "The greatest investment you can make is in knowledge and it is never a waste."

The minister said he would spend time with leaders from 48 countries around the world. They will all study together at the university. Phiri believes this experience will help him lead better in Malawi. He wants to bring new ideas about governance back home to his country.

Phiri is responsible for local government and rural development in Malawi. Local government means the councils and leaders in each district and town. Rural development means helping villages and farming areas grow and improve. By learning new ways, Phiri hopes to make these areas work better. He said the training will give him "immense knowledge" in these important areas. This is part of his work to strengthen local government across Malawi.

en.title: Kukoma Diamonds beat Tigresses in netball league
en.body: Kukoma Diamonds won two games this weekend. They beat FLC Netball Team 57-25 on Saturday. On Sunday they beat Tigresses 61-49 at Blantyre Sports Arena. This was Week Five of the FDH Premier Netball League first round.
en.body_more:
Head coach Noel Musa said his team played very well. "Both teams are big," he said. "We deserved the win because of the way we played." Musa told his players they must train hard and keep improving. "We will keep encouraging and training our players," he added.

Tigresses coach Peace Kalua said her team got better. "I am happy with the improvement we made," she said. But she said her team does not have enough players. "When a player gets tired or hurt, we cannot change them. This hurts us," she explained. Tigresses had won their game on Saturday. They beat Prison Queens 63-44.

On Sunday at the same place, other games also happened. Pacers beat FLC Netball Team 42-40. Prison Queens beat Giants NC 48-43. In the central region, Blue Eagles and Civonets drew 44-44. Kukoma Diamonds are now second in the league with 15 points from 8 games. Vanessa Sisters lead with one more point. They have played one more game. Blue Eagles are third with 14 points from 8 games. Blue Eagles won the first netball league in 2025.

en.title: Mighty Wanderers suspend coach Bob Mpinganjira
en.body: Mighty Wanderers have suspended head coach Bob Mpinganjira. The club announced this on Sunday night. It follows a 2-1 loss to Ekhaya FC in the Airtel Top 8 final at Bingu National Stadium in Lilongwe. The club says the suspension is part of plans for the CAF Champions League.
en.body_more:
The Nomads will face Tanzanian club Simba Sports Club this Sunday at the same stadium. This is the first round first leg of the CAF competition. Patrick Mabedi, a former Malawi national team coach, will manage the team for these two matches. Mabedi last worked as assistant coach for Young Africans, who are Simba SC's biggest rivals.

Chancy Gondwe is the club's board secretary. He said the timing of the suspension is part of their strategy. "We firmly believe this suspension is crucial for our CAF games," Gondwe said. He added that a new head coach will be appointed soon. The club wants to focus fully on the matches ahead.

Mpinganjira accepted the decision calmly. "The board made this choice and I accept it," he said. He will wait to learn what comes next. Under Mpinganjira, Wanderers won the league title last season after eight years without one. They also reached the FDH Bank Cup final and won the Castel Challenge Cup in 2024. The Nomads are now second on the league table with 29 points. They are tied with leaders Silver Strikers.

en.title: Attorney General appeals court decision on MEC move
en.body: Attorney General Frank Mbeta has asked the court to change a ruling about the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC). The MEC wants to move its office from Lilongwe to Blantyre. On August 20, 2026, Judge Kenyatta Nyirenda said no to this plan. Mbeta now wants a higher court to look at this decision again.
en.body_more:
Mbeta says Judge Nyirenda made mistakes in his ruling. He says the judge did not hear what the government wanted to say before he made his decision. Mbeta also says the opposition party and three lawmakers do not have the legal right to stop the move. The opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) used a law from June 5, 2026 to stop the MEC relocation. Judge Nyirenda agreed with the MCP and stopped the move.

The MCP lawyer George Kadzipatike told the court that his clients care about elections. He said the MEC's independence is important. He said changes to the MEC could hurt the MCP's rights. Judge Nyirenda agreed. He said inherent jurisdiction — which is a court's power to do what is fair and right — should not be used just to help one side. It should help justice.

Mbeta filed the appeal on behalf of the Chief Secretary to Government and the Minister of Lands, Housing and Urban Development. The case will now go to the Malawi Supreme Court of Appeal. The case is important because the MEC has had problems. The MEC stopped elections in Nsanje South and Mangochi East. These elections were set for September 29, 2026, but the MEC did not have election materials ready.

en.title: Weather office did not know about vice president's fatal flight
en.body: Lucy Mtilatila is the head of weather services in Malawi. She told Parliament on August 31, 2024 that her office did not know about a VVIP plane flight on June 10, 2024. The flight was going to Mzuzu. It crashed near Chikangawa. Nine people died, including former Vice President Saulos Chilima.
en.body_more:
Mtilatila gave evidence before a Parliamentary Ad-hoc Committee that is looking into what happened. She said that because her office was not told about the flight in advance, no weather forecaster was sent to Mzuzu Airport to help with the flight. This is not normal. For VVIP flights, a weather forecaster should go to both airports — the one where the plane leaves and the one where it lands.

"If we knew about this flight in advance, we would have sent a weather forecaster from Kamuzu Airport to Mzuzu to help on the ground," Mtilatila told the committee. She explained that Mzuzu Airport did not have a permanent weather forecaster because it did not have many commercial flights at that time. Only weather observers were there. Real meteorologists worked at Kamuzu Airport and Chileka Airport.

Mtilatila said her office needs to know about flights at least three hours before they leave. This gives time to prepare weather reports covering the place the plane leaves from, the route, and where it is going. The reports say things like wind and cloud conditions. The forecaster at Kamuzu Airport also did not send weather information to the flight crew because the crew never asked for it, she said.

On the day of the crash, June 10, 2024, Mtilatila said her office did not see any dangerous weather coming. No storm warnings were sent. She told the committee that weather reports focus mainly on clouds and wind, not fog. But fog can be added to a report if it is expected at the landing place and matters for flying. Committee chairperson Walter Nyamilandu Manda asked why weather information was not sent for the flight. Mtilatila repeated that her office did not know the flight was happening, so it could not prepare any special report.

en.title: Blantyre Water Board CEO wins court case and gets job back
en.body: Yeremia Chihana was the Chief Executive Officer of Blantyre Water Board. He was suspended on Friday. On August 30, 2026, the High Court of Malawi ruled in his favour. He got his job back on August 31, 2026.
en.body_more:
The court decision came as a surprise to many people. The reinstatement was confirmed in a letter from Lawrence Kadzitche, the Director of Human Resources and Administration at the water board. The letter said Chihana's suspension had been "completely lifted" and all restrictions were removed. Kadzitche asked staff to continue supporting Chihana as he returned to work.

Chihana had been suspended because of serious allegations. The board said he told people that the board had approved money for projects when it had not. He was also accused of getting a loan of K500 million from First Capital Bank without asking the board for permission first. These actions were called gross misconduct and abuse of power.

Chihana himself spoke to the media and said he was happy to return. People who supported him celebrated outside the court after the judge made the decision. The court order meant Chihana could go back to his work as Chief Executive Officer. The High Court case will continue while Chihana does his job at the water board.

en.title: 330 NGOs fail to send reports to regulator
en.body: The NGO Regulatory Authority (NGORA) says 330 non-governmental organisations have not sent in reports they must file by law. NGORA gave out a public notice on Wednesday. The authority says 1,060 NGOs were supposed to send reports. But 330 did not do this. NGORA says it will take legal action against them.
en.body_more:
Three well-known groups are on the list of NGOs that did not comply with the rules. These are HRDC, HRCC, and CAMA. HRDC is registered as NGO/L/24/140. HRCC is registered as NGO/L/13/036. CAMA is registered as NGO/L/13/068. These groups work in human rights, health, education, and other areas. NGORA did not say why these groups or the other 327 NGOs failed to send their reports.

NGORA says the NGO Reporting Regulations require all registered NGOs to send mandatory reports. A mandatory report is a report that the law says organisations must file. Some NGOs say they did not have enough money to send reports. Funding is money that groups need to work and pay staff.

NGORA says it has not removed the NGOs from the register yet. But the authority warns that it will take legally binding action. This means NGORA can force the groups to follow the rules or face punishment. The list includes NGOs that work on human rights, health, education, women's rights, the environment, and helping buyers. NGORA gave the public notice to make sure all NGOs know they must follow the reporting rules.

en.title: Court delays ruling on DPP Maele's appointment
en.body: The High Court in Lilongwe was set to rule today on whether Fostino Maele's appointment as Director of Public Prosecutions is legal. Judge Anneline Kanthambi was to decide if the case raises constitutional questions. The ruling did not happen. The court said the decision is not ready yet.
en.body_more:
Senior Counsel Kamudoni Nyasulu brought the case to court. He says President Mutharika appointed Maele in November 2025 when another DPP was still in office. That other DPP, Masauko Chamkakala, was appointed on 30 January 2023. His term runs until December 2027. Nyasulu says the Constitution does not allow two DPPs at the same time. He also challenges decisions Maele made to stop criminal cases since taking office.

Nyasulu wants the court to send this case to Chief Justice Rizine Mzikamanda for a constitutional review. If this happens, a panel of at least three judges will hear the case instead of one judge. Nyasulu argues the questions are about the Constitution itself. They affect how Malawi picks its chief prosecutor and whether the President acted within the law. The government still pays Chamkakala his monthly salary and benefits as DPP.

The case also challenges whether Maele can lawfully drop prosecutions while his appointment is questioned. If a court later rules his appointment was wrong, questions would follow about all his decisions — cases he stopped, cases he started, and all other orders from his office. This could affect many criminal prosecutions, including corruption cases. The delay means this legal cloud remains over Maele's office. No new court date has been set yet.

en.title: Former State House aide Collins Magalasi arrested in hotel deal case
en.body: Collins Magalasi has been arrested. He was a helper to former President Peter Mutharika at State House. He also led the Malawi Energy Regulatory Authority (MERA). Police say he is linked to large amounts of cash taken from a hotel deal. The deal cost K128.7 billion to buy Amaryllis Hotel.
en.body_more:
Magalasi's arrest follows a police investigation into how billions of kwacha were withdrawn in cash. Video footage from National Bank of Malawi shows the withdrawals. A man named Charles Gibson Nankhuni withdrew K1.5 billion on January 23, 2026. He withdrew another K1.5 billion days later. Nankhuki is said to be a false name. Magalasi is said to have led this operation. Video footage also shows unmarked vehicles from State House and armed police officers at the bank.

The bank gave the first K1.5 billion in cash after checking with Amaryllis Hotel owner Shiraz Yusuf. Before the money left the bank, the bank told the Financial Intelligence Authority (FIA) about the large withdrawal. FIA is a government body that watches for fraud. FIA did not stop the payment. A second withdrawal of K1.5 billion also happened. In total, about K5 billion was withdrawn in cash from the hotel deal money between January and March 2026.

Documents show about 25 separate withdrawals from the hotel money account. Money was taken by Nankhuni, Mark Kaliati, Rashird Alli and others. Single withdrawals ranged from K10 million to K500 million. Some money was put into bank accounts of businesses. The withdrawals stopped in early March when Parliament began to investigate the hotel deal. The Fiscal Police and the Anti-Corruption Bureau are now investigating together. Magalasi was also a former Presidential Secretary.

en.title: UTM leader helps Catholic choir launch new album
en.body: Dr Matthews Mtumbuka is the running mate for UTM Party in the 2025 election. On Sunday he went to Holy Trinity Parish in Zomba to help launch a new album by St Gregory Catholic Choir. He told the people there that music is a gift from God.
en.body_more:
Mtumbuka spoke as guest of honour at the album launch for St Gregory Catholic Choir Mzimu Woyera. He told worshippers that every person in church has a talent they can use to serve God. He said music is one of these talents. "Every person in the church has a talent that can be used to serve God well. One of these talents is music, and we should use it to glorify God," Mtumbuka told them.

Mtumbuka is the MP for Rumphi Central. He thanked the choir for asking him to come. "I would like to thank St. Gregory Choir for inviting me to be the guest of honour. The people of Rumphi Central are very honoured by this invitation," he said. Zomba City North MP Bester Awali brought Mtumbuka to the event. Awali's helper Joe Pamamera said thank you to Mtumbuka for coming. Even though they are in different political parties, Mtumbuka put that aside for the church. Pamamera said: "We would like to thank Matthews Mtumbuka for gracing this occasion and putting party colours aside to attend this function, especially because the invitation came through Honourable Bester Awali."

Mtumbuka also bought the new album CD. He paid K1.5 million for it. This showed his support for the choir's work. The event brought together people from different political sides to help the church and the community.

en.title: Miss Malawi organisation deletes photo of reigning queen
en.body: The Miss Malawi organisation removed a photo of reigning queen Thandie Chisi from Facebook. The photo showed Chisi at the Airtel Top 8 Cup final. People on social media said the deletion was wrong. They said the organisation was trying to sideline its own queen.
en.body_more:
The photo was posted and then deleted quickly from the Miss Malawi Facebook page. Social media user Chigomezgo Nyasulu was angry about this. Nyasulu wrote: "Very silly of the Miss Malawi page to post a picture of Thandie Chisi and then later delete it! It doesn't look good at all." Many people agreed with Nyasulu.

Chisi presented the Airtel Cup trophy at Bingu National Stadium on Sunday. Ekhaya FC won the cup after beating Mighty Wanderers 2-1. But Chisi did not wear her Miss Malawi crown. This made people ask more questions about what is happening in the Miss Malawi organisation.

Malawi is sending Ireen Navicha to Miss World, not Thandie Chisi. Navicha is the first runner-up. Godfrey Kambewa is the Chief Operations Officer of Miss Malawi Organisation. Kambewa told people that the organisation owns three identical crowns. He said Chisi kept her crown. Navicha got another crown for Miss World. But Chisi did not wear her crown at the Airtel Cup final. The organisation did not say why. Chisi also did not say why. Neither Chisi nor the Miss Malawi organisation gave a public answer about the deleted photo or the missing crown.

en.title: Ekhaya FC wins Airtel Top 8 trophy on debut
en.body: Ekhaya FC won the Airtel Top 8 football trophy for the first time. They beat Mighty Wanderers 2-1 in the final at Bingu National Stadium in Lilongwe on Sunday. Blessings Malinda and Allen Chihana scored for Ekhaya. Mphatso Kamanga scored one goal for Wanderers. This was Ekhaya's first year in the top league.
en.body_more:
Ekhaya started well and scored first. In the 38th minute, Blessings Malinda converted a penalty kick to make it 1-0 at half-time. Wanderers came back strong after the break. Mphatso Kamanga scored four minutes into the second half to make the score 1-1. But Ekhaya took the lead again in the 60th minute when Allen Chihana scored from a Malinda assist. Wanderers tried hard to score again but Ekhaya held on to win.

Ekhaya's journey to the final was impressive. They knocked out defending champions FCB Nyasa Big Bullets in the quarter-finals on penalty kicks. In the semi-finals they beat Karonga United 2-1. Wanderers also had a tough route to the final. They defeated Creck Sporting Club 3-1 in the quarter-finals. In the semi-finals they beat Blue Eagles 5-4 on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

The match had a special family story. Mighty Wanderers chairman Dr Thomson Mpinganjira is the father of William Mpinganjira, who is involved with Ekhaya FC. After the game, Ekhaya coach Enos Chatama said his team was not scared to face big clubs. He told his players to stay focused and not become lazy after winning. Wanderers coach Bob Mpinganjira said his team lacked hunger and did not take their chances.

Ekhaya received K40 million in prize money for winning. Allen Chihana was the top scorer of the tournament with four goals. Minister of Youth, Sports and Culture Alfred Gangata watched the match.

en.title: Bullets fined for fan misconduct during match
en.body: FCB Nyasa Big Bullets has been fined K3.5 million by the Super League of Malawi (Sulom). The fine follows an incident on 19 July 2026 during their FDH Bank Premiership match against Ekhaya Football Club. Some fans threw bottles onto the pitch in protest against the referee's decision. The match was stopped for a short time and ended with no goals scored.
en.body_more:
Sulom's Disciplinary Committee found Bullets guilty of misconduct. The trouble started when referee Mayamiko Kanjere disallowed a goal scored by Bullets forward Ephraim Kondowe. The referee said Kondowe was in an offside position. This decision made some Bullets fans very angry. They threw bottles and behaved badly. Officials stopped the match at Chiwembe Stadium (also called Mpira Stadium) in Blantyre to deal with the problem.

Sulom warned Bullets that the club will lose points if this happens again. The league body said clubs must teach their fans to obey the law and keep order during matches. Albert Chigoga, the Bullets Chief Executive Officer, said the behaviour was wrong. He told fans that football does not allow misconduct. Chigoga said Bullets will now report such incidents to the police so bad fans can be arrested.

Bullets has had many discipline problems before. Last season, the club was fined a total of K15 million. They were fined K5.7 million for trouble at a match against Blue Eagles at Kamuzu Stadium in Blantyre. The Football Association of Malawi also fined Bullets K5 million for misconduct during an FDH Bank Cup match against Mighty Wanderers at Kamuzu Stadium. Bullets received K4 million in fines for trouble during a Castel Challenge Cup match against Mzuzu City Hammers. The club was also fined K1 million for misconduct during a match against Karonga United.

en.title: Silver Ladies finish 4th in CAF Women's Champions League
en.body: Malawi's Silver Strikers Ladies lost 4-0 to Gaborone United Ladies in Botswana. The match was for third place in the CAF Women's Champions League COSAFA Qualifier. Silver Ladies finished fourth in their first time at the tournament. Coach Patricio Kulemeka said the team has learnt many things.
en.body_more:
Silver Strikers Ladies played five matches at the tournament. They won two matches and lost three. In their wins, they beat Costa do Sol from Mozambique 2-1 and Nsingizini Hotspurs from Eswatini 5-1. They lost to Mamelodi Sundowns from South Africa 3-0 and ZESCO Ndola Girls from Zambia 2-1 before the final match.

In the third-place playoff on Saturday, Gaborone United scored four goals. Jessica Maponga scored first. Other players added more goals. One goal was checked by a video camera and was found to be correct. Silver Ladies tried hard but could not stop Gaborone.

Coach Kulemeka said the losses showed what the team must fix. He said some mistakes came again and again in different games. He told reporters: "We have learnt a lot from this competition, particularly from the games we lost." Kulemeka said the team will go home and work on these weak areas. The coach said players will use what they learnt to play better in home matches too.

Kulemeka said fourth place is good for the team's first time. He said the team will come back next year much stronger. Captain Ruth Nyirongo, goalkeeper Ireen Sibande and forward Carolyn Mathyola played for Silver in the tournament. Carolyn Mathyola scored four goals. Kulemeka said the team has now made a strong base for the future.

en.title: Wanderers play Ekhaya in big football final today
en.body: Mighty Wanderers and Ekhaya FC will play a big football match today. The match is the Airtel Top 8 final. It will be at Bingu National Stadium in Lilongwe. Wanderers come from Blantyre. They are an old, strong team. Ekhaya is new. This is their first big final. Both teams want to win.
en.body_more:
Wanderers had to win two hard matches to reach the final. They beat Creck Sporting Club first. Then they played Blue Eagles in the semi-final. The match went to a penalty shootout. Penalty is when a player kicks the ball from a special spot to try to score. Lameck Mithi scored his penalty for Wanderers. Blue Eagles scored too. The score was 5-4 to Wanderers from the penalty spot. Mithi has scored two goals in this competition. He will try to score more today.

Ekhaya's path to the final was even more shocking. They beat FCB Nyasa Bullets in the quarter-final. Nyasa Bullets were the defending champions, meaning they won last year. Ekhaya then beat Karonga United 2-1 in the semi-final. Allen Chihana is Ekhaya's best player. He has scored three goals in the tournament. Chimwemwe Chunga scored the goal that sent Ekhaya to the final.

Wanderers will use players like Isaac Kaliati and Sama Thierry Tanjong. Kaliati is an old, strong player. Tanjong is from Cameroon. Blessings Mwalilino, Gaddie Chirwa, Clement Nyondo and Promise Kamwendo will also play. Wanderers' coach is Bob Mpinganjira. Ekhaya's coach is Enos Chatama. Chatama said his team did not come to the final just to play. They want to win. The final will be a big test for both teams.

en.title: Cotton Crop Falls Short by More Than Half
en.body: Malawi's cotton season closed this week with very low output. The country made 4,500 metric tonnes of cotton. This was far below the goal of 22,800 metric tonnes. Cotton output dropped by more than half from last year's 10,000 metric tonnes. The Cotton Council of Malawi and Cotton Farmers Association both confirmed the market closure on August 23, 2026.
en.body_more:
Only 7,000 farmers grew cotton this year, down from 26,000 last year. Yohane Jim, field manager at Malawi Cotton Company, said farmers left the sector because of problems from the previous year. The Cotton Management Information System is a digital platform that tracks cotton sales and payments. This system had big problems. Some farmers did not get their money on time. Other farmers did not get paid at all. Jim said this caused many farmers to stop growing cotton.

Two large cotton buying companies did not work this season. Malawi Cotton Company and Masapa Cotton Ginners both stayed away. They said the low amount of cotton made it not worth their time. Labson Zidana is president of the Cotton Farmers Association. He said prices were fair at K1,500 per kilogramme, which is the government price. But he said the total amount of cotton was very low, maybe only 5,000 metric tonnes.

Duncan Warren is a cotton farmer and former chair of the Cotton Council. He said the government does not help the cotton sector grow. Since 2010, when the government paid for inputs and Malawi made 100,000 metric tonnes, output has stayed at about 10,000 metric tonnes. Warren said other countries use money to help farmers buy new seeds that grow better. Malawi does not do this. He said cotton is very important for making things in Malawi and for bringing in money from other countries. Without government help, the cotton sector will stay weak.

en.title: Soldier Guilty of Sexual Abuse of 15-Year-Old Girl
en.body: A soldier has been found guilty of having sex with a 15-year-old girl four times. Diof Simaone, age 36, works at Kamuzu Barracks in Lilongwe. The court heard the abuse happened between April and August 2025. The girl became pregnant. Sentencing will happen on Tuesday.
en.body_more:
The Senior Resident Magistrate Court in Lilongwe found Simaone guilty on Friday, August 28, 2026. The court is called a magistrate court — it is where a judge hears cases and decides if someone did wrong. Prosecutor Thandizo Chingaru told the court that Simaone had sex with the child four times. Three times happened at a guest house in Area 44. One time happened at Simaone's own house. The girl gave birth to a baby boy in January 2026.

The girl's mother works as a cleaner at Kamuzu Barracks. She reported what happened to Area 23 Police Unit, and police arrested Simaone. Prosecutor Chingaru asked the court to give the harshest punishment. He said Simaone was a military officer and should have protected the girl, not hurt her. A military officer is a soldier with a duty to keep people safe.

Simaone asked the court for forgiveness. He told the magistrate he wanted to support the girl and the baby. He also asked the victim, her mother, the court, and the whole nation to forgive him. He said what he did was wrong. Simaone comes from Nakoka Village in Traditional Authority Mwambo in Zomba District.

Magistrate Bracious Kondowe found Simaone guilty. Kondowe has not yet decided on the punishment. Simaone will learn his sentence on Tuesday next week.

en.title: Miss Malawi outfit gets mocked on social media
en.body: Ireen Navicha, Malawi's Miss World, wore a green and gold outfit called "Rooted in Purpose" for the World Designer Award. Many people on social media did not like it. They said the design had no real meaning. Some said it looked like green pyjamas. Navicha is still in Vietnam waiting for the Miss World final on 5 September 2026.
en.body_more:
The outfit was made by Testimony Designer. The designer said green means Malawi's land, growth and new life. Gold means a woman's strength and power. But fans did not believe this meaning.

One person wrote: "I only see green, not gold." Another person asked: "Is green pyjamas what shows Malawi's rich land?" A third person said: "Nothing about this dress shows real symbols. We just make up meanings." Many people said the dress should have used Malawi's flag colours: black, red and green.

This loss is hard for Navicha. She did not win the World Fashion Designer Award for Africa. Shreeya Bokhoree from Mauritius won with a dress about her country's culture. The fashion show was at Vietnam Beauty Fashion Fest XVII. Many African countries showed dresses that tell stories about their people and land.

Navicha still has more chances to win points. She will do Top Model Part 2 on 28 August. Then Dances of the World will come on 2 September. The final Miss World crowning will happen on 5 September 2026. Many Malawians have also said bad words to Navicha on social media in past weeks.

en.title: Police remove all traffic aides after bribe video
en.body: Malawi Police Service told all traffic aides to stop work on 27 August 2026. They must go back to normal duties at their stations. This follows a video that went viral on social media. The video showed a traffic police officer asking for K20,000 from a minibus driver in Blantyre. K20,000 is money. A bribe is money you give someone to do something wrong.
en.body_more:
The police order came from headquarters and affects police stations across all of Malawi. All regional police leaders and station heads must follow the order. If they do not follow it, they will face punishment. The message came from Lael Chitembo, the deputy director of human resource management at the police.

Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwaula and her deputy Alfred Chimthere did not answer calls or messages about the order. Police sources say traffic aides are officers sent from police headquarters to help in traffic work and criminal investigations. Attachés are officers sent by station or regional leaders. These officers have no special training.

Coxley Kamange, secretary general of the Minibus Owners Association of Malawi, said well done to the police. He said the police are stopping corruption. He called on the Inspector General to arrest and take to court the traffic officer in the video. He said this officer brought shame to the police service.

Governance commentator Undule Mwakasungula said the order was right. He said the police chief has power over how police work and where police go. He said the order helps the police keep rules and send officers to the right places. But he said people must watch to see if removing traffic aides makes roads less safe.

en.title: President Mutharika promises better funding for rights body
en.body: President Arthur Peter Mutharika met with outgoing commissioners of the Malawi Human Rights Commission (MHRC) at Kamuzu Palace in Lilongwe. He promised that his government will give the Commission more money. The MHRC is a body that protects human rights in Malawi.
en.body_more:
Mutharika said the Commission has done excellent work. He praised the team for protecting the rights of women, children, and old people. He also praised their work on access to information. He told them: "Let me congratulate the Commission. They have done an excellent job in the face of challenges, especially resource challenges. I promise that the Commission will be well resourced so that they are able to carry out their work properly."

Outgoing Commissioner Chikondi Chijozi Jere said the meeting gave the Commission a chance to tell the President about what they have done, what problems they face, and what they want to do in the future. The outgoing team was chosen in 2023. They handled several important human rights cases during their time. Their three-year job ended on August 26, 2026.

For many years, the MHRC has had money problems. These money problems have made the work slow. The Commission has had to work with fewer staff. Human rights groups have long asked the government to give the MHRC more money. They want the Commission to be free to check complaints and teach people about rights without waiting for money.

Mutharika's promise comes at a time when people ask if the government will truly help the MHRC. The Commission must check what the government does — from police work to prison conditions. Without enough money, the Commission cannot do this work well. The new commissioners will now take over the work.

en.title: Water Board Boss Suspended Over Money and Appointments
en.body: Yeremia Chihana, chief of the Blantyre Water Board, is suspended again. The board says he did wrong things. He got money without asking. He appointed a person without permission. This is his second suspension in five months.
en.body_more:
On Thursday, 28 August 2026, the board suspended Chihana. Board chair Stanely Chirwa wrote the letter. Chihana faces three main charges. First, he wrote to the Secretary to the Treasury Cliff Chiunda. Chihana said the board approved a modernisation plan. Modernisation means making something new and better. But the board says this meeting never happened. Chihana falsely claimed the board gave approval at a March 15 2026 meeting.

Second, Chihana appointed Lon Zizwe as acting director of finance. He did this alone on August 17 2026. The board says only the board can make these appointments. The board letter says this appointment is invalid. Charles Msusa is the real acting director, not Zizwe.

Third, Chihana obtained a K500 million overdraft facility from First Capital Bank. An overdraft is borrowed money. He did this on July 23 2026 without board approval. The board did not know about this money.

Chihana tells a different story. He says he is being punished because he refused to travel to Lilongwe for a meeting about a $13 million World Bank project. He claims the board did not follow the right process for this project. He says some board members want to stop reforms. Chihana says he will challenge the suspension in court. He is now barred from entering any board office and cannot contact staff or suppliers.

en.title: Village builds fence around Lucius Banda memorial house
en.body: A chief in Sosola village, Balaka district, has put a wooden fence around a memorial house built for late musician Lucius Banda. The chief said visitors were drinking beer, taking photos, and stepping on nearby graves. The family was not asked first about the fence.
en.body_more:
The memorial house stands on the edge of Sosola village graveyard. The chief explained his reasons for building the fence. "People come to this house without order," he said. "They take pictures while drinking alcohol. Some step on graves behind the house. This is not good for our culture. That is why I built the fence."

The chief said he wants to protect the graveyard and keep it clean. He also said the fence will help stop people being disrespectful to the dead. The chief added that Lucius Banda's family and the committee who built the memorial house did not ask him before they started. However, he said he was not angry about this. He attended the official ceremony when the memorial house opened.

Lucius Banda's family has not yet spoken about the fence. Balaka Police Publicist Gladson M'bumpha said police have not received any complaint about the matter. Reporters and village chiefs visited the site to see what was happening. The growing concern in Sosola is about how visitors treat the memorial house and the graveyard since Lucius Banda died.

en.title: Oil company boss questioned over K700 million payment
en.body: The Anti-Corruption Bureau questioned Emmanuel Matapa, chief of the National Oil Company. The ACB asked him about a K700 million payment made by the oil firm. The payment was based on false information sent by email. Matapa went to ACB offices on Thursday to explain what happened.
en.body_more:
The ACB spokesperson Jacqueline Ngongonda said the bureau started its own investigation. She said the bureau found a suspected crime. The crime is abuse of office. This means a worker used their job wrongly. The bureau wants to know who made the payment decision.

Matapa said he should not leave his job. He said he started work on May 1, 2026. This was after the payment already happened. So he did not make the payment, he said. Two other Nocma workers were arrested on Wednesday. They are deputy chief Miklas Reuben and senior manager Thokozani Jacob Sesani. Police said they may face charges. The charges are negligence by a public officer and misuse of public office. This means they did not take care of public money properly.

The oil company said no money was lost. Spokesman Raymond Likambale said the bank that got the money confirmed receipt. The payment was for work by Mozhandling. They helped process the MT Flora ship. This ship carried 15.1 million litres of fuel. The fuel came through the Port of Nacala in Mozambique. The government changed its fuel buying plan in November 2024. The new plan is government-to-government buying. The old plan used open tenders. Nocma now leads the fuel imports under the new plan.

The investigation is still going on. No criminal charges have been made yet against anyone.

en.title: Bullets coaches wait for work permits
en.body: FCB Nyasa Big Bullets signed two new coaches last week. Lemekani Mwanza is a data analyst. Donewell Yobe is an assistant coach. They cannot start work yet. The government must give them work permits first. The club says this will happen soon.
en.body_more:
Mwanza and Yobe arrived in Malawi ready to join head coach Wedson Nyirenda's team. But they must wait for government clearance before they can begin their jobs. Bullets Chief Executive Officer Albert Chigoga said the club is still waiting for papers from the government.

Chigoga explained that every country has rules for people who want to work there. A work permit is official permission that allows a person from another country to have a job. He said Bullets believes the two coaches will start work next week. The delay is normal. It is not a problem with the coaches themselves.

Bullets are also bringing in new players. Playmaker Sheku Sheriff from Liberia has joined the team. The club wants to sign two or three more players before the transfer window closes. The transfer window officially opened on Tuesday. Chigoga said the coach Wedson Nyirenda and his team asked for these new signings. The club had a slow start to the season and wants to play better in the second half.

Bullets now sit fourth on the league table with 27 points from 14 matches. Silver Strikers and Mighty Wanderers are joint leaders with 29 points. Blue Eagles are third with 28 points. The race for the title is very close.

en.title: Silver Strikers Ladies lose and leave tournament
en.body: Silver Strikers Ladies lost 2-1 to Zesco Ndola Girls of Zambia on Thursday. The game was at Gaborone United Stadium in Botswana. This loss ended Silver Strikers' hope to reach the final of the tournament. The tournament is the 2026 CAF Women's Champions League Cosafa qualifier.
en.body_more:
Penelope Mulubwa and Charity Mubanga scored the goals for Zesco Ndola Girls. Carol Mathyola scored one goal for Silver Strikers. The match was shown live on YouTube so many people could watch it.

Silver Strikers coach Patricio Kulemeka told the news he was sad about the loss. But he said the team learned from playing in this big tournament. He said this will help his players play better in Malawi's league. Kulemeka said the players will gain more skills from this experience.

Silver Strikers will now play a third-place match this Saturday. They will play against Gaborone United. This match is not for the final. It is to find who comes third in the tournament. The match will give Silver Strikers more time to play against other good teams.

In another match, Mamelodi Sundowns Ladies beat Gaborone United 5-0. Sundowns is from South Africa. This big win took Sundowns to the final. Zesco Ndola Girls will play Sundowns in the final game. The winner of that final will be the best team in the Cosafa region and will go to the next part of the CAF Women's Champions League.

en.title: Weather officer says plane could have landed safely
en.body: A weather officer told Parliament on Thursday that the military plane crash on June 10, 2024 could have landed at Mzuzu Airport. Olive Chavunguma worked at the weather station that day. Vice-President Saulos Chilima and eight others died in the crash at Chikangawa Forest.
en.body_more:
Chavunguma said the weather station recorded visibility of eight kilometres at Mzuzu Airport that morning. She told the Parliamentary Ad-hoc Committee investigating the crash that visibility improved in the afternoon. With 35 years of work in aviation, Chavunguma said the plane could have landed. Weather conditions were overcast with drizzles and fog, but the plane had landed before in similar conditions.

Chavunguma warned the committee that weather at Mzuzu Airport differs from weather at Chikangawa, where the plane crashed at Nthungwa Hill. Different locations have different terrain, elevation and atmospheric conditions. Visibility of eight kilometres means a pilot can see well enough to land, she said. But Chavunguma could not confirm that bad weather caused the crash or that pilots had very low visibility in Chikangawa.

The German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation (BFU) said in their report that visibility was less than eight kilometres. Chavunguma said the difference was not significant. She said the BFU report claimed visibility was about three kilometres, but her station recorded eight kilometres. Chavunguma told the committee the BFU did not visit the weather station or ask for weather information. This breaks international rules for air accident investigation. The BFU concluded that bad weather and terrain collision caused the crash. In January this year, President Peter Mutharika ordered a fresh inquiry after Minister of Justice Charles Mhango found gaps in earlier reports.

en.title: Kasungu chiefs call for patrols to stop power theft
en.body: Leaders in Kasungu are telling people to form security patrols. They want to stop people from damaging electricity equipment. Four power transformers have been broken in the district in recent weeks. This has left many communities without power. ESCOM, the electricity company, is visiting chiefs and business people in three districts to teach them about the problem.
en.body_more:
Senior Chief Kaomba spoke at his headquarters during a meeting with ESCOM. He told all the chiefs under him to protect the electricity infrastructure. "Electricity is development. We must safeguard it. Let's form patrols in our areas," he said. Senior Chief Mwase also supported this plan. He said that communities must help stop the vandalism problem.

Police officers from Kasungu Police Station spoke at the meetings. They told residents to watch carefully and work with the police. They want people to help stop theft and damage of public property. ESCOM Chief Public Relations and Communications Officer Pilirani Phiri explained the campaign. She said people must take ownership of the electricity equipment in their areas. "This is the only way we can defeat vandalism," she said. Phiri asked people to think of transformers differently. She said transformers help businesses, health centres and schools.

ESCOM has also asked civil society groups to help teach people about the problem. The electricity company loses money each year. ESCOM says it loses about K3 billion every year from deliberate vandalism. This money could be used to build more power lines and improve the electricity grid. Without this money, ESCOM cannot expand. Communities suffer from long periods without power. Businesses stop working and schools cannot teach at night without electricity.

en.title: US Embassy opens American Chamber of Commerce in Malawi
en.body: The United States Embassy opened the American Chamber of Commerce in Malawi on Tuesday in Blantyre. US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires Melania Arreaga said the chamber will help American businesses in Malawi. It will also create new chances for companies from both countries to work together.
en.body_more:
The chamber gives American companies a place to meet and share ideas. It will help businesses understand Malawi's rules and find partners to work with. The chamber wants to help in areas where Malawi wants to grow. These areas are farming, making goods, clean energy and technology.

Melania Arreaga said the chamber will bring together business owners, government leaders and investors. They will talk about how to do business better and what changes Malawi needs. American companies already work in Malawi in farming, mining and digital services. The chamber will help more American firms come to Malawi.

For Malawi's own business owners, the chamber is a chance to learn new ways of working. They can meet mentors from America and learn how to sell goods to other countries. Small and medium sized businesses can improve their work and meet world standards. The chamber will work with Malawi's Ministry of Trade and Industry to help grow the economy.

Both foreign and local businesses face problems in Malawi. These include not enough power, bad roads and a need for skilled workers. The chamber will push for new laws and partnerships between government and business to fix these problems. Business leaders say the chamber could help solve these issues and bring more investment to Malawi.

en.title: Silver Ladies lose to Ndola in CAF semi-final
en.body: Silver Strikers Ladies lost 2-1 to Zesco Ndola Girls on Thursday in Botswana. The semi-final match was for the CAF Women's Champions League Cosafa Qualifiers. Carolyn Mathyola scored for Silver Ladies, but it was not enough.
en.body_more:
The match took place at Gaborone United Stadium in Gaborone, Botswana. Silver Ladies made history as the first Malawian team to reach the semi-final of this competition. Coach Patricio Kulemeka led the team in this tournament because the main coach Andrew Chikhosi does not have the CAF A license. This is a special paper that shows a coach can train at the highest level in Africa.

Zesco Ndola Girls scored twice in the first 18 minutes. Penelope Mulubwa scored in the 11th minute. Charity Mubanga scored in the 18th minute. Silver Ladies played poorly at the back in the opening part of the match. The Zambian players Penelope Mulubwa and Ilness Phiri found open space and attacked easily.

In the second half, Silver Ladies played better. Carolyn Mathyola scored in the 62nd minute after Ireen Khumalo's shot. Mathyola moved fastest to catch the ball after Zesco failed to clear it. Silver Ladies tried hard to score again, but Zesco Ndola Girls kept their lead until the end.

Silver Ladies' squad has five players from the Malawi National Women's Football Team that played at the Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. These players are Ireen Khumalo, Chikondi Gondwe, Tionge Phiri, Madyina Ngulube and Debroah Henry. Silver Ladies finished second in Group B with two wins and one loss. Zesco Ndola Girls topped Group A with three straight wins. Now Silver Ladies will play for third place in the tournament.

en.title: Two nurses seek to lead Malawi's nurses and midwives union
en.body: Two nurses are standing for president of the National Organisation of Nurses and Midwives (NONM). George Nkhoma and Frank Louis Kamwendo both want to lead the union. NONM will hold elections on 27 November 2026. Both candidates say they will improve pay, working conditions, and welfare for nurses and midwives across Malawi.
en.body_more:
George Nkhoma says nurses and midwives have carried heavy weight in Malawi's health system while their voices stayed weak. He promises to give more power to district and zonal chapters. This means decisions will be made closer to hospitals and clinics, not just in offices. He plans to start a Nurses and Midwives Welfare Campaign every May in all districts.

Nkhoma's campaign agenda includes better pay that matches the cost of living, uniforms for all staff, higher allowances for locum and risk work, and hot meals for nurses on duty. He will set up a Legal Defence Fund to help nurses facing unfair treatment at work. He also wants to create a NONM clinic and a savings group to help members save money.

Frank Louis Kamwendo, age 35, focuses on similar issues but with different plans. He wants shift patterns changed to give a minimum of three shifts in 24 hours. He promises legal help for members facing problems. He will work to restore hot meals within six months and uniforms within 12 months. Kamwendo says he will end the Contributory Pension Scheme and bring back the old pension system. He also plans to set up a savings and credit cooperative within two years.

Both candidates address the welfare of nurses working for the Christian Health Association of Malawi (CHAM). Kamwendo points to his past work pushing for mass recruitment of nurses and his involvement in court cases over union fees and membership rules. He says his record shows he can lead the union well. Both men say they will help nurses work abroad where jobs are not available at home.

en.title: ACB calls NOCMA boss to answer fraud questions
en.body: The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has called Emmanuel Matapa, boss of the National Oil Company of Malawi, to explain a K700 million payment to scammers. The ACB is a government office that checks for corruption—money or power used in wrong ways. Matapa must come to the ACB office in Lilongwe today.
en.body_more:
ACB acting director Gabriel Chembezi signed the call. ACB spokesperson Jacqueline Ngongonda said the bureau made its own complaint to start the check. The complaint looks at whether people broke the law when they made the payment. "We want to know what happened with this money," Ngongonda said. "We will check if anyone abused their office."

The call comes one day after police arrested two other NOCMA workers. The Deputy CEO Miklas Reuben and Senior Operations Manager Thokozani Jacob Sesani were arrested about the same K700 million payment. NOCMA said fake people pretended to be a Mozambican company called Mozhandling Limited. These fake people sent false emails. NOCMA workers read the emails and sent the money to a wrong bank account.

Matapa says he will not leave his job because of this problem. He says the payment happened on 29 April 2026. He only started work on 1 May 2026—two days after the payment. He believes this means he did not make the wrong choice. But the ACB now wants to hear from him directly about what took place.

en.title: Man held over sex abuse of five-year-old daughter
en.body: Police in Mangochi have arrested a 55-year-old man from Namwera. He is accused of sexually abusing his own five-year-old daughter. The alleged abuse happened on 25 August 2026. The child's mother was away at a ceremony at the time. She found the child unwell when she returned home late that night.
en.body_more:
The mother took the child to Namwera Health Centre for a medical check. Doctors found that the child had been sexually abused. The findings matched the mother's concerns. Police then arrested the man. When police asked him questions, he did not give a good answer about what happened.

Mangochi Police Publicist Amina Tepani Daudi said the arrest was made after the mother reported the matter to Namwera Police Post. The man comes from the area of Traditional Authority Jalasi in Mangochi district. He is the child's biological father. At the time of the alleged abuse, the mother had gone to an initiation ceremony in Namwera village, leaving the suspect with the children.

The man has been charged with defiling a child. This goes against Section 138 of the Penal Code. A penal code is a set of laws about crimes and punishments. The medical report from Namwera Health Centre backs up the police case. The man is now expected to appear in court to answer the charge of having sexual intercourse with a female child. The case will be heard by a judge in court.

en.title: Unima graduates told to solve problems, not cause them
en.body: University of Malawi held its second graduation ceremony yesterday at the Great Hall in Zomba. Two thousand one hundred ninety-one students graduated. Vice-Chancellor Professor Samson Sajidu told them to be problem-solvers and good citizens. He said education must be paired with good character and care for others.
en.body_more:
Sajidu spoke to five doctorate graduates, seventy-three master's graduates, and one thousand nine hundred forty-six bachelor's graduates. He said they faced many challenges during their studies — money troubles, health problems, and difficult emotions. But they did not give up. Now they must show the same strength in their jobs.

"Education with character wins trust in the society," Sajidu said. He told graduates to be kind to the communities where they will live. "Education has given you knowledge and skills. But your care for others will define your true legacy," he said. Sajidu also warned them about corruption. Corruption is when people take money or favours they should not take. He said corruption stops Malawi from moving forward and hurts poor people most.

Unima Council Chairperson Benedicto Malunga agreed. He said laziness and corruption block national development. "The value of education is measured through what you deliver to the society," Malunga said. He told graduates to work hard and find new ideas in their jobs. Malunga also noted that Unima has made discipline stronger in the university. Of the two thousand one hundred ninety-one graduates, nine hundred twenty-six were female. Sajidu urged graduates who borrowed money for studies to pay it back to the Higher Education Students Loans and Grants Board. This way, other students could get loans too.

ny.title: Omaliza maphunziro a Unima auzidwa kuthetsa mavuto, osati kuwayambitsa
ny.body: Yunivesite ya Malawi inachita mwambo wake wachiwiri womaliza maphunziro dzulo ku Great Hall ku Zomba. Ophunzira 2,191 anamaliza maphunziro awo. Wachiwiri kwa Chancellor Pulofesa Samson Sajidu anawauza kuti akhale othetsa mavuto komanso nzika zabwino. Iye anati maphunziro ayenera kugwirizanitsidwa ndi khalidwe labwino komanso kusamalira ena.
ny.body_more:
Sajidu adalankhula ndi ophunzira asanu omaliza maphunziro a udokotala, omaliza maphunziro a masters 73, ndi omaliza maphunziro a bachelor 1,946. Anati adakumana ndi mavuto ambiri panthawi ya maphunziro awo - mavuto azachuma, mavuto azaumoyo, ndi malingaliro ovuta. Koma sanataye mtima. Tsopano ayenera kuwonetsa mphamvu zomwezo pantchito zawo.

"Maphunziro okhala ndi khalidwe labwino amapatsa chidaliro m'gulu," adatero Sajidu. Anauza omaliza maphunziro kuti akhale okoma mtima kumadera omwe akukhala. "Maphunziro akupatsani chidziwitso ndi luso. Koma chisamaliro chanu kwa ena chidzatsimikizira cholowa chanu chenicheni," adatero. Sajidu adawachenjezanso za ziphuphu. Ziphuphu ndi pamene anthu amatenga ndalama kapena zinthu zomwe sayenera kulandira. Anati ziphuphu zimaletsa Malawi kupita patsogolo ndipo zimavulaza kwambiri anthu osauka.

Wapampando wa Bungwe la Unima Benedicto Malunga adavomereza. Anati ulesi ndi ziphuphu zimalepheretsa chitukuko cha dziko. "Kufunika kwa maphunziro kumayesedwa kudzera mu zomwe mumapereka kwa anthu," adatero Malunga. Anauza omaliza maphunziro kuti agwire ntchito mwakhama ndikupeza malingaliro atsopano pantchito zawo. Malunga adanenanso kuti Unima yalimbitsa ulemu ku yunivesite. Mwa omaliza maphunziro 2,000,1991, 926 anali akazi. Sajidu analimbikitsa omaliza maphunziro omwe anabwereka ndalama zophunzirira kuti azibwezere ku Higher Education Students Loans and Grants Board. Mwanjira imeneyi, ophunzira ena nawonso angapeze ngongole.

en.title: Ekhaya FC president spends K2 billion on club
en.body: William Mpinganjira, the president of Ekhaya FC, says he has spent K2 billion on the club in three years. He told reporters this in Blantyre on Monday. The money paid for players, coaches, transport, medical care, and health insurance. Ekhaya will play Mighty Wanderers in a cup final on Sunday.
en.body_more:
Mpinganjira said the K2 billion was his long-term plan to make Ekhaya a fully professional club. The money covered many things: coaches, transport, office equipment, media tools, playing kits, medical equipment, and replica jerseys. He said paying players on time and paying all staff on time was important for a good club.

"We have created one of the best football environments for a player in Malawi," Mpinganjira said. He wanted to make sure all players were happy. The investment was not just about buying good players. It was about building a club that would grow and last a long time.

Ekhaya will face Mighty Wanderers at Bingu National Stadium in Lilongwe this coming Sunday in the Airtel Top 8 final. This is a cup match. Mighty Wanderers is owned by Thom Mpinganjira, William's father. Right now, Ekhaya is in tenth place in the FDH Bank Premiership league with 17 points from 14 matches.

James Majawa, a sports expert, said Ekhaya's spending plan was good for all Malawian football. He said the club showed other clubs how to mix good sport results with good business planning. Majawa said clubs should see football as a long-term investment, not quick money that comes and goes.

en.title: Company gives two fire trucks to Lilongwe and Mangochi
en.body: Creck Hardware and General Supplies gave two fire engines to Lilongwe City Council and Mangochi Municipality on Thursday, 27 August. The engines cost K300 million together. Company director Apostle Clifford Kawinga said the gift helps keep people safe. Minister of Local Government Ben Phiri received the donation at Capital Hill.
en.body_more:
Kawinga said Creck Hardware is a responsible company. He wanted to help Malawi's business and safety. The Ministry of Local Government asked private companies to help the country. Kawinga said the donation shows Creck Hardware cares about the government's plans and the safety of all people in Malawi.

Phiri was very happy with the gift. He said it will help firefighting and emergency work. One fire engine goes to Mangochi Municipal Council. The other goes to Lilongwe City Council. Cassim Iman Chisuse is the Mayor of Mangochi Municipality. He said thank you to Creck Hardware for the help. He said Mangochi will take good care of the truck.

Phiri also told people that many councils have no fire engines. Only five district councils have fire trucks now. More than 25 councils across Malawi have no fire engines at all. Many councils also have no garbage trucks. This is a big problem. The donation from Creck Hardware shows that private companies can help fix this problem. The government wants more companies to give help and support to councils across the country.

en.title: Activist Agape Khombe jailed over Facebook posts about lawyer
en.body: Activist Agape Khombe is now in Maula Prison. Police arrested him last Wednesday. He was charged on Friday with offensive communication and cyberstalking. The charges are under the Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act. State prosecutor Prescott Mwayiulipo said Khombe made Facebook posts about lawyer Edgar Kachere. The posts said Kachere cheated footballer Tabitha Chawinga in a house deal in Lilongwe.
en.body_more:
Mwayiulipo told the court that Khombe's Facebook posts accused lawyer Kachere of tricking Tabitha Chawinga during a property transaction. Kachere is a private practice lawyer. The house purchase happened in Lilongwe. The Facebook posts are now at the centre of the case against Khombe.

Khombe asked the court for bail. The court said no. Mwayiulipo said Khombe had broken bail rules in a past case about a defilement charge. That earlier case was not related to this one. Because Khombe broke the rules before, the court kept him in prison.

A lawyer named Viva Nyimba is helping Khombe. Nyimba has not spoken about the case yet. The arrest has brought attention to questions about online speech in Malawi. People are asking where the line is between activism, public speech, and illegal cyberstalking. Khombe is known as an activist. The people he named in his posts are well-known. The case will come back to court. More details about the house deal may come out as the case continues.

en.title: Malawi launches five-year tax plan to raise more money
en.body: Malawi's tax authority launched a five-year plan on Monday in Blantyre. Finance Minister Joseph Mwanamvekha said the plan will help Malawi raise more money locally. The authority collected K1.40 trillion in tax in one quarter. The new plan runs from 2026 to 2031.
en.body_more:
Minister Mwanamvekha called the tax authority the "engine room of the nation." He said the plan is a contract between government and Malawians. The money raised will pay for schools, clinics, roads and public services. Mwanamvekha said Malawi must stop relying on money from other countries. Donor support is falling because of world money problems and wars.

MRA Board Chairperson MacFussy Kawawa said the authority did very well before. It reached almost all its targets in the last six years. It hit all targets in four of those six years. The new plan will focus on finding more taxpayers. It will use new computer systems. It will check who pays tax and who does not. The plan will also give better help to people who pay tax.

MRA Commissioner General Felix Tambulasi said success depends on having good staff and good systems. He said the authority will check its people and systems carefully. Tambulasi said Malawi's tax amount must grow from sixteen percent now to twenty percent by 2031. This will take hard work but the authority will measure if it gets better each year. Mwanamvekha warned that customs money will fall. Regional trade deals mean less customs tax. So the country needs more money from regular taxes on goods and income. Stronger tax money will help pay for the national budget and the National Economic Recovery Plan without needing help from other countries.

en.title: Doctor Bobe murder trial adjourned for court decision
en.body: A doctor was shot and killed at her home in Blantyre in November last year. A pathologist told the court that a bullet to the head caused instant death. Seven people are accused of the murder. The court has adjourned the trial until 30 November 2026.
en.body_more:
Dr Victoria Bobe, 33, was shot at her Chigumula Township home on 17 November 2025. She worked as a doctor at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital and taught at Kamuzu University of Health Sciences. Pathologist Steve Kamiza said the bullet entered the back of her head and left a large wound on the front. Most of her brain tissue came out. Kamiza said the death was instant homicide. A police expert said the bullet came from a semi-automatic rifle fired at close range. The firearm was not found.

A security guard named Julius Mwanamanga told the court he was on duty that night. He said armed people came with covered faces. They tied him up and broke into the house. He heard gunshots but could not see who fired them. Police officer John Julius Makolija said one suspect, Charles Chikafa, claimed the group had help from Peter Mphepo, who was a security guard at the house.

The defence lawyer Michael Goba Chipeta questioned the evidence. Pathologist Kamiza said he did not see who shot the doctor. The police expert said he also did not see the gun or the person who fired it. No DNA test was done on the firearm. Judge Ruth Chinangwa gave both sides 30 days to write their arguments. The court will rule on 30 November 2026 whether the seven accused people have a case to answer.

en.title: Police arrest four MEC officials over abuse of office
en.body: Police arrested four top officials of the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) yesterday in Lilongwe. The four are Andrew Mpesi, the former chief elections officer, Yacinto Chikapa, Khumbo Alfred Phiri, and Andrew Kamkwalala. They face allegations of abuse of office and money laundering. Police say they remain in custody.
en.body_more:
Police deputy spokesperson Alfred Chimthere confirmed the arrests. He said the four men were held on charges bordering on abuse of office and money laundering. Abuse of office means using a job position in a wrong or illegal way.

Mpesi, aged 49, was arrested at Lingadzi Police Station in Area 18, Lilongwe. His lawyer, Chrispine Ndalama, said police had not yet given details about the case. He said the allegations relate to payments for school fees for Mpesi's children and costs from a trip to Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Mpesi resigned from MEC on May 24, 2026, and officially left his job on August 21 after three months' notice.

Chikapa, aged 59, is the director of human resources and administration. Khumbo Alfred Phiri, aged 56, is the director of finance. Andrew Kamkwalala, aged 54, is the deputy chief elections officer. Their lawyer Jefferson Luwa said police were still recording statements from the suspects. The lawyers said their clients had not yet been formally charged.

This is not Mpesi's first arrest. He was arrested in February 2026 over allegations of abuse of office linked to the use of an official vehicle. He spent two days in custody before being released on bail. MEC chairperson Annabel Mtalimanja has not yet made a public statement about the new arrests.

en.title: Prison officers find 500 phones hidden in Zomba jail
en.body: Malawi's Prison Service found more than 500 mobile phones and 1,000 SIM cards hidden in Zomba Central Prison. Officers also found 5 kilograms of cannabis. Prison Service spokesperson Steven Meke told the news on Wednesday. The prison used new scanning machines to find these items.
en.body_more:
The Prison Service started this work in 2025. It worked together with MACRA, which is the group that manages radio and phone work in Malawi. The scanning machines help find phones and other things that are not allowed in the prison.

Meke said the new machines, and other safety steps, make the prison safer. Prisoners can now reform and learn better ways to live. Before the machines came, many phones got into the prison. People used these phones to do fraud and other crimes from inside the jail. Fraud is when someone lies to take money or goods from another person.

The machines stop prisoners from using phones to plan crimes outside the prison walls. The Prison Service says this pilot test at Zomba Central Prison worked very well. Because it worked well, the Prison Service may put the same machines in other prisons across Malawi. The government wants to make all prisons safer and stop crime inside them.

Meke said the Prison Service will keep making prisons more secure. It will stop banned items from entering prisons. It will also help prisoners to change their lives and become better people when they leave jail.

en.title: Court orders Reserve Bank to pay billions in lost wages
en.body: The Industrial Relations Court ruled on November 14, 2025 that the Reserve Bank of Malawi broke the law. The Bank cut executive salaries in 2020. The court said these cuts were unlawful. Former senior workers must now receive compensation. Payments range from MK800 million to MK1.5 billion.
en.body_more:
The case started when Clemence Chinkono, a former Director of Administrative Services, challenged his salary cut. His monthly pay fell from MK12,046,436 to MK9,885,937 on December 30, 2020. IRC Deputy Chairperson Annie Zinenani Gumulira ruled that the Reserve Bank could not cut salaries that workers had the right to receive under their contracts. A contract is a legal agreement between two people or organisations.

The Reserve Bank said the cuts were needed to fix problems in how it paid workers. The court rejected this argument. The judge said: "We cannot cure injustice by perpetrating another form of injustice." This means you cannot fix one wrong action by doing another wrong action. The court ordered the Bank to pay Chinkono the money he claimed, plus interest. Interest is extra money paid on top of a debt.

Other workers affected by the 2020 cuts include Deputy Governor Henry Mathanga, Grant Kabango, William Matambo, Macdonald Mafuta Mwale, Mercy Kumbatira, Joseph Milner, Frazer Mdwazika, Ralph Tseka and Donnex Chitsonga. The salary cuts happened during the time of former Governor Wilson Banda, when executive pay dropped by as much as 50 percent. Reports show Mathanga received about MK1.5 billion, which now appears to be part of this wider compensation case, not a single payment.

Fryson Chodzi, National Coordinator of Forum for National Development, said the ruling teaches a lesson about governance. Governance means how organisations make decisions and use power. He said the public should focus on who made the unlawful decisions, not on the workers receiving compensation. "Those who received compensation were vindicating their legal rights," Chodzi said. He asked whether decision-makers who knowingly broke the law should face greater responsibility when their actions cost public institutions billions of kwacha.

en.title: Silver Ladies play for semi-final place today
en.body: Silver Strikers Ladies play Nsingizini Hotspurs Women today in Gaborone, Botswana. A win will move Silver Ladies to the semi-finals of the CAF Women's Champions League Cosafa Qualifiers. Silver Ladies are second in Group B with three points. They beat Costa do Sol 2-1 but lost 3-0 to Mamelodi Sundowns.
en.body_more:
Silver Ladies coach Patricio Kulemeka said his team will attack hard and score many goals. He said they will also stay strong in defence. Kulemeka said Silver Ladies want to win without waiting for other match results. "Our ambition goes beyond simply progressing," he said. "We are national women's champions representing Malawi."

Nsingizini Hotspurs have no points and cannot reach the semi-finals. They lost 8-0 to Sundowns and 3-1 to Costa do Sol. Their coach Mpendulo Mawelela said his team is getting better. He said they are creating chances but not scoring goals. "We are always learning," Mawelela said. "I am confident we will get a good result in our final match."

Silver Ladies won the inaugural National Bank of Malawi Women's Premiership. They won 16 matches from 18. Group leaders Mamelodi Sundowns Ladies have six points. They play Costa do Sol in the other match today. The top two teams from each group go to the semi-finals. The winner will be Cosafa's only team for the CAF Women's Champions League continental finals later this year.

en.title: Navicha still has chance at Miss World Top 40
en.body: Ireen Navicha, Malawi's Miss World First Princess, did not win the Head to Head Challenge at Miss World 2026 in Vietnam. But she can still reach the Top 40. Other routes are open to her. Stephen Mdala from Miss Malawi Organisation said she remains in the contest.
en.body_more:
Navicha did not get a fast track place through the Head to Head Challenge or the Top Model competition. She also did not win the Sport Challenge, Head Chef Challenge or Talent Challenge. These races all offered automatic entry to the Top 40.

But other ways to advance still exist. Navicha can earn points through Multimedia, People's Choice and Beauty with a Purpose. The judges will also pick some contestants for the Top 40. Mdala said they are hopeful. "Despite not making it in the other challenges, she still has a chance to earn points through the remaining challenges," he said. "The judges will also have a role.
