So we are positive she will make it."

During the Head to Head Challenge, Navicha spoke about teenage pregnancies and early marriages in Malawi. She presented her project called 'When a Mother Is a Child' under the GreyNavies Foundation. This foundation helps teenage mothers return to school. The project has given scholarships, built a hostel and set up a nursery for children while their mothers study. Winners of the Head to Head Challenge came from South Africa, Nigeria, Eritrea, Kenya and Zambia in Africa. Germany, Philippines, Vietnam, Scotland, Korea, Cook Islands, USA, Bahamas, Trinidad and Tobago, Wales and Spain also won.

Lorraine Kljajic, a pageant organiser, said Navicha and Sierra Leone's contestant showed authenticity, confidence and grace. "You may not have won the Head to Head Challenge, but you won many hearts," Kljajic said. The Miss World grand finale will be on 5 September 2026.

en.title: Nico Group brings 25 US investors to Malawi
en.body: Nico Group has brought 25 US investors to Malawi for a two-week tour. The tour started on August 18, 2026. The investors want to find business chances in mining, tourism, agriculture and manufacturing. Nico Group works with the Ministry of Industrialisation, Business, Trade and Tourism on this plan.
en.body_more:
Vizenge Kumwenda is the group managing director of Nico Holdings plc. He said the tour gives investors real experience of what Malawi offers. "Malawi is an emerging market with significant long-term potential," he said. "It offers a compelling investment environment, underpinned by a welcoming population, a growing consumer class and a range of opportunities across sectors."

The partnership brings together Nico Group's money skills and business contacts with the government's plan to attract investment and build industry. The goal is to connect US investors with business chances in Malawi. Minister Simon Itaye said agriculture, tourism, mining and manufacturing are key areas for the economy. He said private-sector work, industry growth, export sales, adding value to goods and new jobs are all important. "Malawi is open for business and presents a range of investment opportunities for domestic, regional and international investors," Itaye said. He added that Malawi sits in a good place in Southern Africa. It can reach local customers and also trade with other African countries through regional and continental trade groups.

Melania Arreaga is the US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires in Malawi. She said stronger business ties between the two countries could help both. Robert Shcarar works for Africap LLC and is one of the US investors on the tour. He called Malawi a promising market with good chances for investment. The Malawi Investment and Trade Centre has run many plans over the years to bring in foreign and local investment.

en.title: Bullets sign Liberian midfielder Sheku Sheriff
en.body: FCB Nyasa Big Bullets have signed Liberian midfielder Sheku Sheriff. He is 26 years old. Sheriff comes from LPRC Oilers in Liberia. He signed a two-year deal. The contract was signed in Blantyre.
en.body_more:
Sheriff plays as an attacking midfielder. He is left-footed. He is known for his creativity and passing. He also scores from free-kicks. A free-kick is a kick given when the other team breaks a rule.

Before joining Bullets, Sheriff played in Liberia's top league. He scored four goals in 14 games. He also helped other players score five times. He has played for other clubs like LISCR FC and Shaita FC. Sheriff also plays for the Liberian national team.

Head coach Wedson Nyirenda said Bullets wanted a midfielder like Sheriff. "We wanted to add a player who can create chances and score," Nyirenda said. "Sheriff has these qualities." The coach said Sheriff plays well with the ball. He also said Sheriff has good character and leadership. This is Bullets's first new player since the summer transfer window opened on Saturday.

Sheriff said he is happy to join Bullets. "This is a big step in my career," he said. He promised to work hard and give his best. Sheriff asked supporters to back the team. "I promise to give 100 per cent whenever I play," he said.

en.title: Malawi must follow tobacco quotas to keep world buyers
en.body: An expert says Malawi must enforce tobacco production quotas to protect quality and markets. Tamani Nkhono-Mvula said in an interview that farmers must produce only the amount they are allowed. He said when farmers follow their quotas, they make better tobacco. Malawi produces more tobacco than buyers want each year.
en.body_more:
Nkhono-Mvula explained that quotas help in two ways. "When farmers produce strictly according to their allocated numbers, they invest more towards the required quality," he said. "If we overproduce, there will be no buyers for the excess crop and if we underproduce, we lose potential revenue." Revenue is money earned from selling goods.

Tobacco is very important to Malawi. It gives about half of all the money Malawi earns from selling things to other countries. It also gives about 13 percent of gross domestic product. Gross domestic product is the total value of all goods made in a country. Tobacco supports millions of people who work in the industry.

Telephorus Chigwenembe is the spokesperson for the Tobacco Commission. He said compliance means much more than just following quotas. "Compliance is mainly about adherence to standards of tobacco production, choice of seed, fertilisers, chemicals, type of labour used and environmental stewardship," he said. Farmers must follow the right methods from the start of planting to the end of processing.

The Tobacco Commission will start a new project called Know Your Grower. This project will collect detailed information about each farmer and their fields. The information will include the exact location of each field. This will help the Tobacco Commission check that farmers are following the rules. Better monitoring will help keep Malawi's tobacco at high quality and help the country sell more tobacco to other countries.

en.title: Group questions acting ACB chief over failed job test
en.body: Citizen Alliance says the government should explain why Gabriel Chembezi leads the Anti-Corruption Bureau as acting chief when he failed the test for the full job. The group says this is a problem for Malawi's anti-corruption work. Baxton Nkhoma leads Citizen Alliance. He says the ACB needs a leader that people can trust.
en.body_more:
On 24 August 2026, Nkhoma made a public statement. He said the latest job search for a new ACB Director General did not find a person who met the required level. Chembezi took the test but did not pass it. Yet Chembezi still leads the ACB in an acting way.

Nkhoma asked: if Chembezi did not pass the test for the full job, why is he good enough for the acting job? Citizen Alliance says this is not an attack on Chembezi as a person. It is a question about how the ACB is run and whether people can trust it. The government says the acting appointment is allowed by law. But Citizen Alliance says that law alone is not enough. The ACB fights corruption. It must have a leader with real skill, good character and the trust of the public.

Citizen Alliance says the acting arrangement was meant to be short. But it has gone on for a long time. This can hurt how people see the ACB. Nkhoma said: the fight against corruption cannot have uncertainty at the top. The group wants a new job search. It must be open, fair and independent. It must have clear rules about skill, honesty and experience. The group wants the government to say what went wrong in the last search. Was the test right? Was the process strong enough? What will change next time? The group asks the President, the Ministry of Justice and Parliament to move fast. Malawi needs a real ACB Director General, the group said.

en.title: Muluzi says bribe claims about ESCOM guards are false
en.body: Atupele Muluzi, who was Minister of Energy, says he did not promise former ESCOM security guards K1 million each. Muluzi is now the leader of the United Democratic Front party. He says the claims are completely false and made up. He says he never asked anyone to stop a court case.
en.body_more:
Muluzi made his statement on his Facebook page. He was answering claims published by Situation Malawi, a news website. The allegations say Muluzi promised the money to the guards while he worked as energy minister.

Muluzi said he had no knowledge of any such arrangement. He asked why serious claims were printed as fact with no evidence shown. He said the allegations could link him to things he never did. He also said he is not scared by what he calls lies. He will keep fighting back against what he calls false information.

Muluzi said political differences are normal in a democracy. But he said making up false allegations and calling them journalism is different. He challenged Situation Malawi to publish any evidence they have. If they cannot show proof, Muluzi asked them to take back the story and say sorry for the false account.

Muluzi ended by stressing three things: facts matter, truth matters, and accountability matters. He said these same standards should apply to the people making claims against him. He said he expects the same accuracy and responsibility from those accusing him. The row is likely to bring more attention to the original allegations.

en.title: Nocma loses K700 million in cyber fraud scam
en.body: Cyber criminals stole K700 million from Malawi's fuel company. The National Oil Company of Malawi (Nocma) sent the money to a fake bank account on April 29, 2026. The scammers pretended to be Mozhandling Limited, a Mozambican firm. Nocma only found out two weeks later when the real company asked for payment.
en.body_more:
The fraudsters took over email messages from Mozhandling Limited. This company normally handles fuel shipments at the Port of Nacala. The criminals forged bank documents and told Nocma that Mozhandling had opened a new account with Bank of America. Nocma believed this was true and instructed the National Bank of Malawi to send $403,605 (about K700 million) to the fake account.

Nocma management said the theft happened because of weak controls. The Government-to-Government fuel buying model was started before good security systems were ready. This created gaps that the criminals used. Nocma has now gone back to the Open Tender System for buying fuel. The company is checking all its payment processes again.

The Malawi Police Service and Bank of America are now investigating to find the stolen money. Nocma is working with law enforcement to try to get the funds back. Experts say this shows how careful state companies must be when handling millions of dollars. Nocma faces hard questions about whether it checked the bank details properly before sending the money. The company should have called Mozhandling using a different phone number to confirm the account change.

en.title: Father and son teams meet in cup final this Sunday
en.body: Mighty Wanderers and Ekhaya FC will play in the Airtel Top 8 final this Sunday at Bingu National Stadium in Lilongwe. The two teams are owned by father and son. Thomson Mpinganjira owns Wanderers. His son William owns Ekhaya FC. This is the first time father and son teams have met in a major final in Malawi.
en.body_more:
Thomson said he will not know his son's name on the pitch. "He is loved as a son, but in this field, I do not know his name," he said. "That's the beauty of football. You compete on the pitch." Thomson said the match is unique and has never happened in Malawi football before. He said people call it the 'Mpinganjira derby'.

Thomson said he was surprised when William took Ekhaya to the Super League. He said he is very proud that Ekhaya made it to the final. William pays for the team from his own money. Thomson said Ekhaya is a young team with much energy. He said if Ekhaya wins, it will be their biggest win ever. "The consequences are far-reaching," Thomson said.

William said the final is a unique story for Malawi football. He said both teams will try hard to win. "I believe Ekhaya will win," he said. "The pressure is on Mighty Wanderers, not Ekhaya FC." William said Malawi football is the real winner because this shows people care about the game. He said this creates jobs for players and helps find new talent. William said Ekhaya is still growing. "We are building with ambition," he said. This is Ekhaya's first major cup final. Mighty Wanderers has won many finals before. The winner will get K40 million.

en.title: Malawi seeks new money plan for voter lessons
en.body: Electoral groups in Malawi want a new way to pay for voter education ahead of the 2030 General Election. They say foreign donors give less money now. The government, private sector, faith groups and communities must help pay and teach voters more about elections.
en.body_more:
At a Post-Election Review National Conference in Lilongwe, Malawi Electoral Commission Chairperson Justice Annabel Mtalimanja said development partners must treat electoral support as a continuous investment. She explained that credible elections cannot depend on money that only arrives close to polling day. "It is imperative for development partners to view electoral support as a continuous investment in democratic governance rather than assistance that begins shortly before polling and ends once results are declared," she said.

Civil Society Elections Integrity Forum chairperson Benedicto Kondowe said civil society organisations need between K25 billion and K30 billion each year from now until 2030 to provide continuous civic and voter education. Chisankho Watch chairperson Bishop Gilford Matonga suggested that the Malawi Electoral Commission and National Initiative for Civic Education Trust could help close the funding gap by using their existing resources to work with more organisations. This approach would increase reach without creating new structures.

The calls follow concerns from the 2025 General Election review. That review found that civic and voter education was insufficient and poorly delivered. Only a few accredited organisations had money to work in rural communities, where voter education is needed most. In 2025, about 155,225 votes were declared null and void. Voter turnout was 76.4 percent, with 5,502,982 people casting ballots. United Nations Resident Coordinator Rebecca Adda-Dontoh called for continued investment to strengthen institutions that protect democratic processes.

en.title: IMF talks about possible loan deal for Malawi
en.body: The IMF is talking with the Malawi government about a new money deal called an ECF. ECF is a loan programme. The IMF Country Representative Yugo Koshima said the talks are going well. The old deal ended more than one year ago. The new deal could help Malawi's economy grow.
en.body_more:
In June this year, an IMF team came to Malawi to talk about the new deal. The team was led by Mission Chief Justin Tyson. They met with government leaders. Koshima said the talks focus on making the economy strong and steady. The government also started a plan called NERP. NERP means National Economic Recovery Plan. Both the ECF and NERP have the same goals: to make the economy strong and help all people.

The old deal was for four years and gave Malawi $175 million, which is about K306 billion. Malawi got that deal in 2022. It ended in May 2025. The government and IMF both agreed to end it early. When they ended it, Malawi lost about $140 million it could have got. Treasury spokesperson Williams Banda said the government wants to be careful with money. This helps the economy get well.

Right now, Malawi has a problem with exchange rates. Exchange rate is how much money you get when you change one currency to another. Official banks give K2,200 for one US dollar. But the black market gives K2,250. This gap is very big. Koshima said the rates should be the same. When the rates are the same, more foreign money flows through banks. This helps trade and brings investors to Malawi.

Koshima said prices in shops are coming down. This is good news. But Malawi must keep doing good things with money. It must have strong money rules. It must also grow farming and other business. If Malawi does these things, the economy will grow more next year. But Koshima said bad things could happen. Weather problems or world shocks could slow growth.

en.title: Malawi's Ireen Navicha misses Miss World Africa challenge
en.body: Ireen Navicha did not win the Head-to-Head Challenge at Miss World 2026 in Vietnam. South Africa's Romanda Hombir won the African round instead. Navicha talked about girls in Malawi who leave school because of teenage pregnancy and early marriage. She will try other ways to reach the Top 40.
en.body_more:
The Head-to-Head Challenge lets beauty pageant contestants show their ideas and projects to judges. Winners can get a place in the Top 40. Navicha used her time to speak about her "When a Mother Is a Child" project. This project works under the GreyNavies Foundation and helps teenage mothers go back to school.

The project gives girls scholarships and a hostel to live in. A nursery also looks after the children of young mothers while the girls are in class. Even with this work, Navicha did not win the African round. Hombir, who is 27 years old, will go to the Top 40 instead. She is from Mpumalanga in South Africa and works as a clinical audiologist, motivational speaker and model. She was crowned Miss World South Africa in July.

Navicha can still reach the Top 40 through other competitions. The new Miss World format has 40 places in the final round. Ten places come from each of four regions: Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas. Contestants can win places through five different ways: Beauty With a Purpose, Multimedia, Head-to-Head, Top Model and People's Choice. The 73rd Miss World Festival ends on September 5 in Vietnam. Navicha stays in the competition and can still try the other selection routes to reach the final round.

en.title: UTM leader and old guard clash over Malawi future
en.body: UTM Vice President Dr Mathews Mtumbuka answered back hard at former Vice-President Khumbo Kachali. Kachali made a joke about UTM leader Dalitso Kabambe at a church meeting in Kasungu. He said Kabambe must wait until 2060 before he can lead. Mtumbuka said this was not funny.
en.body_more:
Kachali made his joke at the Livingstonia Synod church meeting in Kasungu on Sunday. Many people at the meeting laughed. But Mtumbuka was not happy. He wrote on social media that Kachali's words were either a bad joke or a sign of old age, or both.

Mtumbuka told Kachali and other old leaders to step away from politics. He said UTM is not waiting for 2060. Instead, UTM has a plan for 2030. He wrote that young people must have space to lead. "We are modern politicians," he said. "We want real change and new blood."

Mtumbuka ended his message with strong words: "2030, here we come!! 2060 back to sender!" This means UTM will push forward with new ideas, not old ones.

The same day, other leaders came together at Kamuzu Academy in Kasungu for the church meeting. Second Vice-President Enoch Chihana, former president Lazarus Chakwera, and UTM leader Dalitso Kabambe all spoke about peace and unity. They said all Malawians must work as one for the country to grow. But Kachali's joke shows that differences still run deep between the old and young leaders. The fight between them shows that Malawi's leaders do not always agree on the future.

en.title: Malawi honors musician Soldier Lucius Banda
en.body: Two years after his death, Malawi remembered musician Soldier Lucius Banda at Balaka Stadium. Artists sang his songs. The government unveiled his mausoleum in Sosola Village. Lucius died in South Africa on June 30, 2024. His family and fans gathered to celebrate his life and music.
en.body_more:
The mausoleum cost K25 million. It stands in Lucius' home town of Balaka. Inside are photos and things from his life and music work. Lucius had a 35-year music career. He made 20 albums and more than 400 songs. He was born poor but became one of Malawi's greatest musicians.

At the stadium, many artists performed. The Black Missionaries, Anthony Makondetsa, Evance Meleka, Piksy, Lulu, Kelly Kay, Janta and Annie Matumbi all sang. Lucius' son Johnny, known as Mr Zembani, also performed. He thanked fans for coming. Janta said Lucius was more than a musician—he was a teacher who helped many artists. Second Vice President Enock Chihana said Lucius was his close friend and a brave man.

The Lucius Banda Foundation was launched at the concert. A museum will open soon. People's Development Party leader Kondwani Nankhumwa gave K2 million in blankets for the foundation. Lucius' widow Sunganani asked the government to build a dialysis unit in the Eastern Region. Lucius had kidney problems. Patients now travel far to get this help.

Lucius' son Johnny leads Zembani Band. Band leader Sam Smack said Johnny continues his father's work well. Lucius made songs about big issues in Malawi. His music still plays on the radio.

en.title: Safe water and toilets save African children every day
en.body: More than 1,000 children under five die each day from bad water and poor toilets. Two out of five of these children live in just ten African countries. A company called LIXIL and Japan's aid agency JICA have signed a new plan to build toilet and water markets across Africa. They want to help communities buy safe sanitation products locally.
en.body_more:
In Malawi, LIXIL worked with Water For People and Phalombe Hardware to help more than 100,000 people get better toilets and water systems. The work did not just bring in products. The team helped local shops stock items and helped people pay for them through savings groups. They also taught communities why clean water and toilets matter. From the first 10,000 products sold, people reordered more than 18,500 more. Small business owners grew their shops. Families had more choice.

Unsafe water and poor sanitation kill more children than war. In 2025, conflict killed at least 6,266 children. But disease from bad water kills far more — every single day. When fighting happens, safe water systems break down fast. Handwashing and clean toilets become even more critical to stop sickness. Building these markets now means communities are ready when crisis comes.

LIXIL and JICA say one toilet or tap alone cannot fix the problem. Governments, private companies, and local groups must work together. Products need shops to sell them. Communities need to know why they work. Business owners need money to buy stock. Governments need partners who help their plans move fast. LIXIL has already helped 100 million people get better sanitation. By 2031, they aim to help 100 million more. The work will grow in Kenya and Malawi, using JICA's money and ideas.

en.title: Bullets draw with Luanar at Dedza. Title race stays close.
en.body: FCB Nyasa Big Bullets drew 0-0 with Luanar Mitundu on Sunday at Dedza Stadium in the FDH Bank Premiership. Bullets coach Wedson Nyirenda said the pitch was not good. Bullets now have 27 points from 14 games and sit fourth in the table.
en.body_more:
Nyirenda was very cross after the match. He said Dedza Stadium ground is not fit to play football. He said the pitch was not suitable for top-flight games. The coach felt the bad ground stopped his team from scoring. Bullets had many chances but could not find the goal.

The match had many problems. In the 32nd minute, the referee made a bad call. Bullets players stopped playing after a foul. But the referee let play go on. Rahim Mtondera ran clear on goal. Innocent Nyasulu, the Bullets keeper, made a great save. Nyirenda was so angry at the referee that he got a yellow card. Emmanuel Kanthiti, the Luanar keeper, also made many good saves. Clever Kalambo played for Bullets after coming back from a ban.

Bullets have now kept three clean sheets in a row. This is good defence. But they did not score, and this is a problem. Luanar coach Oscar Kaunda said his team played well. He was happy with the draw. Luanar now have 19 points from 14 games and are seventh. Luanar must play Goshen City next in the first round.

Nyirenda said his team will need new players. He will talk with his coaches about what the team needs. The draw means Bullets are four points behind the league leader. The title race is still close. Many grounds in Malawi have bad pitches, and this is a big problem for top-flight football.

en.title: Vice President Ansah speaks at church women's conference
en.body: Vice President Jane Ansah went to a church conference in Ntcheu on Sunday. The Zambezi Evangelical Church held a women's meeting at Manjawira. Ansah told the women to use their faith and skills to make money. Church leaders gave her a goat and a Bible.
en.body_more:
The conference was run by the Chiole Synod Women's Guild Department. Women and church leaders came from across the Chiole Synod. The meeting's theme was "Mchipululu Simofela," which comes from the Bible book Isaiah.

Ansah told the women not to give up when money is hard to find. She said education and skills training help women earn money and help their families. Women must go to school, learn new work, and start small businesses, she said. She also said difficult times are chances to find new ways forward, not reasons to stop trying. Ansah praised the church for helping with schools, farms, and helping poor people. She said the church and government must work together more to help communities.

Ansah also spoke about the Malawi Scorchers women's soccer team and their Africa Cup of Nations campaign. She said the unity and support shown during the games should help all Malawians work together for the country. She called on people to keep this spirit of teamwork.

Chimwemwe Chikhadzula, a church leader, said the women's group helps sick people, old people, and poor families. The group also teaches people how to do work and start small business. But she said they do not have enough cars, materials, or money to start businesses. She asked the government and other helpers to give more support so more people can be helped.

en.title: Many Malawi men find children are not theirs
en.body: DNA tests in Malawi show that about 80 out of every 100 men who test are not the real fathers of their children. Two testing companies in Blantyre and Lilongwe report this same pattern. Men often test when they think their partner was not faithful. The test results are causing family problems and court fights over money and who looks after the children.
en.body_more:
Kingdom Kwapata is a scientist at Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources. He does DNA tests. He says most men come to him after they find messages on WhatsApp that make them worry. About 80 percent of the time, these men are right — the child is not theirs. Kwapata does more than 30 tests every month. That is about 400 tests each year. He says when courts tell men to pay money for children they do not think are theirs, the results are different. About 90 percent of those men turn out to be the real fathers.

Phillip Mwanza runs Attestation Background Checks and DNA Limited Malawi. His clinics are in Blantyre and Lilongwe. He gets about 20 people each month. His results match Kwapata's — about 80 percent of men are not the fathers. Mwanza says tests cost between K600,000 and K1 million. Results come back in 10 days. The tests help men protect their money and land when they split from their partners.

Divorce cases in Malawi are going up fast. Court records show that in 2020, there were 1,170 divorce cases. By 2022, there were 2,504. Most divorces are between people aged 20 to 35. Ruth Mputeni works for the courts. She says the numbers are still being counted. Bishop Gilford Matonga from the Public Affairs Committee says this is a sign of moral problems. He says both men and women are not staying faithful to their partners.

en.title: Malawi's money reserves grow, but help slow
en.body: Malawi's foreign money reserves rose to $616.3 million in June 2026. This is enough money for 2.5 months of goods to buy from other countries. The money came from tobacco sales and private business. But experts say this is still not enough. Businesses still cannot find foreign money to buy things abroad.
en.body_more:
The Reserve Bank of Malawi said the money grew from $596.5 million in May. In June last year, the country had only $555.9 million. This is a rise of $60.4 million in one year. The bank said both the government and private business helped this grow.

But many experts are not happy. They say Malawi needs 3 months of money reserves. The country has only 2.5 months now. Economist Edward Lemani said this may not last. He said Malawi buys too many things from other countries and sells too few. Most money comes from tobacco sales, not from many types of business. Lemani said the country needs more exports from many types of work.

Businesses still have big problems. People cannot get foreign money to put on cards to travel. Factory owners cannot get money to buy things they need from abroad. Economist Christopher Mbukwa said the real test is this: Can businesses get foreign money fast? Does the price at the real market match the price at the bank? Mbukwa said Malawi must grow other types of business. Mining, tourism, and new business from other countries can help. But the country must stop using only tobacco to earn foreign money.

en.title: Wanderers return to top after beating Red Lions
en.body: Mighty Wanderers won 2-1 against Red Lions on Saturday. The win took them to the top of the Malawi FDH Bank Premiership. Wanderers now have 29 points from 14 matches. They lead second-place Silver Strikers by just one point. One week remains in the first round of the league.
en.body_more:
Silver Strikers can move back to the top on Sunday. They play Goshen City Dedza Dynamos at Silver Stadium in Lilongwe. Silver Strikers have 28 points but have played one fewer game. A win would put them on top with one game to play in the first round.

FCB Nyasa Big Bullets, the defending champions, are also still in the race. They have 26 points and will play Luanar Mitundu Football Club at Dedza Stadium on Sunday. The three top teams are separated by only a few points. Every match in the final week matters.

Wanderers coach Bob Mpinganjira said his team needed to recover and play better. He said the team had struggled in their last three games. Mpinganjira said his players could score goals and this would help them win. He also said his team understood how Red Lions played because they had faced other Army teams before.

Red Lions came to the match from Zomba with 19 points from 13 games. They sit sixth in the table. Wanderers are based in Blantyre and play at Mpira Stadium. The first round of the Malawi FDH Bank Premiership will end this weekend.

en.title: Soldier Lucius Banda's Mausoleum Unveiled in Balaka
en.body: The mausoleum of musician Soldier Lucius Banda was unveiled in Sosola Village, Balaka. The mausoleum honors the life of one of Malawi's most famous musicians. Lucius died two years ago. His family built the mausoleum with help from close friends.
en.body_more:
The Lucius Banda Foundation will manage the mausoleum. This foundation will work to preserve and promote Lucius's life and music. Lucius was born and raised in Balaka. He became one of Malawi's most important musicians. His music career lasted 35 years. He made 20 albums and more than 400 songs. These songs spoke about poverty, unfair treatment, government problems, corruption, love, family and justice.

Lucius was also a politician. He was a Member of Parliament for Balaka North two times. He worked with two political parties: the United Democratic Front and the United Transformation Movement. Before he died, he was a presidential adviser on youth and culture under former president Lazarus Chakwera.

The mausoleum has photos, memorabilia and documents of his life and career. It shows his work in music and politics. His son Johnny Zembani Banda said the family wants to build a museum at the site. This museum will be a place where Malawians and visitors can learn about Lucius's life. The museum will show his music, photographs, instruments, belongings and recordings. It will help young people understand the history and society in which Lucius made his music.

After the mausoleum was unveiled, there was a celebration at Balaka Stadium. Many artists performed, including Phungu Joseph Nkasa, Coss Chiwalo, Zembani Band, Paul Subili, Alleluya Band, Black Missionaries and Lulu. Lulu worked with Soldier for many years before starting his own band called Mathumela Band. Lulu recently made a song called 'Soja' to remember Soldier.

ny.title: Nyumba Yaikulu ya Msilikali Lucius Banda Yatsegulidwa ku Balaka
ny.body: Manda a woimba Soldier Lucius Banda adawululidwa ku Sosola Village, Balaka. Mandawa amalemekeza moyo wa m'modzi mwa oimba otchuka kwambiri ku Malawi. Lucius anamwalira zaka ziwiri zapitazo. Banja lake linamanga mandawa mothandizidwa ndi mabwenzi apamtima.
ny.body_more:
Lucius Banda Foundation idzayang'anira mabwinja a nyumbayi. Maziko awa adzagwira ntchito yosunga ndi kukweza moyo ndi nyimbo za Lucius. Lucius anabadwira ndikuleredwa ku Balaka. Anakhala m'modzi mwa oimba ofunikira kwambiri ku Malawi. Ntchito yake yoimba inatenga zaka 35. Anapanga ma Albums 20 ndi nyimbo zoposa 400. Nyimbozi zinkanena za umphawi, nkhanza zosalungama, mavuto aboma, ziphuphu, chikondi, banja ndi chilungamo.

Lucius analinso wandale. Anali membala wa Nyumba Yamalamulo ya Balaka North kawiri. Anagwira ntchito ndi zipani ziwiri zandale: United Democratic Front ndi United Transformation Movement. Asanamwalire, anali mlangizi wa purezidenti pa achinyamata ndi chikhalidwe pansi pa purezidenti wakale Lazarus Chakwera.

Mabwinja a nyumbayi ali ndi zithunzi, zokumbukira ndi zikalata za moyo wake ndi ntchito yake. Akuwonetsa ntchito yake mu nyimbo ndi ndale. Mwana wake wamwamuna Johnny Zembani Banda adati banjali likufuna kumanga nyumba yosungiramo zinthu zakale pamalopo. Nyumba yosungiramo zinthu zakale iyi idzakhala malo omwe anthu aku Malawi ndi alendo angaphunzire za moyo wa Lucius. Nyumba yosungiramo zinthu zakaleyi idzawonetsa nyimbo zake, zithunzi, zida, katundu wake ndi zojambulira zake. Zithandiza achinyamata kumvetsetsa mbiri ndi chikhalidwe cha anthu omwe Lucius adapangira nyimbo zake.

Pambuyo poti manda a anthu adawululidwa, panali chikondwerero ku Balaka Stadium. Oimba ambiri adachita sewero, kuphatikizapo Phungu Joseph Nkasa, Coss Chiwalo, Zembani Band, Paul Subili, Alleluya Band, Black Missionaries ndi Lulu. Lulu adagwira ntchito ndi Soldier kwa zaka zambiri asanayambitse gulu lake lotchedwa Mathumela Band. Posachedwapa Lulu adapanga nyimbo yotchedwa 'Soja' yokumbukira Soldier.

en.title: High Court grants bail to activist Sylvester Namiwa
en.body: The High Court in Lilongwe gave bail to human rights activist Sylvester Namiwa on Friday. Namiwa faces charges of treason and publishing false news. Judge Mzonde Mvula set bail conditions and ordered a hearing for September 8, 2026. Namiwa was arrested on July 30 after a television interview.
en.body_more:
Namiwa, aged 48, is the executive director of the Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (Cdedi). The broadcast was on Luntha Television on July 28. The state says Namiwa committed treason by claiming Vice-President Jane Ansah would become President within two months. This would happen outside any legal process. Treason is a serious crime against the state.

Namiwa also faces a charge of publishing false news. The state claims he said five senior ruling party figures were using people from Dzaleka Refugee Camp and prisons to kill targeted people. Judge Mvula said the law in Malawi gives bail to most people, especially those who live in the country. The 90-day detention period had not ended, but the state did not fight the bail application because it had finished collecting evidence.

Bail conditions are strict. Namiwa must pay K5 million in cash. Two family members must each provide K10 million bonds. Bonds are money promised to the court. He must give his passport to the court. He must report to National Police Headquarters every Monday. The court ordered Namiwa and Cdedi not to speak about the case in public or hold press conferences. This is a significant restriction on his work as an activist.

Namiwa's lawyer, Gift John Mwenye, said the bond money was paid. However, administrative work with the prison, police and prosecutors delayed his release from Maula Prison. The state must show all evidence to the defence within seven days. Any new charges must be served by summons, not by arrest.

en.title: Chilima plane crash inquiry resumes with witness hearings
en.body: A Parliamentary committee investigating the plane crash that killed former Vice President Saulos Klaus Chilima will restart its inquiry next week. The crash happened on 10 June 2024 in Chikangawa Forest. It killed Chilima and eight other people. The committee will hear from witnesses from Monday, 24 August to Friday, 11 September 2026.
en.body_more:
This is Phase Two of the inquiry. The first phase has already finished. This new phase will focus only on what happened on the day of the flight.

The Parliamentary Ad-Hoc Committee will call many types of witnesses. These include airport staff who planned the flight, checked the weather, and filled the plane with fuel. The committee will also hear from weather experts and pilots who have flown the same aircraft. Community members who saw what happened around Nthungwa Forest, near the crash site, will also give evidence. The committee may call other people if their stories are important to the inquiry.

Walter Nyamilandu Manda is the chairperson of the committee. He said the new phase is crucial. It will help the committee understand what happened on the day of the crash. Nyamilandu said in a statement that all the hearings will be open to the public and media. The committee may close some hearings if it chooses to follow parliament's rules.

Malawi has waited more than two years for answers about the crash. It was a shocking event for the nation. Chilima was a very important political figure. The inquiry hopes to find the truth about why the plane crashed in Chikangawa Forest.

en.title: Zambia Certifies Usingini Upland Coffee From Malawi
en.body: A Malawian coffee company has received a certificate from Zambia. The Zambia Bureau of Standards approved Usingini Upland Coffee from Fecko Investment. This approval lets the company sell coffee to other African countries. The coffee is roasted beans, ground coffee, and filter bags.
en.body_more:
Fecko Investment is based in Lilongwe. The company grows and processes Usingini Upland Coffee. Dominic Joseph is the Out-growers National Coordinator. He said the company can now make one thousand kilograms of roasted coffee each month. Three years ago, it made only three hundred kilograms per month. Joseph said the certificate proves the coffee is good enough for the world.

The Certificate was issued on April 30 2026. It follows the African Organisation for Standardisation rules. The Zambia Bureau of Standards checked how the coffee is made. They checked the control and cleanliness of the factory. This certification meets the African Conformity Assessment Programme rules.

The Coffee Association of Malawi said this is very good news. The secretary general is Kondwani Nanchukwa. He said the certificate helps Usingini coffee cross into many African countries. He said the coffee is now acceptable inside and outside Africa. Nanchukwa also said many people smuggle coffee out of Malawi. This means the coffee does not count as official exports. Smuggling is illegal trade. The prices of coffee inside Malawi went up very high. In 2024, coffee cost seven thousand Kwacha per kilogram. At the end of 2025, it cost twenty-one thousand Kwacha per kilogram.

Coffee export money has changed many times. In 2021, Malawi sold coffee worth two point eight million United States dollars. In 2022, it sold only one point one million dollars. In 2023, it sold one point six million dollars. In 2024, it sold three point four million dollars. Joseph said Fecko Investment wants to keep growing. He said the company will help more farmers grow coffee.

en.title: Malawi Scorchers get money after big success
en.body: The Malawi National Women's Football Team, the Scorchers, will get money after doing well at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. The team came second and qualified for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil. On Thursday, leaders gave new promises of money at a lunch at State House in Lilongwe.
en.body_more:
The Scorchers lost the final 3-0 to Cameroon on August 16, 2026. But this was not their first time at this big tournament. Before 2026, Malawi had never been to the Africa Cup of Nations. The team was ranked 153rd in the world.

The Scorchers beat many strong teams. They won 3-2 against Nigeria on July 28, 2026. Nigeria were the defending champions. Temwa Chawinga scored twice and captain Tabitha Chawinga scored once. The team then beat Ghana 2-1 on August 10, 2026, and then beat Algeria to reach the final. This success means Malawi will go to the World Cup for the first time.

On August 20, 2026, First Lady Madam Gertrude Mutharika called on companies to give money to the team. She spoke at the lunch at State House. The National Bank of Malawi has already given K280 million to start a national women's league in July 2025. This league has 10 teams from all three regions. Each team plays 18 matches. The bank also gives K1.5 billion each year for women's football and the Scorchers.

Experts say Malawi must now build a strong system to make more good teams. The country has started an academy in Mzuzu in 2024 and has youth leagues. But Malawi needs more youth competitions and a cup for women. This will help find new players early and train them well before they join the senior team.

en.title: Rights group asks for new rules on seizing assets
en.body: A human rights group in Malawi is asking the government to change the laws about seizing assets from criminals. The Human Rights Consultative Committee said this on Friday in Lilongwe. They say the government must take stolen money and things from bad people. But they also worry the government is not doing this fairly to all people.
en.body_more:
The HRCC Board chairperson Robert Mkwezalamba said the group will give new ideas to the Law Commission. He said: "We must stop criminals from hiding money. But human rights must not be hurt in this fight. The law must be strong enough to do both things."

The HRCC wants the government to check all the things it has taken from people. They want to know what happened to these things. They want to know how much money came from selling them. The group will talk to the Ministry of Justice, the courts, Parliament and lawyers. Together they will write new laws for how to seize assets.

During the news meeting, the HRCC also said good things about the court. The court let Sylvester Namiwa go home on bail. Namiwa is the leader of the Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives. He was in jail. The court said he did treason and shared false news. Judge Mvula set rules for Namiwa. He must give K5 million cash to the court. He must find two people to promise K10 million each. Namiwa must go to the police every Monday. He must live at his home in Kaphiri. He must give his passport to the court. He cannot talk about his case to anyone. He cannot hold news meetings until the case is done.

en.title: Court stops government plan to move election office
en.body: A High Court judge has blocked the government's bid to move the Malawi Electoral Commission from Lilongwe to Blantyre. Judge Kenyatta Nyirenda said on Thursday that the case must continue through the courts. The government wanted to stop the case from going forward, but the judge refused.
en.body_more:
The government, led by Chief Secretary Justin Saidi and Minister Chimwemwe Chipungu, asked the court to lift a stay on the case. A stay is an order that stops a case from moving ahead. Attorney General Frank Mbeta argued that the stay should be removed so the government could ask for the case to be thrown out.

The opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) and three of its lawmakers challenged the relocation plan in court on June 5. That day, Judge Nyirenda gave them an injunction restraining, or stopping, the move to Blantyre. He then put the case on hold pending a decision from the Chief Justice on whether constitutional issues were at stake. Constitutional issues are questions about whether something follows the rules set out in the country's Constitution.

In his ruling on Thursday, Judge Nyirenda said the questions raised must be decided through judicial review. Judicial review is a type of court case where judges check if the government is acting lawfully. The judge said the matters could not be properly decided through simple written evidence. He warned that doing so would damage the importance of constitutional law in Malawi.

MCP lawyer George Kadzipatike argued that his clients have a right to challenge the move because they take part in elections. He said the President has no power to order an independent commission to move through an Executive Order. Executive Orders are written commands from the President. The court will now examine whether the President has legal authority to relocate an independent constitutional body, and whether the relocation violates sections 75 and 76 of the Constitution. Meanwhile, the MEC has delayed elections in Nsanje South and Mangochi East due to lack of materials and problems accessing its sealed warehouse in Lilongwe.

ny.title: Khoti laletsa dongosolo la boma losamutsa ofesi ya zisankho
ny.body: Woweruza milandu wa Khoti Lalikulu waletsa boma kuti lisamutse bungwe la Malawi Electoral Commission kuchoka ku Lilongwe kupita ku Blantyre. Woweruza milandu Kenyatta Nyirenda adati Lachinayi kuti mlanduwu upitirire m'makhoti. Boma linkafuna kuletsa mlanduwu kuti usapitirire, koma woweruza milanduyo anakana.
ny.body_more:
Boma, lotsogozedwa ndi Mlembi Wamkulu Justin Saidi ndi Nduna Chimwemwe Chipungu, linapempha khoti kuti lichotse kuimitsa mlanduwo. Kuimitsa mlandu ndi lamulo lomwe limaletsa mlandu kuti usapitirire. Loya Wamkulu Frank Mbeta anati kuimitsa mlanduwo kuyenera kuchotsedwa kuti boma lipemphe kuti mlanduwo uchotsedwe.

Chipani chotsutsa cha Malawi Congress Party (MCP) ndi atatu mwa opanga malamulo ake adatsutsa dongosolo losamutsa anthu kukhothi pa June 5. Tsiku limenelo, Woweruza Nyirenda adawapatsa lamulo loletsa, kapena kuletsa, kusamuka ku Blantyre. Kenako adayimitsa mlanduwo podikira chigamulo cha Woweruza Wamkulu pankhani ya ngati nkhani za malamulo zili pachiwopsezo. Nkhani za malamulo ndi mafunso okhudza ngati china chake chikutsatira malamulo omwe ali mu Constitution ya dzikolo.

Mu chigamulo chake Lachinayi, Woweruza Nyirenda adati mafunso omwe afunsidwa ayenera kugamulidwa kudzera mukuwunikanso kwa khothi. Kuwunikanso kwa milandu ndi mtundu wa mlandu wa khothi komwe oweruza amafufuza ngati boma likuchita zinthu mwalamulo. Woweruzayo adati nkhanizo sizingagamulidwe bwino kudzera mu umboni wolembedwa wosavuta. Anachenjeza kuti kuchita izi kungawononge kufunika kwa malamulo a malamulo ku Malawi.

Loya wa chipani cha MCP, George Kadzipatike, adati makasitomala ake ali ndi ufulu wotsutsa chisankhochi chifukwa amatenga nawo mbali pa zisankho. Iye anati Purezidenti alibe mphamvu zolamula bungwe lodziyimira pawokha kuti lipereke chigamulo kudzera mu Lamulo la Akuluakulu. Malamulo a Akuluakulu ndi malamulo olembedwa ochokera kwa Purezidenti. Khothi tsopano lifufuza ngati Purezidenti ali ndi mphamvu zovomerezeka zosamukira bungwe lodziyimira pawokha, komanso ngati kusamutsaku kukuphwanya magawo 75 ndi 76 a Malamulo Oyendetsera Dziko. Pakadali pano, MEC yachedwetsa zisankho ku Nsanje South ndi Mangochi East chifukwa cha kusowa kwa zipangizo komanso mavuto olowera m'nyumba yake yosungiramo zinthu yotsekedwa ku Lilongwe.

en.title: Court frees activist Namiwa on bail with strict rules
en.body: High Court Judge Mzondi Mvula freed rights activist Sylvester Namiwa on bail on Friday, 21 August 2026. Namiwa must pay K5 million cash and find two people to promise K10 million each. He cannot leave Kaphiri or speak about the case to anyone.
en.body_more:
Judge Mvula set many conditions for Namiwa's freedom. He must go to Area 30 Police Station every two weeks on Monday. He cannot comment on the case in any way. He cannot hold press meetings about it. He must give his passport to the court, but can ask to travel if he needs to. He must also give a copy of his National ID to the police.

Namiwa was arrested on 30 July 2026 after police called him to National Police Headquarters in Lilongwe. Police first said he published false news and caused trouble. But the charge grew bigger. The Lilongwe Chief Resident Magistrate's Court charged him with treason. Treason is a crime against the country. He also faces a charge of publishing false news that makes people fear.

The charges come from words Namiwa spoke on Luntha TV in July. He said Vice President Jane Ansah would become President in two months. This claim shocked many people in Malawi. No one knows who told him to say it.

Namiwa leads the Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives. This group checks what government workers do. Judge Mvula said he was upset about false stories about the case. He said courts make choices based only on law, not on what people outside say. Namiwa's treason trial will start on 8 September 2026. Until then, he will be free but must follow all the court's rules.

ny.title: Khothi lamasula Namiwa yemwe anali womenyera ufulu wa anthu pa belo ndi malamulo okhwima
ny.body: Woweruza milandu wa Khoti Lalikulu, Mzondi Mvula, wamasula Sylvester Namiwa yemwe anali womenyera ufulu wa anthu pa belo Lachisanu, pa 21 Ogasiti 2026. Namiwa ayenera kulipira ndalama zokwana K5 miliyoni ndikupeza anthu awiri oti alonjeze K10 miliyoni aliyense. Sangachoke ku Kaphiri kapena kulankhula za nkhaniyi kwa aliyense.
ny.body_more:
Woweruza Mvula adakhazikitsa zinthu zambiri kuti Namiwa atuluke. Ayenera kupita ku Area 30 Police Station milungu iwiri iliyonse Lolemba. Sangathe kunenapo kanthu pa nkhaniyi mwanjira iliyonse. Sangathe kuchita misonkhano ya atolankhani. Ayenera kupereka pasipoti yake kukhothi, koma akhoza kupempha kuti apite ngati akufunikira. Ayeneranso kupereka kopi ya National ID yake kwa apolisi.

Namiwa adamangidwa pa 30 Julayi 2026 apolisi atamuyitana ku National Police Headquarters ku Lilongwe. Apolisi adati poyamba adafalitsa nkhani zabodza ndipo adayambitsa mavuto. Koma mlanduwo unakula kwambiri. Khothi la Chief Resident Magistrate ku Lilongwe linamuimba mlandu woukira boma. Kuukira boma ndi mlandu wotsutsana ndi dzikolo. Akukumananso ndi mlandu wofalitsa nkhani zabodza zomwe zimapangitsa anthu kuopa.

Milanduyi imachokera ku mawu omwe Namiwa adalankhula pa Luntha TV mu Julayi. Adati Wachiwiri kwa Purezidenti Jane Ansah adzakhala Purezidenti pakatha miyezi iwiri. Izi zidadabwitsa anthu ambiri ku Malawi. Palibe amene akudziwa yemwe adamuuza kuti anene.

Namiwa akutsogolera Center for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives. Gululi limafufuza zomwe ogwira ntchito m'boma amachita. Woweruza Mvula anati akukhumudwa ndi nkhani zabodza zokhudza nkhaniyi. Anati makhothi amapanga zisankho potengera lamulo lokha, osati zomwe anthu akunja akunena. Mlandu wa Namiwa wokhudza kuukira boma uyamba pa 8 Seputembala 2026. Mpaka nthawi imeneyo, adzakhala mfulu koma ayenera kutsatira malamulo onse a khothi.

en.title: Silver Ladies win first game in big African football tournament
en.body: Silver Strikers Ladies won 2-1 against Costa Do Sol from Mozambique. The game was in Botswana on Friday. Silver Strikers lost first, then came back to win. Ireen Khumalo and Grace Kakangula scored for Silver Strikers.
en.body_more:
The match took place at Gaborone United Stadium in Botswana. Silver Strikers fell behind very fast. Costa Do Sol scored in just 18 seconds. But Silver Strikers did not give up. They came back strong in the second half.

Ireen Khumalo scored the first goal for Silver Strikers. She kicked a free-kick into the net in the 68th minute. This made the score 1-1. Later, Grace Kakangula scored the winning goal. She scored in the 86th minute. Costa Do Sol had only 10 players at that time. One player got a red card and had to leave the game.

Silver Strikers is the champion of Malawi. They won the National Bank of Malawi Women's Premiership. This is their first time in this big African tournament. The tournament is called the CAF Women's Champions League COSAFA Qualifier. Silver Strikers play in Group B. The tournament has eight teams in two groups. The top two teams from each group go to the semi-finals.

Silver Strikers will play their next game on Sunday, August 23. They will face Mamelodi Sundowns Ladies from South Africa. After that, they will play Nsingizini Hotspurs from Eswatini on September 1. Coach Patricio Kulemeka said he is proud of his team. He said the win is very important for their campaign. Five players on the team also played for Malawi at the Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco.

ny.title: Silver Ladies yapambana masewera oyamba mu mpikisano waukulu wa mpira wa ku Africa
ny.body: Silver Strikers Ladies idapambana 2-1 motsutsana ndi Costa Do Sol yaku Mozambique. Masewerawa anali ku Botswana Lachisanu. Silver Strikers idataya koyamba, kenako idabweranso kuti ipambane. Ireen Khumalo ndi Grace Kakangula adagoletsa zigoli za Silver Strikers.
ny.body_more:
Masewerowa adachitikira ku Gaborone United Stadium ku Botswana. Silver Strikers idabwerera m'mbuyo mwachangu kwambiri. Costa Do Sol adagoletsa mu masekondi 18 okha. Koma Silver Strikers sanataye mtima. Adabweranso mwamphamvu mu theka lachiwiri.

Ireen Khumalo adagoletsa chigoli choyamba cha Silver Strikers. Adaponya free-kick mu ukonde mu mphindi ya 68. Izi zidapangitsa kuti zigolizo zikhale 1-1. Pambuyo pake, Grace Kakangula adagoletsa chigoli chopambana. Adagoletsa mu mphindi ya 86. Costa Do Sol anali ndi osewera 10 okha panthawiyo. Wosewera m'modzi adalandira khadi lofiira ndipo adayenera kuchoka pamasewerawa.

Silver Strikers ndiye ngwazi ya Malawi. Adapambana National Bank of Malawi Women's Premiership. Iyi ndi nthawi yawo yoyamba mu mpikisano waukulu wa Africa. Mpikisanowu umatchedwa CAF Women's Champions League COSAFA Qualifier. Silver Strikers imasewera mu Gulu B. Mpikisanowu uli ndi magulu asanu ndi atatu m'magulu awiri. Magulu awiri apamwamba kuchokera pagulu lililonse amapita ku semi-finals.

Silver Strikers idzasewera masewera awo otsatira Lamlungu, pa 23 Ogasiti. Adzasewera ndi Mamelodi Sundowns Ladies ochokera ku South Africa. Pambuyo pake, adzasewera ndi Nsingizini Hotspurs ochokera ku Eswatini pa 1 Seputembala. Mphunzitsi Patricio Kulemeka adati akunyadira timu yake. Iye anati kupambana kumeneku n'kofunika kwambiri pa kampeni yawo. Osewera asanu mu timuyi adaseweranso ndi Malawi pa Women's Africa Cup of Nations ku Morocco.

en.title: Malawi Scorchers get K5 million each from President
en.body: President Peter Mutharika gave K5 million to each player of the Malawi Women's National Football Team. First Lady Gertrude Mutharika gave the money at a lunch on Thursday in Lilongwe. The Scorchers came back from Morocco. They lost 3-0 to Cameroon in the final.
en.body_more:
The Scorchers finished second at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations. This was their first time at the tournament. They also qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil as semi-finalists.

During the tournament, the Scorchers beat Nigeria 3-2, Egypt 3-1, and Ghana 2-1. They lost 2-1 to Zambia but still won their group. In the semi-final, they beat Algeria 2-1. The team won K750,000 as prize money for finishing second.

Team captain Tabitha Chawinga said the players need more help to prepare for the World Cup. She said the team did well even with little support at home. Chawinga asked for more money from the government and other people to help the team train. She said women's football can bring money to the country.

National Bank of Malawi, the team's main sponsor, said it gave K500 million to help women's football. The bank's leader Grant Kabango said the bank will keep helping the team. Cabinet ministers also gave K25 million to the team. Football Association of Malawi president Fleetwood Haiya said the country is now getting good results from investing in women's football.

ny.title: A Scorchers a Malawi alandira K5 miliyoni kuchokera kwa Purezidenti aliyense
ny.body: Purezidenti Peter Mutharika adapereka K5 miliyoni kwa wosewera aliyense wa timu ya mpira wa azimayi ya Malawi. Mkazi woyamba Gertrude Mutharika adapereka ndalamazo pa chakudya chamasana Lachinayi ku Lilongwe. A Scorchers adabwera kuchokera ku Morocco. Adagonja 3-0 ndi Cameroon pamasewera omaliza.
ny.body_more:
A Scorchers adamaliza pa nambala yachiwiri pa mpikisano wa Women's Africa Cup of Nations wa 2026. Iyi inali nthawi yawo yoyamba pa mpikisanowu. Adalowanso mu mpikisano wa FIFA Women's World Cup wa 2027 ku Brazil ngati ofika mu semi-final.

Pa mpikisanowu, a Scorchers adagonjetsa Nigeria 3-2, Egypt 3-1, ndi Ghana 2-1. Adataya 2-1 ndi Zambia koma adapambanabe gulu lawo. Mu semi-final, adagonjetsa Algeria 2-1. Gululi lidapambana K750,000 ngati ndalama zolipirira kuti likhale lachiwiri.

Kaputeni wa gululi Tabitha Chawinga adati osewerawa akufunika thandizo lochulukirapo kuti akonzekere World Cup. Iye adati gululi lidachita bwino ngakhale litakhala ndi chithandizo chochepa kunyumba. Chawinga adapempha ndalama zambiri kuchokera ku boma ndi anthu ena kuti athandize gululi kuphunzitsa. Iye adati mpira wa azimayi ukhoza kubweretsa ndalama mdzikolo.

National Bank of Malawi, yomwe ndi kampani yayikulu yothandizira gululi, idati idapereka K500 miliyoni kuti ithandize mpira wa azimayi. Mtsogoleri wa bankiyi, Grant Kabango, adati bankiyi ipitiliza kuthandiza timuyi. Nduna za boma zinaperekanso K25 miliyoni ku timuyi. Purezidenti wa Football Association of Malawi, Fleetwood Haiya, adati dzikolo tsopano likupeza zotsatira zabwino chifukwa choyika ndalama mu mpira wa azimayi.

en.title: PressCane gives road cones to Milare Police for safety
en.body: PressCane Limited gave new road cones to Milare Police Substation in Blantyre on Wednesday. The police asked for help after their old cones broke. The cones help officers stay safe and visible when they work on roads.
en.body_more:
Mercy Kamanga is the Sales and Marketing Manager at PressCane Limited. She gave the cones at a handover ceremony. She said PressCane makes ethanol in different types. The company uses ethanol to blend petrol in Malawi. PressCane has many tankers that travel to fuel depots. This means the safety of drivers and police officers is very important to the company.

Kamanga also said the donation is part of PressCane's work to help communities. The company operates in the Blantyre area. It wants to support the people who live there. The donation shows this support.

Senior Superintendent Iweni Matinga is the Officer-in-Charge at Milare Police Substation. He received the cones from PressCane. Matinga said the police were looking for cones for a long time. All of their old cones had worn out. He said the police wrote to PressCane to ask for help. Matinga thanked PressCane for giving the cones. He said PressCane is helping police and road safety in the area. The new cones will help officers do their work more safely. Motorists will see police officers better on the busy Blantyre-Chikwawa Road.

ny.title: PressCane yapereka ma cones a msewu kwa apolisi a Milare kuti atetezeke
ny.body: PressCane Limited yapereka ma cone atsopano amisewu ku siteshoni ya apolisi ya Milare ku Blantyre Lachitatu. Apolisi adapempha thandizo ma cone awo akale atasweka. Ma cone amathandiza apolisi kukhala otetezeka komanso owonekera akamagwira ntchito m'misewu.
ny.body_more:
Mercy Kamanga ndi Woyang'anira Malonda ndi Malonda ku PressCane Limited. Iye anapereka ma cone pa mwambo wopereka. Iye anati PressCane imapanga ethanol m'mitundu yosiyanasiyana. Kampaniyo imagwiritsa ntchito ethanol kusakaniza mafuta ku Malawi. PressCane ili ndi matanki ambiri omwe amapita kumalo osungira mafuta. Izi zikutanthauza kuti chitetezo cha oyendetsa ndi apolisi n'chofunika kwambiri kwa kampaniyo.

Kamanga adatinso zoperekazi ndi gawo la ntchito ya PressCane yothandiza madera. Kampaniyo imagwira ntchito mdera la Blantyre. Ikufuna kuthandiza anthu okhala kumeneko. Zoperekazi zikusonyeza thandizo ili.

Senior Superintendent Iweni Matinga ndiye Wapolisi Woyang'anira ku Milare Police Substation. Analandira ma cone kuchokera ku PressCane. Matinga adati apolisi akhala akufunafuna ma cone kwa nthawi yayitali. Ma cone awo onse akale anali atatha. Iye anati apolisi adalembera PressCane kuti apemphe thandizo. Matinga adayamikira PressCane chifukwa chopereka ma cone. Iye adati PressCane ikuthandiza apolisi ndi chitetezo cha pamsewu m'derali. Ma cone atsopanowa athandiza apolisi kuchita ntchito yawo mosamala kwambiri. Oyendetsa magalimoto adzaona apolisi bwino kwambiri pamsewu wotanganidwa wa Blantyre-Chikwawa.

en.title: Malawi faces more blackouts as power plants break down
en.body: Malawi will have less electricity for many weeks. The power company Escom said there is now 42 megawatts less power than needed. During evening hours, the shortfall grows to 83 megawatts. Right now, Malawi can make 347 megawatts but people need 430 megawatts.
en.body_more:
Megawatts are units that measure how much electricity is made. Escom says the problem will stay bad until broken power plants work again. Nkula A will turn on fully by mid-September. Nkula B Unit 6 will work again by early October.

Nkula B Unit 6 broke on 7 August and lost 20 megawatts from the grid. The damage is very bad. Workers must take out broken parts and send them to South Africa to fix them. The broken plant also hurt a new solar power plant. The solar plant makes 10 megawatts. It cannot work well now because Nkula B is down. Nkula A has another problem. Parts inside it are worn out. This causes a loss of 11.1 megawatts. New parts will come by late August. Repairs should finish by mid-September.

Egenco makes the electricity. Their spokesperson Moses Gwaza said the company cannot make enough power for everyone. He said Malawi must build new power plants faster. Money must go to new generation projects, not just to giving electricity to new places. Right now, only about one in four people get electricity from the grid or other sources. The government wants four in five people to have electricity by 2030.

Malawi can make 564.2 megawatts total from all its power plants. Most power comes from water. Water power makes 401.8 megawatts. Diesel power makes 51.4 megawatts. Solar power makes 111 megawatts.

ny.title: Malawi ikuvutika ndi magetsi chifukwa cha kuwonongeka kwa magetsi
ny.body: Malawi idzakhala ndi magetsi ochepa kwa milungu ingapo. Kampani yamagetsi ya Escom yati tsopano pali magetsi ochepa a ma megawatts 42 kuposa momwe amafunikira. Madzulo, kusowa kwa magetsi kumakula kufika pa ma megawatts 83. Pakadali pano, Malawi ikhoza kupanga ma megawatts 347 koma anthu akufunika ma megawatts 430.
ny.body_more:
Ma Megawatt ndi mayunitsi omwe amayesa kuchuluka kwa magetsi omwe apangidwa. Escom ikunena kuti vutoli lidzakhalabe loipa mpaka magetsi osweka agwirenso ntchito. Nkula A idzayatsa kwathunthu pakati pa Seputembala. Nkula B Unit 6 idzagwiranso ntchito kumayambiriro kwa Okutobala.

Nkula B Unit 6 idasweka pa 7 Ogasiti ndipo idataya ma megawatt 20 kuchokera pa gridi. Kuwonongekako ndi koipa kwambiri. Ogwira ntchito ayenera kuchotsa zida zosweka ndikuzitumiza ku South Africa kuti akazikonze. Makina oswekawo adavulazanso makina atsopano amagetsi a dzuwa. Makina amagetsi a dzuwa amapanga ma megawatt 10. Sangagwire ntchito bwino tsopano chifukwa Nkula B yatsika. Nkula A ili ndi vuto lina. Zida mkati mwake zatha. Izi zimapangitsa kutayika kwa ma megawatt 11.1. Zida zatsopano zidzabwera kumapeto kwa Ogasiti. Kukonza kuyenera kutha pakati pa Seputembala.

Egenco imapanga magetsi. Mneneri wawo Moses Gwaza adati kampaniyo singathe kupanga magetsi okwanira kwa aliyense. Anati Malawi iyenera kumanga magetsi atsopano mwachangu. Ndalama ziyenera kupita kumapulojekiti atsopano, osati kungopereka magetsi kumalo atsopano. Pakadali pano, munthu m'modzi mwa anayi okha ndi amene amapeza magetsi kuchokera ku gridi yamagetsi kapena magwero ena. Boma likufuna kuti anthu anayi mwa asanu akhale ndi magetsi pofika chaka cha 2030.

Malawi akhoza kupanga ma megawatts 564.2 kuchokera ku malo ake onse opangira magetsi. Mphamvu zambiri zimachokera ku madzi. Mphamvu yamadzi imapanga ma megawatts 401.8. Mphamvu ya dizilo imapanga ma megawatts 51.4. Mphamvu ya dzuwa imapanga ma megawatts 111.

en.title: Tobacco Commission to Pay Farmers Withheld Money
en.body: The Tobacco Commission will pay farmers their withheld money by Friday next week. The money was held from tobacco sold before August 14 this year. It was held to check that farmers did not sell more than their allowed amount. Telephorus Chigwenembe, the Commission's spokesperson, said payment plans are ready.
en.body_more:
Abiel Kalima Banda, who leads Tama Farmers Trust, said the payment is good news. He asked the Commission to pay the money within one week after farmers pick up their extra tobacco. This will help farmers use the money quickly. Tamani Nkhono Mvula, an agriculture analyst, said the move is fair and right.

Malawi's tobacco crop will be smaller than first thought. The new forecast is 155 million kilogrammes. The old forecast was 196 million kilogrammes. But buyers want 170 million kilogrammes. Because people thought there would be too much tobacco, buyers are paying less money than last year. This started when the selling season began.

AHL Tobacco Sales Limited said Malawi made $273.6 million (K479 billion) from tobacco sales so far this year. Farmers sold 137.7 million kilogrammes. The price was $1.99 for each kilogramme on average. But this is much less than last year. Money earned dropped from $464.9 million to $272.2 million. Farmers sold much less tobacco too. Last year at this time, they sold 182.4 million kilogrammes. This year they sold 136.5 million kilogrammes. AHL said less tobacco came into the selling floors each week. This is why earnings fell so much.

ny.title: Bungwe la Fodya Lilipira Alimi Omwe Anabisa Ndalama
ny.body: Bungwe la Tobacco Commission lipereka ndalama kwa alimi zomwe adasunga pofika Lachisanu sabata yamawa. Ndalamazo zidasungidwa kuchokera ku fodya yomwe idagulitsidwa isanafike pa 14 Ogasiti chaka chino. Zinachitika kuti awonetsetse kuti alimi sanagulitse zoposa zomwe adaloledwa. Telephorus Chigwenembe, wolankhulira bungweli, adati mapulani olipira ali okonzeka.
ny.body_more:
Abiel Kalima Banda, yemwe akutsogolera Tama Farmers Trust, anati malipirowa ndi nkhani yabwino. Anapempha bungwe la Commission kuti lilipire ndalamazo mkati mwa sabata imodzi alimi atatenga fodya wawo wowonjezera. Izi zithandiza alimi kugwiritsa ntchito ndalamazo mwachangu. Tamani Nkhono Mvula, katswiri wa zaulimi, anati izi ndi zolungama komanso zoyenera.

Zomera za fodya ku Malawi zidzakhala zochepa kuposa momwe zinalili poyamba. Zolosera zatsopano ndi makilogalamu 155 miliyoni. Zolosera zakale zinali makilogalamu 196 miliyoni. Koma ogula akufuna makilogalamu 170 miliyoni. Chifukwa anthu ankaganiza kuti padzakhala fodya wochuluka kwambiri, ogula akulipira ndalama zochepa kuposa chaka chatha. Izi zinayamba pamene nyengo yogulitsa inayamba.

AHL Tobacco Sales Limited inati Malawi idapeza $273.6 miliyoni (K479 biliyoni) kuchokera ku malonda a fodya mpaka pano chaka chino. Alimi adagulitsa makilogalamu 137.7 miliyoni. Mtengo wake unali $1.99 pa kilogalamu iliyonse pa avareji. Koma izi ndi zochepa kwambiri kuposa chaka chatha. Ndalama zomwe adapeza zatsika kuchoka pa $464.9 miliyoni kufika pa $272.2 miliyoni. Alimi adagulitsanso fodya wochepa kwambiri. Chaka chatha panthawiyi, adagulitsa makilogalamu 182.4 miliyoni. Chaka chino adagulitsa makilogalamu 136.5 miliyoni. AHL idati fodya wochepa ankagulitsidwa sabata iliyonse. Ichi ndichifukwa chake ndalama zomwe amapeza zidatsika kwambiri.

en.title: CHL Share Price Falls: Investors Told to Stay Patient
en.body: Continental Holdings plc (CHL) shares fell sharply after the stock market listing on August 10. The price dropped from K350 per share to K197.91 per share. This is just K2.91 above the starting price of K195. Market experts say investors should stay calm and wait for long-term growth.
en.body_more:
The fall happened after a fast rise. Some investors bought shares quickly to make fast money, but then sold them just as fast. Benedict Nkhoma, a stock market investor, said the price change does not mean CHL's businesses got worse. He said the price range between K195 and K200 is important and may help the share price settle down. "The price correction does not mean that CHL's underlying businesses have suddenly deteriorated," Nkhoma said.

Kondwani Makwakwa, an analyst at Stockbrokers Malawi Limited, said the first rise in price came from excitement about the new listing. He said the fall shows price discovery—the real price the market wants to pay. "Short-term investors who bought at the peak may have lost money," Makwakwa said. He added that future price changes will depend more on how well CHL makes money and grows its business.

Brian Kampanje, another analyst, said the fall was steep but not a surprise. The IPO had a 93 percent subscription rate, showing strong interest. But Kampanje said some investors panicked and sold at a loss. He told first-time investors to be patient. "The message for true investors looking for long-term growth is that the world is not ending tomorrow," Kampanje said. He also urged the government to look into why some people sold shares at a loss.

Purity Chitalo, chairperson of the Minority Shareholders Association of Listed Companies Central Region, warned investors not to make quick choices based on fear. She said if CHL stays strong, long-term investors will gain more than those chasing fast profits. The IPO sold 701.8 million shares for K135.4 billion. The public now owns 23.29 percent of CHL. Trans Africa Holdings owns 34.35 percent, Press Trust owns 17.8 percent, and the Employees Share Ownership Programme owns 9.98 percent.

ny.title: Mtengo wa Gawo la CHL Watsika: Ogulitsa Auzidwa Kuti Akhale Oleza Mtima
ny.body: Masheya a Continental Holdings plc (CHL) adatsika kwambiri pambuyo poti msika wamasheya walembedwa pa Ogasiti 10. Mtengo unatsika kuchoka pa K350 pagawo lililonse kufika pa K197.91 pagawo lililonse. Izi ndi K2.91 yokha kuposa mtengo woyambira wa K195. Akatswiri amsika amati osunga ndalama ayenera kukhala chete ndikudikirira kukula kwa nthawi yayitali.
ny.body_more:
Kugwa kumeneku kunachitika pambuyo poti mitengo yakwera mofulumira. Ena mwa omwe amaika ndalama adagula magawo mwachangu kuti apeze ndalama mwachangu, koma kenako adawagulitsa mwachangu momwemonso. Benedict Nkhoma, yemwe amaika ndalama pamsika wamasheya, adati kusintha kwa mitengo sikutanthauza kuti mabizinesi a CHL aipiraipira. Iye adati mitengo pakati pa K195 ndi K200 ndi yofunika ndipo ingathandize kuti mtengo wa magawo ukhale pansi. "Kukonza mitengo sikutanthauza kuti mabizinesi omwe ali pansi pa CHL aipiraipira mwadzidzidzi," adatero Nkhoma.

Kondwani Makwakwa, katswiri wa Stockbrokers Malawi Limited, adati kukwera koyamba kwa mtengo kudabwera chifukwa cha chisangalalo ndi mndandanda watsopano. Iye adati kutsikaku kukuwonetsa kupezeka kwa mitengo - mtengo weniweni womwe msika ukufuna kulipira. "Amalonda anthawi yochepa omwe adagula pamsika akhoza kutaya ndalama," adatero Makwakwa. Anawonjezera kuti kusintha kwa mitengo mtsogolo kudzadalira kwambiri momwe CHL imapezera ndalama ndikukulitsa bizinesi yake.

Brian Kampanje, katswiri wina, adati kutsikaku kunali kwakukulu koma sikudabwitsa. IPO inali ndi chiwongola dzanja cha 93 peresenti cholembetsa, kusonyeza chidwi chachikulu. Koma Kampanje anati ena mwa omwe amaika ndalama zawo m'mabanki awo anachita mantha ndipo anagulitsa mopanda phindu. Anauza omwe amaika ndalama koyamba kuti akhale oleza mtima. "Uthenga kwa omwe amaika ndalama zenizeni omwe akufuna kukula kwa nthawi yayitali ndi wakuti dziko silikutha mawa," adatero Kampanje. Analimbikitsanso boma kuti lifufuze chifukwa chake anthu ena amagulitsa magawo mopanda phindu.

Purity Chitalo, wapampando wa Minority Shareholders Association of Listed Companies Central Region, anachenjeza oika ndalama kuti asapange zisankho mwachangu chifukwa cha mantha. Anati ngati CHL ikhalabe yolimba, oika ndalama nthawi yayitali adzapeza zambiri kuposa omwe akufunafuna phindu mwachangu. IPO idagulitsa magawo 701.8 miliyoni pa K135.4 biliyoni. Anthu tsopano ali ndi 23.29 peresenti ya CHL. Trans Africa Holdings ili ndi 34.35 peresenti, Press Trust ili ndi 17.8 peresenti, ndipo Employees Share Ownership Programme ili ndi 9.98 peresenti.

en.title: Bank happy with Scorchers watch parties at Wafcon
en.body: National Bank of Malawi held more than 12 watch parties. People came to watch the Scorchers play at the Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. The bank says many customers and Malawians came. The Scorchers played their first time at this big tournament.
en.body_more:
Daniel Jere is the Chief Finance Officer of NBM. He said the watch parties were a success. "The idea was to let customers come together," Jere said. "They watched their team in a fun place. The watch parties went better than we hoped. This also helped us show that NBM loves football."

Christine Mathotho watched a match at Moneymen in Blantyre. She said thank you to the bank. "Everybody came to watch," she said. "The bank brought Malawians together." Eliza Nyaka watched at Woodlands in Lilongwe. She said the bank cares about women's football. The first watch party was at Woodlands. A big crowd came to watch the Scorchers play Nigeria. Malawi won 3-2.

More people wanted to watch after that win. They met at AJ's Lounge in Blantyre. The Scorchers beat Egypt 3-1 in the next game. Then Malawi played Zambia and lost 2-1. But Malawi went to the semi-finals anyway. This made some fans sad and some happy.

More watch parties opened in other towns. The bank made watch parties at Linde Lounge in Mzuzu and Café 92 in Lilongwe. For the last games, NBM held watch parties in four places. These were Linde Lounge in Mzuzu, Aero Lounge in Lilongwe, Moneymen Club in Blantyre, and Stay in Mulunguzi Cottage in Zomba. NBM gave money to help the Scorchers last year. The bank will keep helping women's football.

ny.title: Bank akusangalala ndi maphwando a Scorchers ku Wafcon
ny.body: Banki Yadziko Lonse ya Malawi inachita maphwando owonera oposa 12. Anthu anabwera kudzaonera Scorchers ikusewera pa Women's Africa Cup of Nations ku Morocco. Bankiyo ikunena kuti makasitomala ambiri ndi anthu aku Malawi anabwera. Scorchers adasewera koyamba pa mpikisano waukuluwu.
ny.body_more:
Daniel Jere ndi Chief Finance Officer wa NBM. Iye anati maphwando owonera apambana. "Lingaliro linali loti makasitomala asonkhane," adatero Jere. "Adayang'anira timu yawo pamalo osangalatsa. Maphwando owonera adatha bwino kuposa momwe tinkayembekezera. Izi zidatithandizanso kuwonetsa kuti NBM imakonda mpira."

Christine Mathotho adawonera masewera ku Moneymen ku Blantyre. Adati zikomo ku banki. "Aliyense adabwera kudzawonera," adatero. "Bankiyo idasonkhanitsa anthu aku Malawi." Eliza Nyaka adawonera ku Woodlands ku Lilongwe. Adati bankiyo imasamala za mpira wa azimayi. Phwando loyamba lowonera linali ku Woodlands. Khamu lalikulu linabwera kudzawonera Scorchers ikusewera ndi Nigeria. Malawi idapambana 3-2.

Anthu ambiri amafuna kuwonera atapambana. Adakumana ku AJ's Lounge ku Blantyre. Scorchers adagonjetsa Egypt 3-1 pamasewera otsatira. Kenako Malawi idasewera ndi Zambia ndipo idataya 2-1. Koma Malawi idapita ku semi-finals. Izi zidapangitsa mafani ena kukhala achisoni ndipo ena adasangalala.

Maphwando owonera ambiri adatsegulidwa m'matauni ena. Bankiyi idapanga maphwando a mawotchi ku Linde Lounge ku Mzuzu ndi Café 92 ku Lilongwe. Pamasewera omaliza, NBM idachita maphwando a mawotchi m'malo anayi. Awa anali Linde Lounge ku Mzuzu, Aero Lounge ku Lilongwe, Moneymen Club ku Blantyre, ndi Stay ku Mulunguzi Cottage ku Zomba. NBM idapereka ndalama zothandizira Scorchers chaka chatha. Bankiyi ipitiliza kuthandiza mpira wa azimayi.

en.title: Court to rule on activist Namiwa's bail on Friday
en.body: Activist Sylvester Namiwa will learn if he can leave prison on Friday. The Lilongwe High Court will rule on his bail at 10:00 a.m. on August 21. Namiwa was arrested three weeks ago. He faces charges of treason and publishing false news. He has been held at Maula Prison in Lilongwe.
en.body_more:
Namiwa is the head of the Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI). His lawyer asked the court to let him go free on bail while his case continues. A spokesperson for CDEDI, Promise Thomu, said the ruling will come on Friday morning.

The State did not oppose bail. The only question was about the bail bond amount of MWK2 million and who would be his sureties. A sureties is a person who promises to help ensure someone comes to court. Judge Mzondi Mvula heard the bail case on August 13 but did not give a ruling that day. He said he would email both sides when he was ready to decide.

Namiwa's health got worse while in prison. He fell ill and was taken to ABC Clinic. After he was released from hospital, he was taken straight back to Maula Prison. A group called the Human Rights Defenders Coalition said this was wrong. They said keeping Namiwa in prison when the State did not oppose bail was unfair. They said it broke rules about fair and fast trials.

For Namiwa's family and supporters, Friday's ruling is very important. It could mean he walks free or stays in prison. His case has drawn attention because of his health and how long he has waited for the court's decision.

ny.title: Khothi lipereka chigamulo pa belo la Namiwa Lachisanu
ny.body: Womenyera ufulu wa anthu Sylvester Namiwa adzadziwa ngati angatuluke m'ndende Lachisanu. Khothi Lalikulu la Lilongwe lidzapereka chigamulo pa belo yake nthawi ya 10:00 koloko m'mawa pa Ogasiti 21. Namiwa adamangidwa milungu itatu yapitayo. Akukumana ndi milandu yokhudza kuukira boma komanso kufalitsa nkhani zabodza. Wakhala akusungidwa ku ndende ya Maula ku Lilongwe.
ny.body_more:
Namiwa ndi mtsogoleri wa Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives (CDEDI). Loya wake adapempha khothi kuti limulole kuti atuluke ali ndi belo pomwe mlandu wake ukupitirira. Wolankhulira CDEDI, Promise Thomu, adati chigamulochi chidzaperekedwa Lachisanu m'mawa.

Boma silinatsutse belo. Funso lokhalo linali lokhudza ndalama zolipirira belo za MWK2 miliyoni komanso omwe angakhale otsimikiza kuti apereke belo. Wotsimikizira ndi munthu amene akulonjeza kuthandiza kuti wina abwere kukhothi. Woweruza Mzondi Mvula adamva mlandu wa belo pa Ogasiti 13 koma sanapereke chigamulo tsiku lomwelo. Anati adzatumiza imelo kwa onse awiri akakonzeka kusankha.

Thanzi la Namiwa linaipiraipira ali m'ndende. Anadwala ndipo anatengedwera ku ABC Clinic. Atatulutsidwa kuchipatala, anatengedwera kundende ya Maula.
