In the quarter-finals, Malawi beat Ghana 2-1. In the semi-final, they beat Algeria. But Cameroon beat them 3-0 in the final on Sunday.

Despite losing the final, the Scorchers achieved a big thing. This was their first time at WAFCON, and they reached the final. They also qualified for the World Cup, which will happen in Brazil in 2027. The team's success has made many people in Malawi proud. The Scorchers will touch down in Malawi on Wednesday to the military parade and celebrations.

ny.title: Asilikali a ku Malawi akukonzekera kubwereranso ku dziko lawo
ny.body: Dziko la Malawi lidzalandira timu ya mpira wa azimayi, a Scorchers, ndi gulu lankhondo Lachitatu. Gululi linayenerera mpikisano wa FIFA Women's World Cup wa 2027 ku Brazil ndipo linakhala lachiwiri pa mpikisano wa Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON). Unduna wa Masewera, Achinyamata ndi Chikhalidwe ndi Lilongwe City Council akukonzekera chikondwererochi.
ny.body_more:
Macmillan Mwale, mkulu wa maubwenzi a anthu mu undunawu, anati timuyi ikuyenera kulandiridwa bwino kwambiri. "Akwanitsa kulowa nawo mpikisano wa Women's World Cup womwe udzachitike ku Brazil chaka chamawa ndipo akwanitsa kufika pa nambala 2 mu WAFCON, kotero akuyenera kulandiridwa bwino," adatero Mwale. Chochitikachi chidzachitikira ku Lilongwe mothandizidwa ndi NBM, omwe ndi othandizira kwambiri timuyi, Malawi Police Service, ndi Malawi Defence Force.

Scorchers adasewera masewera asanu ndi limodzi ku WAFCON. Adapambana masewera anayi ndipo adataya awiri. Gululi lidagonjetsa Nigeria 3-2 pamasewera awo oyamba. Kenako adagonjetsa Egypt 3-1. Zambia idawagonjetsa 2-1 pagulu. Mu kotala-mapeto, Malawi idagonjetsa Ghana 2-1. Mu semi-final, adagonjetsa Algeria. Koma Cameroon idawagonjetsa 3-0 pa komaliza Lamlungu.

Ngakhale adataya komaliza, Scorchers adachita bwino kwambiri. Iyi inali nthawi yawo yoyamba ku WAFCON, ndipo adafika pa komaliza. Iwonso adayenerera mpikisano wa World Cup, womwe udzachitike ku Brazil mu 2027. Kupambana kwa timuyi kwapangitsa anthu ambiri ku Malawi kunyada. A Scorchers adzafika ku Malawi Lachitatu ku mwambo wa asilikali ndi zikondwerero.

en.title: Malawi inflation falls but food prices rise fast
en.body: Malawi's yearly inflation went down to 20.8 per cent in July. It was 21.1 per cent in June. The National Statistical Office told people this on August 15. Food inflation fell but prices went up fast each month.
en.body_more:
Food prices slowed from 14.7 per cent in June to 14.3 per cent in July. But non-food inflation went up a little. It rose from 32.1 per cent to 32.2 per cent. This means things like clothes and fuel got more costly.

Month by month, prices jumped much more. They went up 2.0 per cent in July. In June they went up only 0.1 per cent. Food prices led this jump. They went up 2.9 per cent in July. In June they had gone down 0.3 per cent. Non-food prices stayed flat at 0.7 per cent each month.

Rural areas felt the pain more. Food prices there went up 3.0 per cent each month. Non-food prices went up 2.0 per cent. In towns, food went up 2.3 per cent and non-food went up 0.3 per cent. Rural monthly inflation was 2.6 per cent. Town monthly inflation was 1.4 per cent.

Experts say prices are still hard for poor families. Food costs are worse in villages. The number keeps changing. No one knows if prices will keep going up or slow down in the next months.

ny.title: Kukwera kwa mitengo ya chakudya ku Malawi kwatsika koma mitengo ya chakudya yakwera mofulumira
ny.body: Kukwera kwa mitengo kwa dziko la Malawi kwatsika kufika pa 20.8 peresenti mu Julayi. Kunali 21.1 peresenti mu Juni. Ofesi ya National Statistical Office idauza anthu izi pa Ogasiti 15. Kukwera kwa mitengo kwa chakudya kunatsika koma mitengo inakwera mofulumira mwezi uliwonse.
ny.body_more:
Mitengo ya chakudya inatsika kuchoka pa 14.7 peresenti mu June kufika pa 14.3 peresenti mu July. Koma kukwera kwa mitengo ya chakudya osati chakudya kunakwera pang'ono. Kunakwera kuchoka pa 32.1 peresenti kufika pa 32.2 peresenti. Izi zikutanthauza kuti zinthu monga zovala ndi mafuta zinakwera kwambiri.

Mwezi uliwonse, mitengo inakwera kwambiri. Inakwera ndi 2.0 peresenti mu July. Mu June inakwera ndi 0.1 peresenti yokha. Mitengo ya chakudya inatsogolera kukweraku. Inakwera ndi 2.9 peresenti mu July. Mu June inatsika ndi 0.3 peresenti. Mitengo ya chakudya osati chakudya inakhalabe yosasinthasintha pa 0.7 peresenti mwezi uliwonse.

Malo akumidzi anamva ululu kwambiri. Mitengo ya chakudya kumeneko inakwera ndi 3.0 peresenti mwezi uliwonse. Mitengo ya chakudya osati chakudya inakwera ndi 2.0 peresenti. M'matauni, chakudya chinakwera ndi 2.3 peresenti ndipo chakudya chosadya chinakwera ndi 0.3 peresenti. Kukwera kwa mitengo ya chakudya pamwezi kumidzi kunali 2.6 peresenti. Kukwera kwa mitengo ya chakudya pamwezi ku tawuni kunali 1.4 peresenti.

Akatswiri amati mitengo ikadali yovuta kwa mabanja osauka. Mitengo ya chakudya yakwera kwambiri m'midzi. Chiwerengerochi chikupitirirabe kusintha. Palibe amene akudziwa ngati mitengo ipitirira kukwera kapena kuchepa m'miyezi ikubwerayi.

en.title: Activist Namiwa taken to hospital, then back to jail
en.body: Sylvester Namiwa, the head of the Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives, was taken to ABC Hospital in Lilongwe on Sunday. He was feeling unwell. After a check-up, he was taken back to prison. The High Court has not yet ruled on his bail application.
en.body_more:
Namiwa faces treason charges and charges of publishing news likely to cause public alarm. He was arrested on 30 July 2026. He has been in custody ever since.

Namiwa's lawyer, Gift Mwenye, asked the court for bail. The State proposed bail conditions. These included a bond of K2 million. The State also asked for two sureties bonded at K3 million each in non-cash form. Namiwa must give up his travel papers. He must report to police every two weeks on Fridays.

Mwenye told the court that K2 million was too much money. Namiwa does human rights work. He does this work for no pay. He does not have a regular income. The State lawyer, Tapiwa Msimuko, said the State did not object to bail. She said police investigations were finished. But she asked the court to keep the bail conditions if Namiwa is released.

Judge Mzonde Mvula said the court must decide. He said he needed more time to think about both sides' arguments. The High Court must rule on bail. Earlier, Namiwa tried to get bail at the Lilongwe Chief Resident Magistrate Court. That court said no. Only the High Court can decide bail for treason charges. Namiwa stays in prison while he waits for the judge's decision.

ny.title: Namiwa womenyera ufulu wa anthu watengedwa kupita kuchipatala, kenako kubwerera kundende
ny.body: Sylvester Namiwa, mkulu wa Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives, adatengedwera ku chipatala cha ABC ku Lilongwe Lamlungu. Anali kumva kudwala. Atapimidwa, adabwereranso kundende. Khothi Lalikulu silinapereke chigamulo pa pempho lake la belo.
ny.body_more:
Namiwa akukumana ndi milandu yokhudza kuukira boma komanso milandu yofalitsa nkhani zomwe zingachititse mantha anthu. Anamangidwa pa 30 Julayi 2026. Kuyambira nthawi imeneyo wakhala m'ndende.

Loya wa Namiwa, Gift Mwenye, adapempha khoti kuti limupatse belo. Boma lidapereka zikhalidwe za belo. Izi zikuphatikizapo bond ya K2 miliyoni. Boma lidapemphanso ma sureties awiri omwe ali ndi bond ya K3 miliyoni aliyense osati ndalama. Namiwa ayenera kusiya mapepala ake oyendera. Ayenera kukaonekera ku polisi milungu iwiri iliyonse Lachisanu.

Menye adauza khoti kuti K2 miliyoni ndi ndalama zambiri. Namiwa amagwira ntchito yokhudza ufulu wa anthu. Amagwira ntchito imeneyi popanda malipiro. Alibe ndalama zokhazikika. Loya wa boma, Tapiwa Msimuko, adati Boma silinatsutse belo. Iye adati kafukufuku wa apolisi watha. Koma adapempha khoti kuti lisunge zikhalidwe za belo ngati Namiwa atulutsidwa.

Woweruza Mzonde Mvula adati khoti liyenera kusankha. Iye adati amafunikira nthawi yochulukirapo kuti aganizire za mfundo za mbali zonse ziwiri. Khoti Lalikulu liyenera kupereka chigamulo pa belo. Poyamba, Namiwa anayesa kupeza belo ku Khoti Lalikulu la Magistrate ku Lilongwe. Khotilo linati ayi. Khoti Lalikulu lokha ndi lomwe lingagamule belo pa milandu yokhudza kuukira boma. Namiwa akukhala m'ndende pamene akuyembekezera chigamulo cha woweruza.

en.title: Malawi Scorchers lose final to Cameroon at WAFCON
en.body: Malawi's Scorchers lost 3-0 to Cameroon in the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final on Sunday in Rabat, Morocco. The match was played at Prince Moulay El Hassan Stadium. Marie Ngah scored twice for Cameroon. Naomi Eto scored once. This was Malawi's first time in a WAFCON final.
en.body_more:
The Scorchers reached the final in their first appearance at the continental tournament. Before the final, Malawi beat defending champions Nigeria 3-2. They then defeated Egypt 3-1. Malawi lost 2-1 to Zambia but finished top of their group with six points. In the quarter-finals, Malawi beat Ghana 2-1. In the semi-finals, Malawi defeated Algeria 3-1.

Captain Tabitha Chawinga scored twice against Algeria. Her sister Temwa Chawinga also scored. In five matches before the final, Malawi scored 13 goals. Temwa scored five goals. Tabitha scored four. Rose Kabzere scored two. Faith Chinzimu scored one. However, Malawi conceded seven goals in those five matches. Kabzere missed the final because she was suspended after getting a red card in the semi-final.

Cameroon reached the final by a different path. They defeated Mali 2-1, beat Ghana 1-0, and drew 1-1 with Cape Verde. In the quarter-finals, Cameroon beat Nigeria 1-0. In the semi-final, Cameroon played Morocco. The match ended 0-0. Cameroon won the penalty shoot-out 3-1. Cameroon scored five goals in the tournament and conceded two. Goalkeeper Michaely Bihina made nine saves against Nigeria.

Malawi coach Lovemore Fazili said his team was ready. He said the players wanted to win. Cameroon coach Valentine Nguele said her team was prepared for Malawi's attack. Despite the loss, Malawi qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil by reaching the WAFCON semi-finals. This was Malawi's first World Cup qualification.

ny.title: Malawi Scorchers yataya timu yomaliza ndi Cameroon ku WAFCON
ny.body: Masewerowa adachitikira ku Prince Moulay El Hassan Stadium ku Malawi. Marie Ngah adagoletsa zigoli ziwiri ku Cameroon. Naomi Eto adagoletsa kamodzi. Uwu unali nthawi yoyamba ku Malawi mu mpikisano wa WAFCON.
ny.body_more:
A Scorchers adafika pa fainali koyamba pa mpikisano wa continental. Asanafike fainali, Malawi idagonjetsa Nigeria 3-2 omwe adateteza. Kenako adagonjetsa Egypt 3-1. Malawi idagonjetsedwa ndi Zambia 2-1 koma idamaliza pamwamba pa gulu lawo ndi mapointi asanu ndi limodzi. Mu kotala fainali, Malawi idagonjetsa Ghana 2-1. Mu semi-finals, Malawi idagonjetsa Algeria 3-1.

Captain Tabitha Chawinga adagoletsa zigoli ziwiri motsutsana ndi Algeria. Mlongo wake Temwa Chawinga nayenso adagoletsa zigoli. Mu masewera asanu asanafike fainali, Malawi idagoletsa zigoli 13. Temwa adagoletsa zigoli zisanu. Tabitha adagoletsa zigoli zinayi. Rose Kabzere adagoletsa zigoli ziwiri. Faith Chinzimu adagoletsa chimodzi. Komabe, Malawi idagoletsa zigoli zisanu ndi ziwiri mumasewera asanu amenewo. Kabzere adaphonya fainali chifukwa adayimitsidwa atalandira khadi lofiira mu semi-finals.

Cameroon idafika fainali ndi njira ina. Adagonjetsa Mali 2-1, adagonjetsa Ghana 1-0, ndikufanana 1-1 ndi Cape Verde. Mu kotala fainali, Cameroon idagonjetsa Nigeria 1-0. Mu semi-final, Cameroon idasewera ndi Morocco. Masewerowa adathera 0-0. Cameroon idapambana penalty 3-1. Cameroon idagoletsa zigoli zisanu mu mpikisanowu ndipo idagoletsa ziwiri. Woyang'anira zigoli Michaely Bihina adapulumutsa zigoli zisanu ndi zinayi motsutsana ndi Nigeria.

Mphunzitsi wa Malawi Lovemore Fazili adati timu yake yakonzeka. Iye adati osewerawo akufuna kupambana. Mphunzitsi wa Cameroon Valentine Nguele adati timu yake yakonzeka kuukira Malawi. Ngakhale kuti adagonja, Malawi idayenerera kulowa mu 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup ku Brazil pofika mu semi-final ya WAFCON. Iyi inali nthawi yoyamba yoyenerera dziko la Malawi kukhala mu World Cup.

en.title: School gives girl second chance after exam struggles
en.body: Maranatha Academy will take Duwana Muhamad. She is 16 years old. She sat her Primary School Leaving Certificate exams alone. She was the only girl in her class at Mangale Primary School in Mangochi. She did not pass the exams. But the school says she can still come.
en.body_more:
Duwana sat the exams with seven boys. All her female classmates had left school before the exams. Early marriage, teenage pregnancy, and poverty made girls leave school. Duwana stayed and took the test by herself.

Ernest Kaonga is the Managing Director of Maranatha Academy Secondary Schools. He said the school cannot turn away from her. "We cannot simply look away," Kaonga said. He said Duwana faces many challenges. Being the only girl in a class of boys is very hard. Kaonga said that failing an exam does not end a child's future. Duwana deserves another chance, he said.

Duwana will go to Maranatha Girls Academy. The school will give her free schooling. She will get academic support and counselling. She will sleep at the school. The academy will also give her K500,000 every term for pocket money. This money helps her buy things she needs.

Kaonga said Duwana's story is important. It shows the big problems girls face in Mangochi. Many girls have to leave school because of early marriage. Some get pregnant. Some are too poor. Some live too far away. Kaonga hopes Duwana's story will help change communities. He wants other girls to stay in school. He believes that with help, Duwana can become a role model. She can show other girls that they can finish their schooling too.

ny.title: Sukulu yapatsa atsikana mwayi wachiwiri pambuyo pa zovuta za mayeso
ny.body: Maranatha Academy itenga Duwana Muhamad. Ali ndi zaka 16. Analemba yekha mayeso ake a Primary Leaving Certificate. Iye anali mtsikana yekhayo mkalasi mwake ku Mangale Primary School ku Mangochi. Sanapambane mayesowo. Koma sukuluyo ikunena kuti akhoza kubwera.
ny.body_more:
Duwana adalemba mayeso ndi anyamata asanu ndi awiri. Atsikana onse omwe anali nawo m'kalasi adasiya sukulu mayeso asanayambe. Kukwatiwa ali aang'ono, kutenga mimba zachinyamata, ndi umphawi zidapangitsa atsikana kusiya sukulu. Duwana adakhalabe ndipo adalemba mayeso yekha.

Ernest Kaonga ndi Mtsogoleri Wamkulu wa Masukulu a Sekondale a Maranatha Academy. Anati sukuluyo singamusiye. "Sitingangoyang'ana kwina," adatero Kaonga. Anati Duwana akukumana ndi mavuto ambiri. Kukhala mtsikana yekhayo m'kalasi la anyamata n'kovuta kwambiri. Kaonga adati kulephera mayeso sikuthetsa tsogolo la mwana. Duwana akuyenera mwayi wina, adatero.

Duwana adzapita ku Maranatha Girls Academy. Sukuluyo idzamupatsa maphunziro aulere. Adzalandira chithandizo chamaphunziro ndi upangiri. Adzagona kusukulu. Sukuluyi idzamupatsanso K500,000 semesita iliyonse kuti apeze ndalama. Ndalamazi zimamuthandiza kugula zinthu zomwe akufuna.

Kaonga adati nkhani ya Duwana ndi yofunika. Ikuwonetsa mavuto akuluakulu omwe atsikana amakumana nawo ku Mangochi. Atsikana ambiri amasiya sukulu chifukwa cha ukwati wawo wachinyamata. Ena amatenga mimba. Ena ndi osauka kwambiri. Ena amakhala kutali kwambiri. Kaonga akuyembekeza kuti nkhani ya Duwana ithandiza kusintha madera. Akufuna kuti atsikana ena apitirize sukulu. Akukhulupirira kuti akathandizidwa, Duwana akhoza kukhala chitsanzo chabwino. Angasonyeze atsikana ena kuti nawonso akhoza kumaliza sukulu yawo.

en.title: First Lady joins church women prayers in Lilongwe
en.body: Malawi's First Lady Gertrude Mutharika joined more than 2,000 women on Sunday at Lingadzi CCAP church in Lilongwe. They gathered for the annual Women's Guild Conference. The conference started on Friday and ended on Sunday. The event brought women together from many CCAP churches under the Mpando Presbytery.
en.body_more:
The First Lady spoke to the women about peace. She said Malawians must seek peace with God and with each other. She told the women that peace helps a country grow and change. She said people must choose peace even when life is hard.

The First Lady warned people not to use words and actions that cause hate and division. She asked all Malawians to forgive each other, show love, and work together as one. She said a peaceful country can build a strong future. Peace is a foundation for growth, she told the women.

Yvonne M'mangitsa, the chairlady of Lingadzi CCAP Women's Guild, said the guild was happy to have the First Lady visit. M'mangitsa praised the First Lady for her humility and for coming to the conference. The theme of this year's conference was "Seek Peace and Pursue It." This message spoke to the hearts of all the women who came. The conference was one of the biggest church gatherings for women this year in Malawi.

ny.title: Mayi Woyamba alowa nawo mapemphero a akazi a tchalitchi ku Lilongwe
ny.body: Mayi woyamba wa dziko la Malawi, Gertrude Mutharika, adalowa nawo azimayi oposa 2,000 Lamlungu ku tchalitchi cha Lingadzi CCAP ku Lilongwe. Anasonkhana ku Msonkhano wapachaka wa Women's Guild. Msonkhanowu unayamba Lachisanu ndipo unatha Lamlungu. Chochitikachi chinasonkhanitsa azimayi ochokera m'matchalitchi ambiri a CCAP omwe ali pansi pa Mpando Presbytery.
ny.body_more:
Mayi Woyamba analankhula ndi azimayiwo za mtendere. Anati anthu aku Malawi ayenera kufunafuna mtendere ndi Mulungu komanso wina ndi mnzake. Anauza akaziwo kuti mtendere umathandiza dziko kukula ndi kusintha. Anati anthu ayenera kusankha mtendere ngakhale moyo utakhala wovuta.

Mayi Woyamba anachenjeza anthu kuti asagwiritse ntchito mawu ndi zochita zomwe zimayambitsa chidani ndi magawano. Anapempha anthu onse aku Malawi kuti akhululukire wina ndi mnzake, asonyeze chikondi, ndikugwira ntchito limodzi ngati amodzi. Anati dziko lamtendere lingathe kumanga tsogolo lolimba. Mtendere ndi maziko a kukula, anatero azimayiwo.

Yvonne M'mangitsa, wapampando wa Lingadzi CCAP Women's Guild, anati gululi linali losangalala kuti Mayi Woyamba abwera kudzacheza. M'mangitsa anayamikira Mayi Woyamba chifukwa cha kudzichepetsa kwake komanso kubwera ku msonkhanowo. Mutu wa msonkhano wa chaka chino unali "Fufuzani Mtendere ndi Kuutsatira." Uthengawu unakhudza mitima ya akazi onse omwe anabwera. Msonkhanowu unali umodzi mwa misonkhano yayikulu kwambiri ya tchalitchi cha akazi chaka chino ku Malawi.

en.title: Malawi women's football reaches world cup after 25 years
en.body: Malawi's women's football team qualified for the 2026 FIFA Women's World Cup for the first time. The team beat Angola 2-0 in Lilongwe. This success follows years of hard work from pioneers who kept women's football alive when few people cared about the game.
en.body_more:
Women's football started in Malawi in late 1998. The first match was in Blantyre with eleven teams. A young player named Maggie Chombo became famous in 1996. She played in a social football match before a Cosafa Cup game at Kamuzu Stadium. People loved watching her play.

The Malawi team, called the Scorchers, made their first international match on 20 April 2002. They lost 8-0 to Zambia. For many years, the team was not strong. In 2004, they lost 9-0 in the Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. But the team did not stop.

Two sisters changed Malawi's football. Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga were discovered playing football in their village in Rumphi. They moved to Lilongwe to play. Tabitha became the first Malawi woman to play in Europe in 2014. She scored 39 goals in 14 matches in Sweden. Temwa followed her to Europe and later played in the United States. More players went to play in other countries.

In 2023, the Scorchers won the Cosafa Women's Championship. Temwa scored nine goals and won Player of the Tournament. The team beat Seychelles 17-0. Then in 2025, Malawi beat Angola to qualify for the 2026 Africa Cup of Nations. The first game in Luanda was 0-0. Malawi won the second game 2-0 in Lilongwe. Many players now play for teams in France, Sweden, Egypt, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia.

ny.title: Mpira wa azimayi ku Malawi wafika pa chikho cha dziko lonse patatha zaka 25
ny.body: Gulu la mpira wa azimayi la Malawi linayenerera mpikisano wa FIFA Women's World Cup wa 2026 koyamba. Gululi linagonjetsa Angola 2-0 ku Lilongwe. Kupambana kumeneku kukutsatira zaka zambiri za ntchito yolimba kuchokera kwa apainiya omwe adasunga mpira wa akazi ulipo pomwe anthu ochepa anali kusamala za masewerawa.
ny.body_more:
Mpira wa azimayi unayamba ku Malawi kumapeto kwa chaka cha 1998. Masewera oyamba anali ku Blantyre ndi magulu khumi ndi limodzi. Wosewera wachinyamata dzina lake Maggie Chombo adatchuka mu 1996. Anasewera masewera a mpira wa anthu asanayambe masewera a Cosafa Cup ku Kamuzu Stadium. Anthu ankakonda kumuonera akusewera.

Timu ya Malawi, yotchedwa Scorchers, idasewera masewera awo oyamba apadziko lonse lapansi pa 20 Epulo 2002. Adagonja 8-0 ndi Zambia. Kwa zaka zambiri, timuyi sinali yamphamvu. Mu 2004, adagonja 9-0 pamasewera oyenerera a Africa Cup of Nations. Koma timuyi sinasiye.

Alongo awiri adasintha mpira wa Malawi. Tabitha ndi Temwa Chawinga adapezeka akusewera mpira kumudzi kwawo ku Rumphi. Anasamukira ku Lilongwe kukasewera. Tabitha adakhala mkazi woyamba wa ku Malawi kusewera ku Europe mu 2014. Adagoletsa zigoli 39 pamasewera 14 ku Sweden. Temwa adamutsatira kupita ku Europe ndipo pambuyo pake adasewera ku United States. Osewera ambiri adapita kukasewera kumayiko ena.

Mu 2023, Scorchers adapambana mpikisano wa Cosafa Women's Championship. Temwa adagoletsa zigoli zisanu ndi zinayi ndipo adapambana mpikisano wa Player of the Tournament. Gululi lidagonjetsa Seychelles 17-0. Kenako mu 2025, Malawi idagonjetsa Angola kuti iyenerere mpikisano wa Africa Cup of Nations wa 2026. Masewera oyamba ku Luanda anali 0-0. Malawi idapambana masewera achiwiri 2-0 ku Lilongwe. Osewera ambiri tsopano akusewera m'magulu aku France, Sweden, Egypt, Democratic Republic of Congo ndi Zambia.

en.title: Chihana arrives in South Africa for SADC summit
en.body: Malawi's Second Vice President Enock Kamzingeni Chihana landed in Durban, South Africa on Saturday evening. He will represent Malawi at two big regional meetings. Chihana was met at the airport by Malawi's High Commissioner Stella Ndau and Foreign Affairs Minister George Chaponda. He received a briefing about the summit schedule right away.
en.body_more:
The SADC Organ Troika Summit and the 46th SADC Ordinary Summit of Heads of State and Government will happen on Sunday and Monday. SADC is the Southern African Development Community. It is a group of countries in the region that work together. Malawi now chairs the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security. This means Malawi leads talks on these topics. Malawi took this role from Tanzania. Eswatini will take the role after Malawi.

The wider SADC summit is led by South Africa. The meetings will discuss many big topics. Leaders want to grow manufacturing and trade across the region. They want to build better roads, power lines and water systems. They will talk about farming and minerals. Southern Africa has many minerals that other countries need.

After the Sunday meetings end, Chihana will go to a state banquet. South African President Cyril Ramaphosa will host it. The summit theme is "Resilient, Sustainable and Inclusive Industrialisation through Infrastructure Development, Agricultural and Critical Minerals Transformation in Pursuit of a Just World." This means leaders want to help Southern Africa grow in a fair way. They want all people to benefit from the region's resources.

Chihana's presence shows Malawi plays an important role in regional peace and security talks. The meetings will help SADC member states work better together on politics, money and safety issues.

ny.title: Chihana wafika ku South Africa ku msonkhano wa SADC
ny.body: Wachiwiri kwa Purezidenti wa Malawi, Enock Kamzingeni Chihana, wafika ku Durban, South Africa Loweruka madzulo. Iye adzayimira Malawi pa misonkhano ikuluikulu iwiri yachigawo. Chihana adakumana pa eyapoti ndi Kazembe Wamkulu wa Malawi, Stella Ndau, ndi Nduna Yoona za Zakunja, George Chaponda. Adalandira chidziwitso chokhudza nthawi ya msonkhano nthawi yomweyo.
ny.body_more:
Msonkhano wa SADC Organ Troika ndi Msonkhano Wachibadwidwe wa Atsogoleri a Maboma ndi Maboma wa 46th SADC udzachitika Lamlungu ndi Lolemba. SADC ndi Southern African Development Community. Ndi gulu la mayiko m'chigawochi omwe amagwira ntchito limodzi. Malawi tsopano ndi mtsogoleri wa SADC Organ on Politics, Defense and Security. Izi zikutanthauza kuti Malawi ikutsogolera zokambirana pa mitu iyi. Malawi idatenga udindowu kuchokera ku Tanzania. Eswatini idzatenga udindowu pambuyo pa Malawi.

Msonkhano waukulu wa SADC ukutsogoleredwa ndi South Africa. Misonkhanoyi idzakambirana mitu yayikulu yambiri. Atsogoleri akufuna kukulitsa kupanga ndi malonda m'chigawo chonsecho. Akufuna kumanga misewu yabwino, mawaya amagetsi ndi machitidwe amadzi. Adzakambirana za ulimi ndi mchere. Kumwera kwa Africa kuli ndi mchere wambiri womwe mayiko ena amafunikira.

Misonkhano ya Lamlungu ikatha, Chihana adzapita ku phwando la boma. Purezidenti wa South Africa Cyril Ramaphosa adzachititsa msonkhanowu. Mutu wa msonkhanowu ndi "Kukula kwa mafakitale kokhazikika, kokhazikika komanso kophatikizana kudzera mu chitukuko cha zomangamanga, kusintha kwa ulimi ndi mchere wofunikira pofunafuna dziko lolungama." Izi zikutanthauza kuti atsogoleri akufuna kuthandiza Kumwera kwa Africa kukula mwachilungamo. Akufuna kuti anthu onse apindule ndi chuma cha derali.

Kupezeka kwa Chihana kukusonyeza kuti Malawi ili ndi gawo lofunika kwambiri pa zokambirana za mtendere ndi chitetezo m'chigawochi. Misonkhanoyi ithandiza mayiko omwe ali mamembala a SADC kugwira ntchito limodzi bwino pa nkhani zandale, ndalama ndi chitetezo.

en.title: MCP drops court case against two ministers
en.body: The Malawi Congress Party stopped a court case against two government officials. The case was about Chief Secretary Justin Saidi and Minister Chimwemwe Chipungu. MCP said these men did not pay rent for buildings used by the Electoral Commission. The court date was August 17. MCP's lawyer George Kadzipatike told the court to stop the case on August 14.
en.body_more:
The fight started because the Electoral Commission needs to rent a warehouse at Njewa and a building owned by Capital Development Limited in Lilongwe. MCP said Saidi and Chipungu did not help pay for these rentals on time. The case would have happened in the High Court in front of Judge Kenyatta Nyirenda.

Kadzipatike said MCP received orders from the party leaders to stop the court case. He told the High Court the news in writing on August 14. He also told the Attorney General, Frank Mbeta. Mbeta said he was ready to fight the case. He had not yet seen the notice when he spoke to reporters.

But stopping this case does not finish the whole fight. An injunction — a court order that stops something — still blocks the Electoral Commission from moving to Blantyre. This injunction is still strong and in force. Kadzipatike said the government must follow this court order. He said the Attorney General must guide the government on what to do next. The government must choose to obey the court or face what comes next.

The withdrawal of the contempt case means the hearing on August 17 will not happen against Saidi and Chipungu. However, the larger dispute about the Electoral Commission's future home in Blantyre stays alive in court. The government and the Electoral Commission must make sure they follow the injunction order.

ny.title: MCP yasiya mlandu wokhudza nduna ziwiri kukhoti
ny.body: Chipani cha Malawi Congress Party chinaimitsa mlandu kukhothi motsutsana ndi akuluakulu awiri aboma. Mlanduwu unali wokhudza Mlembi Wamkulu Justin Saidi ndi Nduna Chimwemwe Chipungu. MCP inati amunawa sanalipire lendi nyumba zomwe zimagwiritsidwa ntchito ndi Electoral Commission. Tsiku loti khothi lichitike linali pa 17 Ogasiti. Loya wa MCP George Kadzipatike adauza khothi kuti liyimitse mlanduwu pa 14 Ogasiti.
ny.body_more:
Mkangano unayamba chifukwa bungwe la Electoral Commission liyenera kubwereka nyumba yosungiramo katundu ku Njewa ndi nyumba ya Capital Development Limited ku Lilongwe. MCP inati Saidi ndi Chipungu sanathandize kulipira lendi izi pa nthawi yake. Mlanduwu ukanachitikira ku Khoti Lalikulu pamaso pa Woweruza Kenyatta Nyirenda.

Kadzipatike anati MCP inalandira malamulo ochokera kwa atsogoleri a chipani kuti ayimitse mlanduwo kukhoti. Anauza Khoti Lalikulu nkhaniyi polemba pa 14 Ogasiti. Anauzanso Loya Wamkulu, Frank Mbeta. Mbeta anati anali wokonzeka kumenyana mlanduwo. Sanawonebe chidziwitsocho pamene ankalankhula ndi atolankhani.

Koma kuletsa mlanduwu sikuthetsa mkangano wonse. Lamulo - lamulo la khoti lomwe limaletsa china chake - likuletsabe bungwe la Electoral Commission kusamuka ku Blantyre. Lamuloli likadali lamphamvu komanso logwira ntchito. Kadzipatike anati boma liyenera kutsatira lamulo la khoti ili. Anati Loya Wamkulu ayenera kutsogolera boma pa zomwe angachite kenako. Boma liyenera kusankha kumvera khoti kapena kukumana ndi zomwe zikubwera pambuyo pake.

Kuchotsedwa kwa mlandu wonyoza kumatanthauza kuti mlanduwu udzamvedwa pa Ogasiti 17 motsutsana ndi Saidi ndi Chipungu. Komabe, mkangano waukulu wokhudza nyumba yamtsogolo ya Electoral Commission ku Blantyre ukupitilizabe kukhothi. Boma ndi Electoral Commission ayenera kuonetsetsa kuti akutsatira lamulo loletsa.

en.title: Malawi women ready for Africa Cup final
en.body: Malawi's women's football team, the Scorchers, will play Cameroon in the Africa Cup of Nations final tomorrow in Rabat, Morocco. Captain Tabitha Chawinga said the team feels no pressure and is ready to fight. The Scorchers have won all their games except one loss to Zambia.
en.body_more:
Chawinga, who plays in France, told reporters that the team has peace and will go into the final with calm minds. "We are being driven by God," she said. "The mood in camp is good. The players are determined to fight for the title and make history."

The team accepted being called underdogs. "The pressure should be on Cameroon because they are the favourites," Chawinga said. "From day one, we have been the underdogs and we are OK with that." Another player, Faith Chimzimu, who plays in Sweden, said the team becomes hungrier with each game. "We are encouraging each other and pushing each other," she said.

Malawi beat Nigeria 3-2, Egypt 3-1, Ghana 2-1 and Algeria 3-1 to reach the final. They lost only once, 2-1 to Zambia. Cameroon beat Mali 2-1 and Ghana 1-0. Cameroon also beat Nigeria 1-0 and Morocco 3-1 on penalties in the quarter-finals and semi-finals. This is Malawi's first time in a Wafcon final. Cameroon will play in their fourth final. The winners will get 2 million dollars. That is about 3.5 billion Malawi kwacha. The runners-up will get 750,000 dollars, which is about 1.3 billion kwacha.

ny.title: Azimayi aku Malawi akukonzekera mpikisano wa Africa Cup
ny.body: Gulu la mpira wa azimayi la Malawi, Scorchers, lidzasewera ndi Cameroon pa mpikisano womaliza wa Africa Cup of Nations mawa ku Rabat, Morocco. Captain Tabitha Chawinga adati gululo silikumva kukakamizidwa ndipo lakonzeka kumenyana. Scorchers apambana masewera awo onse kupatulapo kugonja kamodzi ndi Zambia.
ny.body_more:
Chawinga, yemwe amasewera ku France, adauza atolankhani kuti timuyi ili ndi mtendere ndipo idzalowa mu fainali ndi maganizo odekha. "Tikutsogoleredwa ndi Mulungu," adatero. "Mtima uli bwino mumsasa. Osewerawa atsimikiza mtima kumenyera mutu ndikulemba mbiri."

Timuyi yavomereza kutchedwa kuti ndi osasewera bwino. "Kupanikizika kuyenera kukhala pa Cameroon chifukwa ndi yomwe imakonda kwambiri," adatero Chawinga. "Kuyambira tsiku loyamba, takhala osasewera bwino ndipo tili bwino ndi zimenezo." Wosewera wina, Faith Chimzimu, yemwe amasewera ku Sweden, adati timuyi imakhala ndi njala kwambiri pamasewera aliwonse. "Timalimbikitsana ndikukankhirana," adatero.

Malawi idagonjetsa Nigeria 3-2, Egypt 3-1, Ghana 2-1 ndi Algeria 3-1 kuti ifike kumapeto. Adataya kamodzi kokha, 2-1 ndi Zambia. Cameroon idagonjetsa Mali 2-1 ndi Ghana 1-0. Cameroon idagonjetsanso Nigeria 1-0 ndi Morocco 3-1 pa ma penalty mu kotala fainali ndi semi-finals. Iyi ndi nthawi yoyamba ya Malawi mu mpikisano wa Wafcon. Cameroon idzasewera mu mpikisano wawo wachinayi wa fainali. Opambana adzalandira madola 2 miliyoni. Ndalamazo ndi pafupifupi 3.5 biliyoni ya Malawi kwacha. Omaliza adzapeza madola 750,000, zomwe ndi pafupifupi 1.3 biliyoni ya kwacha.

en.title: School exam results show mixed marks across Malawi
en.body: Malawi's school exam results show good and bad news. Primary school exams went down. Junior certificate exams went up. The Malawi National Examinations Board released the results. Secretary Ken Ndala and Dorothy Nampota signed the statement.
en.body_more:
Out of 245,048 primary school students, 198,903 passed. This is 81.17 percent pass rate. It dropped from last year's 87.5 percent. More than 154,880 junior certificate students sat exams. About 125,777 passed. This is 81.21 percent — up from 77.61 percent last year.

Boys did better than girls in both exams. Male primary students passed at 85.69 percent. Female primary students passed at 76.94 percent. At junior certificate level, male students passed at 84.04 percent and female students at 78.49 percent. Students with disabilities passed at 71.5 percent for primary exams and 82.41 percent for junior certificate exams.

Some areas did better than others. Zomba Urban district had the best results — 29 percent of primary students got top marks. Mzuzu City came second with 26.91 percent. Lilongwe West was third with 25.73 percent. National secondary schools had the best results of all, with 91.21 percent pass rate. Government secondary schools did well. Community Day Secondary Schools did less well.

Education experts say the government must do more. Limbani Nsapato from the Civil Society Education Coalition said government must find out why primary results fell. He said schools need more teachers, better buildings and more learning tools. Foster Lungu, an educator at Mzuzu University, said schools do not have enough money. Many primary schools have only a few teachers. Students sit on the floor. Secondary schools also need more resources and better teaching. The government must act fast to fix these problems.

ny.title: Zotsatira za mayeso a sukulu zikuwonetsa ma mark osiyanasiyana ku Malawi konse
ny.body: Zotsatira za mayeso a sukulu ku Malawi zikusonyeza nkhani zabwino ndi zoipa. Mayeso a pulayimale adatsika. Mayeso a satifiketi ya junior adakwera. Bungwe la Malawi National Examinations Board lidatulutsa zotsatira zake. Mlembi Ken Ndala ndi Dorothy Nampota adasaina chikalatacho.
ny.body_more:
Mwa ophunzira 245,048 a kusukulu ya pulayimale, 198,903 adapambana. Izi ndi 81.17 peresenti ya chiŵerengero chopambana. Chatsika kuchokera pa 87.5 peresenti ya chaka chatha. Ophunzira a satifiketi ya junior certificate oposa 154,880 adalemba mayeso. Pafupifupi 125,777 adapambana. Izi ndi 81.21 peresenti — kuchokera pa 77.61 peresenti chaka chatha.

Anyamata adachita bwino kuposa atsikana m'mayeso onse awiri. Ophunzira a pulayimale aamuna adapambana pa 85.69 peresenti. Ophunzira a pulayimale achikazi adapambana pa 76.94 peresenti. Pa mlingo wa satifiketi ya junior, ophunzira aamuna adapambana pa 84.04 peresenti ndipo ophunzira aakazi adapambana pa 78.49 peresenti. Ophunzira olumala adapambana pa 71.5 peresenti ya mayeso a pulayimale ndi 82.41 peresenti ya mayeso a junior certificate.

Malo ena adachita bwino kuposa ena. Chigawo cha Zomba Urban chidali ndi zotsatira zabwino kwambiri — 29 peresenti ya ophunzira a pulayimale adapeza ma mark apamwamba. Mzuzu City idabwera yachiwiri ndi 26.91 peresenti. Lilongwe West inali yachitatu ndi 25.73 peresenti. Masukulu a sekondale a dziko lonse anali ndi zotsatira zabwino kwambiri kuposa onse, ndi chiŵerengero chopambana cha 91.21 peresenti. Masukulu a sekondale a boma adachita bwino. Masukulu a sekondale a Community Day adachita bwino pang'ono.

Akatswiri a maphunziro akuti boma liyenera kuchita zambiri. Limbani Nsapato wochokera ku Civil Society Education Coalition adati boma liyenera kupeza chifukwa chake zotsatira za pulayimale zidatsika. Iye adati masukulu akufunika aphunzitsi ambiri, nyumba zabwino komanso zida zambiri zophunzirira. Foster Lungu, mphunzitsi ku Mzuzu University, adati masukulu alibe ndalama zokwanira. Masukulu ambiri a pulayimale ali ndi aphunzitsi ochepa okha. Ophunzira amakhala pansi. Masukulu a sekondale amafunikanso zinthu zambiri komanso maphunziro abwino. Boma liyenera kuchitapo kanthu mwachangu kuti likonze mavutowa.

en.title: President Mutharika returns home from South Africa
en.body: President Peter Mutharika came back to Malawi on Saturday afternoon, August 15. He landed at Kamuzu International Airport after a private visit to South Africa. Chief Secretary Justin Saidi said the President had returned. People are talking about big changes in the government.
en.body_more:
Mutharika left Malawi on August 5 for this trip to South Africa. This was his fourth private visit abroad since he won the election on September 16, 2025. The President came back at a busy time. Next month, his government will mark one full year in power.

Many people are saying Mutharika will make big changes to his cabinet soon. A cabinet is a group of top leaders who help run the government. Some leaders may lose their jobs. Others may get new jobs. But Mutharika has not yet said what changes he will make.

The President has also sent a clear message to people who want his job. Mutharika said he will serve until 2030. This is his full time as President. He told others to wait for their turn. He said any race for President must wait until after 2030. This was a strong warning to rivals who are watching his power.

Now that Mutharika is back home, people are waiting to see what happens next. In the coming days, the government may announce the changes. Everyone is watching State House to see who will move or who will leave.

ny.title: Purezidenti Mutharika wabwerera kwawo kuchokera ku South Africa
ny.body: Purezidenti Peter Mutharika adabwerera ku Malawi Loweruka masana, pa 15 Ogasiti. Adafika pa bwalo la ndege la Kamuzu International Airport atapita ku South Africa payekha. Mlembi Wamkulu Justin Saidi adati Purezidenti wabwerera. Anthu akulankhula za kusintha kwakukulu m'boma.
ny.body_more:
Mutharika adachoka ku Malawi pa Ogasiti 5 kupita ku South Africa. Uwu unali ulendo wake wachinayi wachinsinsi kunja kwa dziko kuyambira pomwe adapambana chisankho pa Seputembala 16, 2025. Purezidenti adabweranso panthawi yotanganidwa. Mwezi wamawa, boma lake lidzakhala ndi chaka chimodzi chathunthu muulamuliro.

Anthu ambiri akunena kuti Mutharika apanga kusintha kwakukulu ku nduna yake posachedwa. Nduna ndi gulu la atsogoleri apamwamba omwe amathandizira kuyendetsa boma. Atsogoleri ena akhoza kutaya ntchito zawo. Ena angapeze ntchito zatsopano. Koma Mutharika sananenebe kusintha komwe apanga.

Purezidenti watumizanso uthenga womveka bwino kwa anthu omwe akufuna ntchito yake. Mutharika adati adzatumikira mpaka 2030. Iyi ndi nthawi yake yonse monga Purezidenti. Adauza ena kuti adikire nthawi yawo. Adati mtundu uliwonse wa Purezidenti uyenera kudikira mpaka pambuyo pa 2030. Imeneyi inali chenjezo lamphamvu kwa otsutsana nawo omwe akuyang'ana mphamvu zake.

Tsopano popeza Mutharika wabwerera kwawo, anthu akuyembekezera kuwona zomwe zichitike. M'masiku akubwerawa, boma likhoza kulengeza kusinthaku. Aliyense akuyang'ana Nyumba ya Malamulo kuti aone amene asamuke kapena amene achoka.

en.title: Banks help women business owners get loans
en.body: Women business owners in Malawi are getting more help to borrow money from banks. Partnerships between banks and women-led businesses now give loans without collateral. Collateral is money or goods you promise to give if you cannot pay back a loan. The meeting was held in Lilongwe on Thursday.
en.body_more:
Juliet Kimoto works for Graca Machel Trust. She spoke about how these partnerships work well. The meeting brought together COMESA Federation of Women in Business (COMFWB) Malawi Chapter and Graca Machel Trust.

Selina Mwenelupembe leads COMFWB Malawi Chapter. She said the government has made spaces where women business owners can talk to people who make rules. These spaces help women tell government and banks what they need. She said many women now want bigger businesses because of these efforts. Banks and the government are working together to give unsecured loans to women. Unsecured loans do not need collateral.

Juliette Kimotho is Advocacy Manager for Graca Machel Trust. She leads the Women Creating Wealth programme. This programme helps women entrepreneurs work with government and banks. It has made it easier for women to get loans without collateral.

Yvonne Chanika is CEO of CiFoods. She said that meetings between COMFWB and partners help make policies that work for women in real life. These talks ensure that new rules and programmes help women who run businesses every day.

ny.title: Mabanki amathandiza azimayi omwe ali ndi mabizinesi kupeza ngongole
ny.body: Eni mabizinesi achikazi ku Malawi akupeza thandizo lochulukirapo kuti abwereke ndalama ku mabanki. Mgwirizano pakati pa mabanki ndi mabizinesi otsogozedwa ndi akazi tsopano umapereka ngongole popanda chikole. Chikole ndi ndalama kapena katundu amene umalonjeza kupereka ngati sungathe kubweza ngongole. Msonkhanowu unachitikira ku Lilongwe Lachinayi.
ny.body_more:
Juliet Kimoto amagwira ntchito ku Graca Machel Trust. Iye analankhula za momwe mgwirizanowu umagwirira ntchito bwino. Msonkhanowu unasonkhanitsa COMESA Federation of Women in Business (COMFWB) Malawi Chapter ndi Graca Machel Trust.

Selina Mwenelupembe akutsogolera COMFWB Malawi Chapter. Iye anati boma lapanga malo omwe eni mabizinesi achikazi amatha kulankhula ndi anthu omwe amapanga malamulo. Malo awa amathandiza akazi kuuza boma ndi mabanki zomwe akufunikira. Iye anati akazi ambiri tsopano akufuna mabizinesi akuluakulu chifukwa cha khama limeneli. Mabanki ndi boma akugwira ntchito limodzi kuti apereke ngongole zopanda chikole kwa akazi. Ngongole zopanda chikole sizifuna chikole.

Juliette Kimotho ndi Advocacy Manager wa Graca Machel Trust. Iye akutsogolera pulogalamu ya Women Creating Wealth. Pulogalamuyi imathandiza akazi amalonda kugwira ntchito ndi boma ndi mabanki. Yapangitsa kuti zikhale zosavuta kwa akazi kupeza ngongole popanda chikole.

Yvonne Chanika ndi CEO wa CiFoods. Iye anati misonkhano pakati pa COMFWB ndi ogwirizana nawo imathandiza kupanga mfundo zomwe zimagwirira ntchito akazi m'moyo weniweni. Zokambiranazi zikutsimikizira kuti malamulo ndi mapulogalamu atsopano amathandiza akazi omwe amayendetsa mabizinesi tsiku lililonse.

en.title: Ctech Systems makes new loan software for Malawi banks
en.body: Ctech Systems Limited has made a new computer system. It is called Ctech Loan265. The system helps savings groups, small banks and money lenders do their work. It uses cloud technology. This means workers can use it online from anywhere. Chimwemwe Mwalwanda works for Ctech Systems. She said the system helps lenders manage loans better.
en.body_more:
Ctech Loan265 brings all loan work onto one platform. Loan work is money a person or business must pay back. The system manages customer sign-up, loan applications, loan approval, money given out, money paid back, and late payments. It watches loan money and makes reports. The system also counts interest. Interest is extra money paid on a loan.

The platform gives lenders better control of their loans. Workers can see loan money that is owed. They can see loan money paid back. They can see late payments. Mwalwanda said this helps leaders make good choices about money. The system also has strong lock-in security. This keeps money information safe. Each worker sees only their own work area.

Ctech Loan265 uses Software-as-a-Service model. This means savings groups and small banks do not buy the system. They pay a fee each month to use it. They do not need to build their own computer systems. They do not need to pay for workers to fix computers. Mwalwanda said this helps small lenders grow their work. The system was made in Malawi. Ctech Systems made it to help Malawi's money sector grow. Leaders can see what happens with loans on the computer screen. They can see trends and risks. This helps them give money to the right people.

ny.title: Ctech Systems yapanga pulogalamu yatsopano yobwereketsa ndalama ku mabanki aku Malawi
ny.body: Ctech Systems Limited yapanga makina atsopano a kompyuta. Amatchedwa Ctech Loan265. Makinawa amathandiza magulu osunga ndalama, mabanki ang'onoang'ono ndi obwereketsa ndalama kuchita ntchito zawo. Amagwiritsa ntchito ukadaulo wamtambo. Izi zikutanthauza kuti ogwira ntchito amatha kugwiritsa ntchito intaneti kulikonse. Chimwemwe Mwalwanda amagwira ntchito ku Ctech Systems. Anati makinawa amathandiza obwereketsa ndalama kusamalira bwino ngongole.
ny.body_more:
Ctech Loan265 imabweretsa ntchito zonse za ngongole pa nsanja imodzi. Ntchito ya ngongole ndi ndalama zomwe munthu kapena bizinesi iyenera kubweza. Dongosololi limayang'anira kulembetsa kwa makasitomala, mafomu ofunsira ngongole, kuvomereza ngongole, ndalama zoperekedwa, ndalama zobwezedwa, ndi malipiro ochedwa. Limayang'anira ndalama za ngongole ndikupanga malipoti. Dongosololi limawerengeranso chiwongola dzanja. Chiwongola dzanja ndi ndalama zowonjezera zolipidwa pa ngongole.

Pulogalamuyi imapatsa obwereketsa kuwongolera bwino ngongole zawo. Ogwira ntchito amatha kuwona ndalama za ngongole zomwe zili ndi ngongole. Amatha kuwona ndalama za ngongole zikulipidwa. Amatha kuwona malipiro ochedwa. Mwalwanda adati izi zimathandiza atsogoleri kupanga zisankho zabwino pankhani ya ndalama. Dongosololi lilinso ndi chitetezo champhamvu chotseka. Izi zimasunga chidziwitso cha ndalama kukhala chotetezeka. Wantchito aliyense amawona malo ake antchito okha.

Ctech Loan265 imagwiritsa ntchito njira ya Software-as-a-Service. Izi zikutanthauza kuti magulu osungira ndalama ndi mabanki ang'onoang'ono sagula dongosololi. Amalipira ndalama mwezi uliwonse kuti agwiritse ntchito. Safunika kumanga makompyuta awoawo. Safunika kulipira antchito kuti akonze makompyuta. Mwalwanda adati izi zimathandiza obwereketsa ang'onoang'ono kukulitsa ntchito yawo. Dongosololi linapangidwa ku Malawi. Ctech Systems idachita izi kuti ithandize gawo la ndalama ku Malawi kukula. Atsogoleri amatha kuwona zomwe zimachitika ndi ngongole pakompyuta. Amatha kuwona zomwe zikuchitika komanso zoopsa. Izi zimawathandiza kupereka ndalama kwa anthu oyenera.

en.title: Rights group asks to free Chinese wildlife trafficker Lin
en.body: The Human Rights Consultative Committee (HRCC) asked the Director of Public Prosecutions to drop corruption charges against Lin Yunhua. Lin is a Chinese man convicted of wildlife trafficking. HRCC says Lin finished his prison sentence already. He is still in jail over new charges of paying bribes to prison staff.
en.body_more:
HRCC chairperson Robert Mkwezalamba wrote a letter on July 15, 2026. He asked the DPP Fostino Maele to stop the corruption case. Mkwezalamba said the Director of Public Prosecutions has the power to do this under Section 99 of the Constitution.

Lin was arrested in August 2019. He was part of a gang that hunted and sold elephants and rhinos. In September 2021, a court in Lilongwe gave him 14 years in jail for wildlife trafficking and money laundering. Money laundering is hiding money that comes from crime. Lin got help from presidential pardon programs in December 2021, July 2023 and March 2024. HRCC says he finished his full sentence. But the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) filed new charges in 2025. The charges say Lin gave K30 million to a prison officer. He also built the officer a house in Lilongwe's Area 49. This was between 2019 and 2021. A news report in October 2024 first told this story.

HRCC says it is unfair that Lin was charged but the prison officers were not charged. The officers were only punished by losing their jobs, not taken to court. HRCC says this breaks the law equally. But the ACB already asked the High Court to drop the case. The court said no. The court said the DPP alone can stop cases, not the ACB.

Many groups do not agree with HRCC. Twelve groups working on nature and rights say dropping the charges would be wrong. They say Malawi must fight corruption and stop wildlife crime. The Justice Ministry said Lin is in jail legally. It said there is no risk of paying money to Lin.

ny.title: Gulu la ufulu lapempha kuti munthu wochita malonda a nyama zakuthengo ku China amasulidwe Lin
ny.body: Komiti Yolangiza za Ufulu Wachibadwidwe (HRCC) yapempha Mtsogoleri wa Makhothi kuti achotse milandu yachinyengo yokhudza Lin Yunhua. Lin ndi mwamuna waku China wopezeka ndi mlandu wogulitsa nyama zakuthengo. HRCC ikunena kuti Lin wamaliza kale chilango chake cha kundende. Akadali m'ndende chifukwa cha milandu yatsopano yopereka ziphuphu kwa ogwira ntchito kundende.
ny.body_more:
Wapampando wa HRCC, Robert Mkwezalamba, adalemba kalata pa Julayi 15, 2026. Adapempha DPP Fostino Maele kuti aletse mlandu wa ziphuphu. Mkwezalamba adati Mtsogoleri wa Makhothi ali ndi mphamvu zochitira izi motsatira Gawo 99 la Malamulo Oyendetsera Dziko.

Lin adamangidwa mu Ogasiti 2019. Anali m'gulu la zigawenga zomwe zinkasaka ndi kugulitsa njovu ndi zipembere. Mu Seputembala 2021, khothi ku Lilongwe lidamupatsa zaka 14 m'ndende chifukwa chogulitsa nyama zakuthengo komanso kuyeretsa ndalama. Kuyeretsa ndalama ndikubisa ndalama zomwe zimachokera ku umbanda. Lin adalandira thandizo kuchokera ku mapulogalamu okhululukira a purezidenti mu Disembala 2021, Julayi 2023 ndi Marichi 2024. HRCC ikunena kuti adamaliza chilango chake chonse. Koma Bungwe Lolimbana ndi Ziphuphu (ACB) lidapereka milandu yatsopano mu 2025. Milanduyi ikunena kuti Lin adapereka K30 miliyoni kwa wapolisi wa ndende. Anamanganso nyumba ya apolisi ku Lilongwe's Area 49. Izi zinali pakati pa 2019 ndi 2021. Nkhani ina mu Okutobala 2024 inanena nkhaniyi koyamba.

HRCC ikunena kuti n'kosalungama kuti Lin anaimbidwa mlandu koma apolisi a ndende sanaimbidwe mlandu. Apolisiwo anangolangidwa chifukwa chotaya ntchito zawo, osati kutengedwera kukhoti. HRCC ikunena kuti izi zikuphwanya lamulo mofanana. Koma ACB idapempha kale Khoti Lalikulu kuti lichotse mlanduwo. Khotilo linanena kuti ayi. Khotilo linati DPP yokha ndiyo ingaletse milandu, osati ACB.

Magulu ambiri sakugwirizana ndi HRCC. Magulu khumi ndi awiri omwe amagwira ntchito yokhudza chilengedwe ndi ufulu akuti kuchotsa milanduyo kungakhale kolakwika. Amati dziko la Malawi liyenera kulimbana ndi ziphuphu ndikuletsa umbanda wa nyama zakuthengo. Unduna wa Zachilungamo unati Lin ali m'ndende mwalamulo. Unanena kuti palibe chiopsezo cholipira ndalama kwa Lin.

en.title: Government loses K811 billion in tax money
en.body: The government lost K811.6 billion in tax money between 2022 and 2024. Tax expenditure is money the government does not collect through tax breaks and special rates. This amount more than doubled in two years. The loss puts pressure on money for schools, roads and health.
en.body_more:
Tax expenditure means the government gives tax breaks to some groups and businesses. These breaks include exemptions, deductions, credits and allowances. The government also gives preferential rates to selected sectors. Key sectors like agriculture, mining, tourism and health services have received these special tax breaks.

The large rise in tax expenditure means the Treasury loses more money that could pay for development projects. This also signals a growing fiscal deficit. A fiscal deficit is when a government spends more money than it collects. If this is not managed with care, it can harm the economy.

In response, the Treasury said it will tighten oversight and improve data collection. The government will review existing tax breaks to align them with the national development goals. The Treasury also launched a digital tax administration system. This system makes filing easier and ensures data accuracy. It also speeds up revenue collection and helps track payments in real time.

Business leaders are asked to engage with tax authorities early and verify they are eligible for tax breaks. They must keep accurate records to avoid penalties. A balanced approach to tax breaks, where benefits are linked to measurable development outcomes, helps ensure public funds support sustainable growth. The government's commitment to fiscal discipline and tax reforms offers a path for Malawi's economy to achieve steady growth and job creation.

ny.title: Boma lataya ndalama zokwana K811 biliyoni za msonkho
ny.body: Boma lataya ndalama zokwana K811.6 biliyoni za msonkho pakati pa 2022 ndi 2024. Ndalama zogwiritsidwa ntchito pamisonkho ndi ndalama zomwe boma silimasonkhanitsa kudzera mu kuchotsera msonkho ndi mitengo yapadera. Ndalamazi zawonjezeka kuwirikiza kawiri m'zaka ziwiri. Kutayika kumeneku kukuika mavuto pa ndalama za masukulu, misewu ndi zaumoyo.
ny.body_more:
Ndalama zolipirira msonkho zimatanthauza kuti boma limapereka mpumulo wa misonkho kwa magulu ndi mabizinesi ena. Mpumulowu umaphatikizapo kuchotsera msonkho, kuchotsera ndalama, ngongole ndi ndalama zothandizira. Boma limaperekanso mitengo yosankhidwa ku magawo ena. Magawo ofunikira monga ulimi, migodi, zokopa alendo ndi ntchito zaumoyo alandila mpumulo wapaderawu wa msonkho.

Kukwera kwakukulu kwa ndalama zolipirira msonkho kumatanthauza kuti Treasury itaya ndalama zambiri zomwe zingalipire mapulojekiti otukula. Izi zikuwonetsanso kuti ndalama zikuchepa. Phindu la ndalama ndi pamene boma limagwiritsa ntchito ndalama zambiri kuposa zomwe limasonkhanitsa. Ngati izi sizikuyang'aniridwa mosamala, zitha kuvulaza chuma.

Poyankha, Treasury inati ilimbitsa kuyang'anira ndikuwongolera kusonkhanitsa deta. Boma lidzawunikanso mpumulo wa misonkho womwe ulipo kuti ugwirizane ndi zolinga zachitukuko cha dziko. Treasury idayambitsanso njira yoyendetsera misonkho ya digito. Njirayi imapangitsa kuti kutumiza kukhale kosavuta ndikutsimikizira kulondola kwa deta. Imathandizanso kusonkhanitsa ndalama mwachangu komanso imathandizira kutsatira malipiro nthawi yeniyeni.

Atsogoleri amalonda akupemphedwa kuti alankhule ndi akuluakulu amisonkho msanga ndikutsimikizira kuti ali oyenerera mpumulo wa misonkho. Ayenera kusunga zolemba zolondola kuti apewe zilango. Njira yoyenera yopezera mpumulo wa misonkho, komwe maubwino amalumikizidwa ndi zotsatira zoyezeka zachitukuko, zimathandiza kuonetsetsa kuti ndalama za boma zikuthandizira kukula kokhazikika. Kudzipereka kwa boma pa kayendetsedwe ka zachuma ndi kusintha kwa misonkho kumapereka njira yoti chuma cha Malawi chipitirire kukula komanso kupanga ntchito.

en.title: Malawi Women's Football Team Reaches World Cup
en.body: Malawi's women's football team, the Scorchers, has reached the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final and qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup. National Bank of Malawi Chief Executive Officer Harold Jiya said the bank is proud to have supported women's football in Malawi. He said good support and money help teams win big games.
en.body_more:
Jiya told the team and the Football Association of Malawi that the bank has always believed in women's football. He said NBM gave money to help find and teach young female players. The bank started the NBM Women's Football Premier League to give women a place to play and show their skill.

Jiya said the Scorchers' success shows that money spent on women's football works well. He told the players that NBM will keep helping them play for Malawi in big games around the world. He said the team brings pride and hope to the whole country.

The Scorchers won the COSAFA title in 2023 and then played in the 2026 WAFCON in Morocco. They reached the semi-finals and secured a place at the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup. The team's success is different from Malawi's men's football team, which has not won big games. Women's netball team, the Queens, also ranks in the top six in the world.

ny.title: Timu ya mpira wa azimayi ya Malawi yafika pa World Cup
ny.body: Gulu la mpira wa azimayi ku Malawi, Scorchers, lafika pa mpikisano womaliza wa Women's Africa Cup of Nations ndipo lafika pa mpikisano wa FIFA Women's World Cup wa 2027. Mkulu wa bungwe la National Bank of Malawi, Harold Jiya, anati bankiyi ikunyadira kuti yathandiza mpira wa azimayi ku Malawi. Iye anati thandizo labwino komanso ndalama zimathandiza magulu kupambana masewera akuluakulu.
ny.body_more:
Jiya adauza timuyi ndi bungwe la Football Association of Malawi kuti bankiyi nthawi zonse imakhulupirira mpira wa azimayi. Anati NBM idapereka ndalama zothandizira kupeza ndikuphunzitsa osewera achikazi achichepere. Bankiyi idayambitsa NBM Women's Football Premier League kuti ipatse akazi malo osewerera ndikuwonetsa luso lawo.

Jiya adati kupambana kwa Scorchers kukuwonetsa kuti ndalama zomwe zimagwiritsidwa ntchito pa mpira wa azimayi zimagwira ntchito bwino. Adauza osewerawo kuti NBM ipitiliza kuwathandiza kusewera Malawi pamasewera akuluakulu padziko lonse lapansi. Anati timuyi imabweretsa kunyada ndi chiyembekezo kudziko lonse.

Scorchers idapambana mpikisano wa COSAFA mu 2023 kenako idasewera mu WAFCON ya 2026 ku Morocco. Adafika mu semi-finals ndipo adapeza malo ku FIFA Women's World Cup ya 2027. Kupambana kwa timuyi ndikosiyana ndi timu ya mpira wa amuna ku Malawi, yomwe sinapambane masewera akuluakulu. Timu ya netball ya akazi, Queens, ilinso m'gulu la asanu ndi limodzi apamwamba padziko lonse lapansi.

en.title: Malawi's Miss World contestant ranks 64th in Vietnam
en.body: Ireen Navicha is competing at Miss World 2026 in Vietnam. She ranks 64th in the Top 100 standings. But many Malawians are asking questions. Navicha finished second runner-up at Miss Malawi. Thandie Chisi won the Miss Malawi title. So Chisi should represent Malawi, not Navicha.
en.body_more:
Navicha is still in the competition despite the controversy back home in Malawi. Her 64th place position gives her room to move up or down as the pageant continues. The Top 100 standings are not the same as the official Miss World judging results. This means her ranking could change a lot before the final.

Pageant watchers have a list called the Sashing List. It is made by people who follow the competition and rate the contestants. Navicha has not yet appeared in this top 20 list. The Sashing List is not official. It does not decide who goes to the next round. It is just what some pageant fans think.

Navicha can still do more activities and challenges. These will help her try to climb higher in the rankings. The Miss World 2026 final will take place on September 5 in Nha Trang, Vietnam. The judges will pick the winner at the end of the competition. Contestants from all around the world are competing.

ny.title: Wopikisana nawo mpikisano wa Miss World ku Malawi ali pa nambala 64 ku Vietnam
ny.body: Ireen Navicha akupikisana pa mpikisano wa Miss World 2026 ku Vietnam. Ali pa nambala 64 pa mndandanda wa Top 100. Koma anthu ambiri aku Malawi akufunsa mafunso. Navicha adamaliza pa nambala yachiwiri pa mpikisano wa Miss Malawi. Thandie Chisi adapambana mpikisano wa Miss Malawi. Chifukwa chake Chisi ayenera kuyimira Malawi, osati Navicha.
ny.body_more:
Navicha akadali mu mpikisano ngakhale kuti pali mkangano ku Malawi. Udindo wake wa 64 umamupatsa mwayi wokwera kapena kutsika pamene mpikisano ukupitirira. Maimidwe a Top 100 si ofanana ndi zotsatira zovomerezeka za Miss World. Izi zikutanthauza kuti udindo wake ukhoza kusintha kwambiri mpikisano usanachitike.

Owonera mpikisano ali ndi mndandanda wotchedwa Sashing List. Umapangidwa ndi anthu omwe amatsatira mpikisanowo ndikuwunikira omwe akupikisana nawo. Navicha sanawonekere pamndandanda wa 20 wapamwamba uwu. Mndandanda wa Sashing si wovomerezeka. Siwusankha yemwe akupita ku gawo lotsatira. Ndi zomwe mafani ena a mpikisano amaganiza.

Navicha akhoza kuchita zochitika zambiri ndi zovuta. Izi zimuthandiza kuyesa kukwera pamwamba pa mndandanda. Fainali ya Miss World 2026 idzachitika pa Seputembala 5 ku Nha Trang, Vietnam. Oweruza adzasankha wopambana kumapeto kwa mpikisano. Opikisana ochokera padziko lonse lapansi akupikisana.

en.title: Eleven African innovators chosen for energy challenge
en.body: Eleven African innovators have been chosen for the Future of Energy Conference 2026 Innovation Challenge. The Africa Centre for Energy Policy (ACEP) and Africa Change Lab (ACL) made the announcement on 16 August in Accra, Ghana. The innovators come from Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, and Ghana. They are working on clean energy solutions across Africa.
en.body_more:
The innovators are competing in two groups: the Pan-African Low Carbon Track and the AfroHackathon Track. The challenge looks for new ideas to help Africa's energy change, sustainable industry, climate strength, and valuable minerals.

In the Pan-African Low Carbon Track, the finalists are Blessing Unoka from Nigeria (solar powered food processing), Godfrey Noel from Kenya (climate finance for small farmers), Rhyl Kiio from Kenya (biogas for off-grid communities), Tatu Kassim from Tanzania (banana waste packaging), and Tracy Achieng from Kenya (KilimoChills Solution). In the AfroHackathon Track, the finalists are AbdulBasit Bashir from Nigeria (AfreVolt battery solution), Brian Mwai from Kenya (REVLOG lithium battery recovery), Christopher Amewuho from Ghana (AfroCycle battery recycling), Joshua Ebinabo War from Nigeria (Lenol solar battery hubs), Modester Nanyunga from Tanzania (SolarPay Swap Hubs for fishing communities), and Priscila Adhiambo from Kenya (Pamoja Cell cold storage batteries).

The selected innovators will now move to the next stage. They will prepare to show their ideas to policymakers, investors, researchers, and industry leaders. The final pitch event will happen during the Future of Energy Conference in Accra from 25 to 26 August 2026. The challenge is supported by Africa Change Lab, the Africa Centre for Energy Policy, and the United Nations Development Programme through the Timbuktoo Initiative. This support helps African innovators build strong, scalable solutions for energy security and inclusive economic growth.

ny.title: Atsopano khumi ndi mmodzi aku Africa asankhidwa kuti achite nawo mpikisano wamagetsi
ny.body: Akatswiri khumi ndi mmodzi ochokera ku Africa asankhidwa kuti achite nawo mpikisano wa Future of Energy Conference 2026 Innovation Challenge. Bungwe la Africa Centre for Energy Policy (ACEP) ndi Africa Change Lab (ACL) adalengeza izi pa 16 Ogasiti ku Accra, Ghana. Akatswiri ochokera ku Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, ndi Ghana akuchokera ku Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, ndi Ghana. Akugwira ntchito yokonza njira zopezera mphamvu zoyera ku Africa konse.
ny.body_more:
Opanga zinthu zatsopano akupikisana m'magulu awiri: Pan-African Low Carbon Track ndi AfroHackathon Track. Vutoli likuyang'ana malingaliro atsopano othandizira kusintha kwa mphamvu ku Africa, mafakitale okhazikika, mphamvu ya nyengo, ndi mchere wamtengo wapatali.

Mu Pan-African Low Carbon Track, omwe afika kumapeto ndi Blessing Unoka wochokera ku Nigeria (wokonza chakudya pogwiritsa ntchito mphamvu ya dzuwa), Godfrey Noel wochokera ku Kenya (ndalama zoyendetsera nyengo kwa alimi ang'onoang'ono), Rhyl Kiio wochokera ku Kenya (biogas ya madera omwe sagwiritsa ntchito magetsi), Tatu Kassim wochokera ku Tanzania (kuyika zinyalala za nthochi), ndi Tracy Achieng wochokera ku Kenya (KilimoChills Solution). Mu AfroHackathon Track, omwe afika kumapeto ndi AbdulBasit Bashir wochokera ku Nigeria (ma batire a AfreVolt), Brian Mwai wochokera ku Kenya (REVLOG lithium batteries recovery), Christopher Amewuho wochokera ku Ghana (AfroCycle batteries recycling), Joshua Ebinabo War wochokera ku Nigeria (ma batire a solar batteries a Lenol), Modester Nanyunga wochokera ku Tanzania (SolarPay Swap Hubs for communities asodzi), ndi Priscila Adhiambo wochokera ku Kenya (ma batire oziziritsa a Pamoja Cell).

Opanga atsopano osankhidwa tsopano apita ku gawo lotsatira. Akonzekera kuwonetsa malingaliro awo kwa opanga mfundo, osunga ndalama, ofufuza, ndi atsogoleri amakampani. Chochitika chomaliza chidzachitika pa Msonkhano wa Future of Energy ku Accra kuyambira pa 25 mpaka 26 Ogasiti 2026. Vutoli likuthandizidwa ndi Africa Change Lab, Africa Center for Energy Policy, ndi United Nations Development Programme kudzera mu Timbuktoo Initiative. Thandizoli limathandiza opanga atsopano aku Africa kumanga mayankho olimba komanso osinthika kuti ateteze mphamvu komanso kukula kwachuma komwe kumaphatikizapo.

en.title: Plane crash inquiry moves to forensic phase
en.body: A committee in Parliament is investigating the plane crash that killed Vice President Saulos Chilima and eight others in June 2024. The inquiry is now moving into a new phase. Independent experts from South Africa will examine evidence. The second phase of witness hearings will start on August 24, 2026.
en.body_more:
The Parliamentary Ad Hoc Committee has hired two South African forensic experts to review the case. Their names are Dr Robert Gabriel Ngude and Dr Wilson Sibusiso Ntsele. They will check medical records and evidence from the crash. The committee may also exhume remains to learn more about what happened.

The first phase of the inquiry already heard from over 150 witnesses. These witnesses revealed serious problems. The aircraft's battery had expired in 2004 but was still being used. The plane had no Flight Data Recorder and no Cockpit Voice Recorder. These machines record what happens during a flight. The plane also lacked these safety tools. Communication between the pilots and Mzuzu Airport was not recorded. When the plane disappeared, the emergency response was slow.

Witnesses also said military and police officers blocked the crash site. They kept National Intelligence Service officers away from the wreckage. However, the first phase did not find what caused the crash. It did not prove if anyone did this on purpose. The inquiry found the plane was not safe to fly, but many questions remain unanswered.

The committee now plans to check medical files more carefully. It will ask air traffic controllers and military commanders to explain what they know. The committee will also talk with families before any exhumation happens. The inquiry can recommend people for criminal prosecution, but it cannot arrest anyone or put them in prison.

ny.title: Kufufuza za ngozi za ndege kwasanduka gawo la kafukufuku wa zamalamulo
ny.body: Komiti ku Nyumba Yamalamulo ikufufuza za ngozi ya ndege yomwe inapha Wachiwiri kwa Purezidenti Saulos Chilima ndi anthu ena asanu ndi atatu mu June 2024. Kafukufukuyu tsopano akupita ku gawo latsopano. Akatswiri odziyimira pawokha ochokera ku South Africa adzafufuza umboni. Gawo lachiwiri la kumvetsera mboni lidzayamba pa Ogasiti 24, 2026.
ny.body_more:
Komiti Yoyang'anira Nyumba Yamalamulo yalemba ntchito akatswiri awiri a zamalamulo aku South Africa kuti awunikenso nkhaniyi. Mayina awo ndi Dr Robert Gabriel Ngude ndi Dr Wilson Sibusiso Ntsele. Adzayang'ana zolemba zachipatala ndi umboni wochokera ku ngoziyi. Komitiyi ikhozanso kufukula zotsalira kuti idziwe zambiri za zomwe zinachitika.

Gawo loyamba la kafukufukuyu lidamveka kale kuchokera kwa mboni zoposa 150. Mboni izi zavumbulutsa mavuto akuluakulu. Batire la ndegeyo linatha ntchito mu 2004 koma linkagwiritsidwabe ntchito. Ndegeyo inalibe Flight Data Recorder komanso Cockpit Voice Recorder. Makinawa amalemba zomwe zimachitika paulendo. Ndegeyo inalibe zida zotetezera izi. Kulankhulana pakati pa oyendetsa ndege ndi Mzuzu Airport sikunalembedwe. Ndegeyo itasowa, kuyankha mwadzidzidzi kunali kochedwa.

Amboni adatinso asitikali ndi apolisi adatseka malo omwe ngoziyo idagwera. Anasunga akuluakulu a National Intelligence Service kutali ndi zotsalira. Komabe, gawo loyamba silinapeze chomwe chidayambitsa ngoziyi. Sizinatsimikizire ngati wina adachita izi dala. Kafukufukuyu adapeza kuti ndegeyo sinali yotetezeka kuuluka, koma mafunso ambiri sanayankhidwe.

Komitiyi tsopano ikukonzekera kuyang'ana mafayilo azachipatala mosamala kwambiri. Idzafunsa oyang'anira magalimoto a ndege ndi akuluakulu a asilikali kuti afotokoze zomwe akudziwa. Komitiyi idzakambirananso ndi mabanja asanafufuze mtembo uliwonse. Kafukufukuyu angalimbikitse anthu kuti akaimbidwe mlandu, koma sangagwire aliyense kapena kuwaika m'ndende.

en.title: Lindian mining company says licence is legal
en.body: Lindian Resources Limited owns a rare earth mine at Kangankunde in Balaka District. The company says its mining licence is legal and good. The government asked the company to upgrade its licence two weeks ago. Lindian has done its first production blast at the mine.
en.body_more:
The mining firm said in a statement that the Ministry of Mining checked the mine and found no illegal mining. The company's licence is valid and in good standing. Rift Valley Resource Developments Limited is the Malawian company that owns the licence. The ministry was happy that the mineral samples were exported with the right permission for testing and science work.

Robert Martin is the top leader of Lindian Resources Limited. He said the firm works under Malawi's laws. He said the mine will start full production in the fourth quarter of 2026. The company needs to stockpile ore to have steady production after the mine starts work.

Ignatius Kamwanje is a mining and stones expert. He said the problem is most people do not understand mining. He said the mine will work in many phases. People need to test samples as they go. Grain Malunga is the national coordinator of the Chamber of Mines and Energy. He said the project took ten years to build. He said the mine will soon make money for the country.

When the mine works, it will make about K205 billion every year for 40 years. The mine has 261 million metric tonnes of ore. The high-grade starter zone has 26 million tonnes for early production. The mine will start in October this year. The Attorney General said mining firms must obey licence rules or they will be shut down.

ny.title: Kampani ya migodi ya ku Lindian yati chilolezo ndi chovomerezeka
ny.body: Lindian Resources Limited ili ndi mgodi wa rare earth ku Kangankunde m'boma la Balaka. Kampaniyo ikunena kuti chilolezo chake cha migodi ndi chovomerezeka komanso chabwino. Boma lidapempha kampaniyo kuti ikonzenso chilolezo chake milungu iwiri yapitayo. Lindian yachita kafukufuku wake woyamba pa mgodiwo.
ny.body_more:
Kampani ya migodi inanena m'mawu ake kuti Unduna wa Migodi unayang'ana mgodi ndipo sunapeze migodi yosaloledwa. Chilolezo cha kampaniyo ndi chovomerezeka ndipo chili bwino. Rift Valley Resource Developments Limited ndi kampani yaku Malawi yomwe ili ndi chilolezocho. Undunawu unasangalala kuti zitsanzo za mchere zinatumizidwa kunja ndi chilolezo choyenera choyesera ndi ntchito zasayansi.

Robert Martin ndiye mtsogoleri wamkulu wa Lindian Resources Limited. Anati kampaniyo imagwira ntchito motsatira malamulo a Malawi. Anati mgodiwo uyamba kupanga mokwanira mu kotala lachinayi la 2026. Kampaniyo iyenera kusunga miyala kuti ikhale ndi kupanga kosalekeza mgodiwo utangoyamba kugwira ntchito.

Ignatius Kamwanje ndi katswiri wa migodi ndi miyala. Anati vuto ndilakuti anthu ambiri samvetsa migodi. Anati mgodiwo udzagwira ntchito m'magawo ambiri. Anthu ayenera kuyesa zitsanzo pamene zikupita. Grain Malunga ndi wogwirizanitsa dziko lonse wa Chamber of Mines and Energy. Anati ntchitoyi inatenga zaka khumi kuti imangidwe. Anati mgodiwo upanga ndalama posachedwa mdzikolo.

Mgodiwo ukagwira ntchito, upanga pafupifupi K205 biliyoni chaka chilichonse kwa zaka 40. Mgodiwu uli ndi matani 261 miliyoni a miyala yamtengo wapatali. Malo oyambira apamwamba ali ndi matani 26 miliyoni opangira koyambirira. Mgodiwu uyamba mu Okutobala chaka chino. Loya Wamkulu adati makampani amigodi ayenera kutsatira malamulo a ziphaso apo ayi adzatsekedwa.

en.title: Malawi Women's Football Team Reaches World Cup Final
en.body: Malawi's Scorchers women's football team has reached the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. They qualified by finishing in the top four at the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. Each player will get at least K52.5 million as a payment for playing in the World Cup.
en.body_more:
The team beat Algeria 3-1 on Wednesday at Stade Olympique de Rabat in Morocco. This win took Malawi to the final of the Africa Cup of Nations for the first time. They will now face Cameroon on 16 August.

Taitha Chawinga and Temwa Chawinga have been the top players for Malawi. Together they have scored 9 goals in the tournament. Temwa has 5 goals and is joint-top goalscorer with Zambia's Barbra Banda. Taitha has 4 goals. Sports analyst Tadala Manda said the sisters played very well. But she said Malawi must score more goals and not waste chances. If they waste chances against Cameroon, they will lose, she said.

Coach Lovemore Fazili said he is happy with the win but the game was hard. He said the final on Sunday is very important for Malawi. Temwa Chawinga said many people did not believe Malawi could reach this level. She said the team showed the world that Malawi has good players. Football Association president Fleetwood Haiya said on Facebook that Malawi has reached a historic moment.

FIFA has said it will give the same prize money to women's World Cup players as men's World Cup players in 2026 and 2027. At the 2026 Men's World Cup, each team gets K20.8 billion just for taking part. Women players will now get similar amounts. Team captain Taitha Chawinga said the money will help motivate the players. But she said the most important thing is to play well and get world attention at the World Cup.

ny.title: Timu ya mpira wa azimayi ya Malawi yafika pa mpikisano wa World Cup Final
ny.body: Gulu la mpira wa azimayi la ku Malawi la Scorchers lafika pa mpikisano wa FIFA Women's World Cup ku Brazil mu 2027. Lafika pamlingo woyenerera mwa kumaliza m'gulu la anayi apamwamba pa mpikisano wa 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations ku Morocco. Wosewera aliyense adzalandira ndalama zosachepera K52.5 miliyoni ngati malipiro osewerera mu World Cup.
ny.body_more:
Timuyi idagonjetsa Algeria 3-1 Lachitatu ku Stade Olympique de Rabat ku Morocco. Kupambana kumeneku kunapangitsa kuti Malawi ifike kumapeto kwa mpikisano wa Africa Cup of Nations koyamba. Tsopano akumana ndi Cameroon pa 16 Ogasiti.

Taitha Chawinga ndi Temwa Chawinga akhala osewera apamwamba ku Malawi. Onse pamodzi apeza zigoli 9 mu mpikisanowu. Temwa ali ndi zigoli 5 ndipo ndi wopambana zigoli limodzi ndi Barbra Banda wa ku Zambia. Taitha ali ndi zigoli 4. Katswiri wa zamasewera Tadala Manda adati alongowa adasewera bwino kwambiri. Koma adati Malawi iyenera kupeza zigoli zambiri osati kutaya mwayi. Ngati atataya mwayi motsutsana ndi Cameroon, adzataya, adatero.

Mphunzitsi Lovemore Fazili adati akusangalala ndi kupambana koma masewerawa anali ovuta. Adati masewera omaliza Lamlungu ndi ofunikira kwambiri ku Malawi. Temwa Chawinga adati anthu ambiri sakhulupirira kuti Malawi ingafike pamlingo uwu. Adati timuyi yawonetsa dziko lonse kuti Malawi ili ndi osewera abwino. Purezidenti wa Football Association Fleetwood Haiya adati pa Facebook kuti Malawi yafika pa mbiri yakale.


FIFA yati ipereka ndalama zofanana kwa osewera a World Cup azimayi ndi osewera a World Cup amuna mu 2026 ndi 2027. Pa 2026 Men's World Cup, gulu lililonse limalandira K20.8 biliyoni chifukwa chongotenga nawo mbali. Osewera azimayi tsopano alandira ndalama zofanana. Kaputeni wa timuyi Taitha Chawinga adati ndalamazo zithandiza kulimbikitsa osewerawo. Koma adati chofunika kwambiri ndikusewera bwino ndikukopa chidwi cha dziko lonse pa World Cup.

en.title: African parliaments must rebuild public trust
en.body: The United Nations Development Programme and other world leaders have called on African parliaments to rebuild public trust. They spoke at a conference in Lilongwe yesterday. The conference brought together about 300 leaders from African parliaments. UNDP representative Fenella Frost said public trust in government is falling. She said this trust is very important for democracy and development.
en.body_more:
Frost explained that without trust, new laws and plans fail. Citizens do not believe the government can help them. She said parliaments must listen to all people. This includes women, young people, and people with disabilities. These groups must have a say in government decisions.

Speaker of Parliament Sameer Suleman agreed. He said Parliament is not listening enough to the people it serves. Suleman said Parliament must be more honest and clear about what it does. "We are not responsive enough. We are not checking government power enough. We are not being open enough," he said. Suleman is also the leader of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association Africa Region.

The conference runs until 16 August. It is held at Bingu International Conference Centre. About 300 people from 17 African countries are there. They include parliament speakers, members of parliament, and other officials. The conference theme is "Renewing the Social Contract: Parliaments as Catalysts for Inclusive Growth and Citizen Trust." Stephen Twigg, secretary general of Commonwealth Parliamentary Association, said this trust problem is worldwide. But African parliaments must act now. The conference gives them a chance to share ideas and help each other.

ny.title: Nyumba zamalamulo zaku Africa ziyenera kumanganso chidaliro cha anthu
ny.body: Bungwe la United Nations Development Programme ndi atsogoleri ena apadziko lonse lapansi apempha ma nyumba amalamulo aku Africa kuti ayambitsenso chidaliro cha anthu. Iwo adalankhula pamsonkhano womwe unachitikira ku Lilongwe dzulo. Msonkhanowu unasonkhanitsa atsogoleri pafupifupi 300 ochokera ku nyumba zamalamulo zaku Africa. Woyimira bungwe la UNDP, Fenella Frost, adati chidaliro cha anthu ku boma chikuchepa. Iye adati chidalirochi n'chofunika kwambiri pa demokalase ndi chitukuko.
ny.body_more:
Frost anafotokoza kuti popanda kudalirana, malamulo ndi mapulani atsopano amalephera. Nzika sizikhulupirira kuti boma lingawathandize. Iye anati ma nyumba amalamulo ayenera kumvera anthu onse. Izi zikuphatikizapo akazi, achinyamata, ndi anthu olumala. Magulu awa ayenera kukhala ndi mawu pa zisankho za boma.

Spika wa Nyumba Yamalamulo Sameer Suleman adavomereza. Iye anati Nyumba Yamalamulo siikumvetsera mokwanira anthu omwe imatumikira. Suleman adati Nyumba Yamalamulo iyenera kukhala yowona mtima komanso yomveka bwino pa zomwe imachita. "Sitikuyankha mokwanira. Sitikufufuza mphamvu za boma mokwanira. Sitikutsegula mokwanira," adatero. Suleman ndi mtsogoleri wa Commonwealth Parliamentary Association Africa Region.

Msonkhanowu ukuchitika mpaka pa 16 Ogasiti. Uchitikira ku Bingu International Conference Centre. Anthu pafupifupi 300 ochokera m'maiko 17 aku Africa alipo. Akuphatikizapo okamba nkhani za nyumba yamalamulo, mamembala a nyumba yamalamulo, ndi akuluakulu ena. Mutu wa msonkhanowu ndi "Kukonzanso Mgwirizano wa Anthu: Ma Nyumba a Malamulo monga Othandizira Kukula Konse ndi Citizen Trust." Stephen Twigg, mlembi wamkulu wa Commonwealth Parliamentary Association, adati vuto la kudalirana ili lili padziko lonse lapansi. Koma ma nyumba amalamulo aku Africa ayenera kuchitapo kanthu tsopano. Msonkhanowu umawapatsa mwayi wogawana malingaliro ndi kuthandizana.

en.title: Land audit finds ministers broke rules in Lilongwe
