en.body: A government audit found that serving and former ministers broke land rules in Lilongwe. Minister of Lands Chimwemwe Chipungu said he will publish their names in newspapers. The audit checked Areas 3 and 10 in Lilongwe. It found at least 20 current and former Cabinet ministers broke the rules.
en.body_more:
The audit also named judges, members of Parliament, senior government officials, and private people. Some Ministry of Lands staff also helped with the illegal land deals. Chipungu said some officials had already been reported to police. He promised no one would be protected because of their power or position.

The audit found many problems in how land is managed. Records are old and broken. Some plots were given twice to different people. Some people used fake title documents to steal land. The cadastral maps, which show where land is, date back to 2016 and do not show new changes. The audit found that people got land outside the proper rules. Some plots were made in areas that should be protected, like conservation areas and flood zones.

Chipungu said the ministry will take action. It will cancel some leases and tear down illegal buildings. People who received land but did not develop it within 24 months will lose it. They will get 60 days to fix this or lose their plots. The ministry will also update its records and check documents more carefully.

Newspapers and experts called for more action. The Nation newspaper said the government must prosecute those who broke the law. Experts said land administration in Malawi has been weak for years because of poor governance. Willy Kambwandira, from a transparency group, said Malawi has enough laws but lacks the will to enforce them. Governance expert Blessings Mbendera warned that political power is abused in land deals. He said little is done to stop this, which shows weak land governance in the country.

ny.title: Kuwunika malo kwapeza kuti nduna zaswa malamulo ku Lilongwe
ny.body: Kafukufuku wa boma adapeza kuti nduna zomwe zinalipo kale komanso zakale zinali kuswa malamulo okhudza malo ku Lilongwe. Nduna ya Zamalo Chimwemwe Chipungu adati adzafalitsa mayina awo m'manyuzipepala. Kafukufukuyu adayang'ana Madera 3 ndi 10 ku Lilongwe. Adapeza kuti nduna zosachepera 20 zomwe zilipo panopa komanso zakale zinali kuswa malamulowo.
ny.body_more:
Kafukufukuyu adatchulanso oweruza milandu, mamembala a Nyumba Yamalamulo, akuluakulu aboma, ndi anthu ena. Ogwira ntchito ku Unduna wa Zamalo nawonso adathandizira pa mgwirizano wosaloledwa wa malo. Chipungu adati akuluakulu ena adanenedwa kale ku polisi. Adalonjeza kuti palibe amene adzatetezedwa chifukwa cha mphamvu kapena udindo wawo.

Kafukufukuyu adapeza mavuto ambiri momwe malo amayendetsedwera. Zolemba ndi zakale komanso zosweka. Malo ena adaperekedwa kawiri kwa anthu osiyanasiyana. Anthu ena adagwiritsa ntchito zikalata zabodza zaumwini kuba malo. Mamapu a cadastral, omwe akuwonetsa komwe kuli malo, adachokera mu 2016 ndipo sakuwonetsa kusintha kwatsopano. Kafukufukuyu adapeza kuti anthu adapeza malo kunja kwa malamulo oyenera. Malo ena adapangidwa m'malo omwe ayenera kutetezedwa, monga madera osungira zachilengedwe ndi madera osefukira madzi.

Chipungu adati unduna uchitapo kanthu. Udzathetsa mapangano ena ndikugwetsa nyumba zosaloledwa. Anthu omwe adalandira malo koma sanawakulitse mkati mwa miyezi 24 adzataya. Adzalandira masiku 60 kuti akonze izi kapena kutaya malo awo. Undunawu udzasinthanso zolemba zake ndikuwona zikalata mosamala kwambiri.

Manyuzipepala ndi akatswiri adapempha kuti pakhale zochita zambiri. Nyuzipepala ya The Nation inati boma liyenera kutsutsa anthu omwe aswa lamulo. Akatswiri anati kayendetsedwe ka malo ku Malawi kakhala kofooka kwa zaka zambiri chifukwa cha ulamuliro woipa. Willy Kambwandira, wochokera ku gulu lochita zinthu mowonekera, anati Malawi ili ndi malamulo okwanira koma ilibe chifuniro chowatsatira. Katswiri wa kayendetsedwe ka boma Blessings Mbendera anachenjeza kuti mphamvu zandale zimagwiritsidwa ntchito molakwika pa mgwirizano wa malo. Anati palibe chomwe chachitika kuti izi zithetsedwe, zomwe zikusonyeza kuti kayendetsedwe ka malo kofooka m'dzikolo.

en.title: Court moves Namiwa bail hearing to Thursday
en.body: The High Court in Lilongwe has moved the bail hearing for Sylvester Namiwa to Thursday, August 13. Namiwa is the leader of the Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives. He was arrested on July 30 and faces two charges: treason and publishing false news. The court said it has a full schedule today.
en.body_more:
Namiwa will have spent 14 days in jail by the time the hearing happens on Thursday. His lawyer, Gift Mwenye, said the court told them the delay was because of other cases. Mwenye said the defence accepts this reason.

Namiwa was arrested after he spoke on Luntha TV in July. During the interview, he said Vice President Jane Ansah would become President within two months. He also said five powerful people have a licence to kill. Licence to kill means the right to hurt or kill people without punishment. The police say this information was false and could scare the public.

A magistrate's court sent Namiwa's case to the High Court. The High Court must now decide if Namiwa can leave jail while he waits for his trial. The State prosecutor is Brenda Kapenda from the Directorate of Public Prosecutions. Some groups that fight for human rights have asked the government to free Namiwa and drop the charges. But the government has not changed its position. Namiwa has not been found guilty. The court will decide the truth of the charges when the trial happens.

ny.title: Khothi lasamutsa mlandu wa Namiwa pa belo Lachinayi
ny.body: Khoti Lalikulu ku Lilongwe lasuntha mlandu wa Sylvester Namiwa woti amve mlandu wa belo kupita ku Lachinayi, Ogasiti 13. Namiwa ndi mtsogoleri wa Centre for Democracy and Economic Development Initiatives. Anamangidwa pa Julayi 30 ndipo akukumana ndi milandu iwiri: kuukira boma ndi kufalitsa nkhani zabodza. Khotilo lati lili ndi nthawi yonse yokonzekera mlanduwu lero.
ny.body_more:
Namiwa adzakhala atakhala masiku 14 m'ndende pofika nthawi yomwe mlanduwu udzachitike Lachinayi. Loya wake, Gift Mwenye, adati khothi lawauza kuti kuchedwako kudachitika chifukwa cha milandu ina. Mwenye adati oteteza akuvomereza chifukwa ichi.

Namiwa adamangidwa atalankhula pa Luntha TV mu Julayi. Pa nthawi yofunsidwa, adati Wachiwiri kwa Purezidenti Jane Ansah adzakhala Purezidenti mkati mwa miyezi iwiri. Anatinso anthu asanu amphamvu ali ndi chilolezo chopha. Chilolezo chopha chimatanthauza ufulu wovulaza kapena kupha anthu popanda chilango. Apolisi akuti izi ndi zabodza ndipo zitha kuopseza anthu.

Khothi la magistrate linatumiza mlandu wa Namiwa ku Khothi Lalikulu. Khothi Lalikulu tsopano liyenera kusankha ngati Namiwa angatuluke m'ndende pamene akuyembekezera mlandu wake. Woyimira milandu wa boma ndi Brenda Kapenda wochokera ku Directorate of Public Prosecutions. Magulu ena omwe amamenyera ufulu wa anthu apempha boma kuti limasule Namiwa ndikuchotsa milanduyo. Koma boma silinasinthe malingaliro ake. Namiwa sanapezeke wolakwa. Khothi lidzasankha zoona za milanduyo mlandu ukachitika.

en.title: Malawi women's football team reaches Africa Cup final
en.body: Malawi's Scorchers beat Algeria 3-1 on Wednesday night in Rabat, Morocco. This made them the first new team ever to reach the Women's Africa Cup of Nations final. The team will play Cameroon on Sunday. First Lady Gertrude Mutharika said the team must win and bring the trophy home.
en.body_more:
Captain Tabitha Chawinga scored two goals. Her sister Temwa Chawinga scored one. The victory sent Malawi into celebration across the country. First Lady Mutharika wrote on Facebook that this moment is historic. She said, "Now, 90 minutes separate us from the ultimate prize in African women's football. Let's bring the trophy home."

Malawi's journey in the tournament was remarkable. The Scorchers beat Nigeria 3-2 in their first game. Then they beat Egypt 3-1. They lost 2-1 to Zambia but finished top of their group. In the knockout stages, they beat Ghana 2-1 in the quarter-final. Then came Algeria in the semi-final, and they won again.

Cameroon, called the Indomitable Lionesses, reached the final by beating Morocco on penalties. The match between Morocco and Cameroon ended 0-0, then Cameroon won after the penalty kicks. Now Malawi and Cameroon will play on Sunday for the continental title.

The Scorchers have already achieved another historic goal. By reaching the final, they have qualified Malawi for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. This is the first time Malawi will play in a World Cup. Additionally, NBS Bank gave K245 million to the team members to share as a reward for their success in the tournament. But the players want to win the Africa Cup and make history even greater.

ny.title: Timu ya mpira wa azimayi ya Malawi yafika pa mpikisano wa Africa Cup
ny.body: Gulu la Scorchers la Malawi lagonjetsa Algeria 3-1 Lachitatu usiku ku Rabat, Morocco. Izi zapangitsa kuti likhale gulu loyamba latsopano kufika pa mpikisano womaliza wa Women's Africa Cup of Nations. Gululi lidzasewera ndi Cameroon Lamlungu. Mkazi woyamba Gertrude Mutharika adati gululi liyenera kupambana ndikubweretsa chikho kunyumba.
ny.body_more:
Kaputeni Tabitha Chawinga adagoletsa zigoli ziwiri. Mlongo wake Temwa Chawinga adagoletsa chimodzi. Kupambanaku kudapangitsa Malawi kusangalala m'dziko lonselo. Mkazi wa Purezidenti Mutharika adalemba pa Facebook kuti nthawi ino ndi yakale. Iye anati, "Tsopano, mphindi 90 zatisiyanitsa ndi mphoto yayikulu mu mpira wa azimayi aku Africa. Tiyeni tibweretse chikho kunyumba."

Ulendo wa Malawi mu mpikisanowu unali wodabwitsa. Scorchers adagonjetsa Nigeria 3-2 pamasewera awo oyamba. Kenako adagonjetsa Egypt 3-1. Adagoletsa 2-1 ndi Zambia koma adamaliza pamwamba pa gulu lawo. Mu gawo lomaliza, adagonjetsa Ghana 2-1 mu kotala fainali. Kenako Algeria idabwera mu semi-final, ndipo adapambananso.

Cameroon, yotchedwa Indomitable Lionesses, idafika kumapeto pogonjetsa Morocco pa ma penalty. Masewera pakati pa Morocco ndi Cameroon adathera 0-0, kenako Cameroon idapambana pambuyo pa ma penalty kicks. Tsopano Malawi ndi Cameroon zisewera Lamlungu kuti zipambane mpikisano wa continental.

Scorchers akwaniritsa kale cholinga china chambiri. Pofika pa fainali, athandiza Malawi kuti ilowe nawo mu FIFA Women's World Cup ya 2027 ku Brazil. Iyi ndi nthawi yoyamba kuti Malawi isewera mu World Cup. Kuphatikiza apo, NBS Bank yapereka K245 miliyoni kwa mamembala a timuyi kuti agawane ngati mphotho chifukwa cha kupambana kwawo mu mpikisanowu. Koma osewerawa akufuna kupambana Africa Cup ndikulemba mbiri yabwino kwambiri.

en.title: Malawi Scorchers reach Wafcon final with 3-1 win
en.body: Malawi's women's football team, the Scorchers, won 3-1 against Algeria in the semi-final of the Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon). The match was at the Olympic Stadium in Rabat, Morocco. Captain Tabitha Chawinga scored two goals. Her sister Temwa scored one. This is Malawi's first time at Wafcon. They will now play in the final.
en.body_more:
Tabitha Chawinga was named player of the match. Algeria scored one goal through Ikram Adjabi. The match had two red cards. In the 22nd minute, Algeria's Morgane Belkhiter was sent off for a foul on Tabitha. This gave Malawi an advantage. Tabitha scored in the 34th minute with an overhead kick from a corner. Temwa scored in the 45th minute to make it 2-0 at half-time.

Before half-time ended, Malawi's Rose Kadzere was sent off after a VAR review. Both teams then played with 10 players. Algeria scored in the 60th minute through Ikram Adjabi. But Tabitha scored again in the 76th minute to make it 3-1. Coach Lovemore Fazili made changes, bringing on Vanessa Chikupila and Leticia Chinyamula. Malawi kept the win until the end.

This is a historic moment for Malawi women's football. The Scorchers beat Nigeria 3-2, Egypt 3-1, and Ghana 2-1 earlier in the tournament. They also lost to Zambia 2-1. By beating Ghana, they also qualified for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil. NBS Bank plc gave the team K245 million as a reward. Each player will get K7 million. Bank chief Temwani Simwaka said the team showed courage and strong will to win.

Malawi will face either Morocco or Cameroon in the final. This will be the biggest match in Malawi women's football history.

ny.title: Malawi Scorchers yafika pa fainali ya Wafcon ndi chigonjetso cha 3-1
ny.body: Gulu la mpira wa azimayi la Malawi, Scorchers, linapambana 3-1 motsutsana ndi Algeria mu semi-final ya Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon). Masewerawa anali ku Olympic Stadium ku Rabat, Morocco. Captain Tabitha Chawinga anagoletsa zigoli ziwiri. Mlongo wake Temwa anagoletsa chimodzi. Iyi ndi nthawi yoyamba ya Malawi ku Wafcon. Tsopano asewera mu final.
ny.body_more:
Tabitha Chawinga adasankhidwa kukhala wosewera wabwino kwambiri pamasewerawa. Algeria idapeza chigoli chimodzi kudzera mwa Ikram Adjabi. Masewerawa anali ndi makadi awiri ofiira. Pa mphindi ya 22, Morgane Belkhiter wa ku Algeria adachotsedwa ntchito chifukwa chochita cholakwika ndi Tabitha. Izi zidapatsa Malawi mwayi. Tabitha adaponya chigoli mu mphindi ya 34 ndi kick yochokera pakona. Temwa adaponya chigoli mu mphindi ya 45 kuti zigoli zifike 2-0 nthawi yopuma.

Nthawi yopuma isanathe, Rose Kadzere wa ku Malawi adachotsedwa ntchito atangomaliza kuwunikira kwa VAR. Magulu onse awiri adasewera ndi osewera 10. Algeria idaponya chigoli mu mphindi ya 60 kudzera mwa Ikram Adjabi. Koma Tabitha adaponyanso chigoli mu mphindi ya 76 kuti zigoli zifike 3-1. Mphunzitsi Lovemore Fazili adasintha, ndikubweretsa Vanessa Chikupila ndi Leticia Chinyamula. Malawi idapambana mpaka kumapeto.

Iyi ndi nthawi yakale kwambiri ya mpira wa azimayi aku Malawi. A Scorchers adagonjetsa Nigeria 3-2, Egypt 3-1, ndi Ghana 2-1 koyambirira kwa mpikisano. Adagonjetsedwanso ndi Zambia 2-1. Pogonjetsa Ghana, adayenereranso mpikisano wa FIFA Women's World Cup wa 2027 ku Brazil. NBS Bank plc idapatsa timuyi K245 miliyoni ngati mphotho. Wosewera aliyense adzalandira K7 miliyoni. Mkulu wa banki Temwani Simwaka adati timuyi yawonetsa kulimba mtima komanso kufunitsitsa kupambana.

Malawi idzakumana ndi Morocco kapena Cameroon pamasewera omaliza. Uwu udzakhala masewera akuluakulu kwambiri m'mbiri ya mpira wa azimayi ku Malawi.

en.title: FAM explains why women's football leader left Morocco early
en.body: Adelaide Migogo, who leads women's football in Malawi, left the Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco before the tournament ended. She returned home after the group stage. FAM says this was planned, not a mistake. The Malawi women's team, called the Scorchers, went on to play in the quarter-finals.
en.body_more:
FAM operations director Gomezgani Zakazaka said Migogo and other leaders were told before they left for Morocco that they would come home after the group stage finished. This was to save money. He said Migogo did not learn about her early return while she was there. She came back with other FAM leaders, including second vice-president Lameck Zetu Khonje, Daud Mtanthiko, and Patrick Kapanga.

Zakazaka said Migogo had another job to do at home. She had to lead Silver Strikers Ladies FC to Botswana for the CAF Champions League Cosafa Qualifying Tournament. This tournament will run from August 20 to 29 in Gaborone. Migogo needed to plan the travel and get ready for this work.

Zakazaka added that only FAM president Fleetwood Haiya and head of delegation Felister Dossi stayed in Morocco. The other leaders who went home were not just from FAM. They also included chairpersons who lead FAM member associations. Zakazaka said there was nothing wrong with the plan.

Not everyone agreed. Sunduzwayo Madise, who used to lead the Malawi National Council of Sports board, posted on Facebook that Migogo should have stayed. He asked: when the Scorchers moved to the quarter-finals, why did the delegation not stay longer? He said Malawi needed her in Morocco. Some people on social media also said FAM made a bad choice.

ny.title: FAM yafotokoza chifukwa chake mtsogoleri wa mpira wa azimayi adachoka ku Morocco koyambirira
ny.body: Adelaide Migogo, yemwe akutsogolera mpira wa azimayi ku Malawi, adachoka ku Women's Africa Cup of Nations ku Morocco mpikisano usanathe. Anabwerera kwawo atatha gawo lamagulu. FAM ikunena kuti izi zidakonzedwa, osati kulakwitsa. Gulu la azimayi la Malawi, lotchedwa Scorchers, linapitiliza kusewera mu kotala-fainali.
ny.body_more:
Woyang'anira ntchito za FAM, Gomezgani Zakazaka, anati Migogo ndi atsogoleri ena adauzidwa asananyamuke kupita ku Morocco kuti abwerera kwawo gulu likatha. Izi zinali zoti asunge ndalama. Anati Migogo sanadziwe za kubwerera kwake msanga pamene anali kumeneko. Anabweranso ndi atsogoleri ena a FAM, kuphatikizapo wachiwiri kwa purezidenti Lameck Zetu Khonje, Daud Mtanthiko, ndi Patrick Kapanga.

Zakazaka anati Migogo anali ndi ntchito ina yoti agwire kunyumba. Anayenera kutsogolera Silver Strikers Ladies FC kupita ku Botswana ku CAF Champions League Cosafa Qualifying Tournament. Mpikisanowu udzayamba pa 20 mpaka 29 Ogasiti ku Gaborone. Migogo anafunika kukonzekera ulendo ndikukonzekera ntchitoyi.

Zakazaka anawonjezera kuti purezidenti wa FAM, Fleetwood Haiya, ndi mtsogoleri wa gulu, Felister Dossi, ndi omwe adatsala ku Morocco. Atsogoleri ena omwe adapita kwawo sanali ochokera ku FAM okha. Anaphatikizaponso apurezidenti omwe akutsogolera mabungwe a mamembala a FAM. Zakazaka anati palibe cholakwika ndi dongosololi.

Si onse omwe adavomereza. Sunduzwayo Madise, yemwe kale ankatsogolera bungwe la Malawi National Council of Sports, adalemba pa Facebook kuti Migogo akanayenera kukhalabe. Anafunsa kuti: pamene Scorchers adasamukira ku kotala fainali, n’chifukwa chiyani gululo silinakhalepo nthawi yayitali? Anati Malawi imamufuna ku Morocco. Anthu ena pa malo ochezera a pa Intaneti adatinso FAM idasankha molakwika.

en.title: Lawyer Kadzipatike freed on bail after arrest
en.body: A court in Lilongwe freed lawyer George Jivason Kadzipatike on bail on Wednesday. Kadzipatike went to the police office on Tuesday after the Malawi Revenue Authority and police searched his law offices. The magistrate told him to pay K2.5 million in cash and find one person to promise K5 million.
en.body_more:
Kadzipatike is a lawyer and a member of parliament for Dowa Kasangadzi. He is also the legal affairs chief for the Malawi Congress Party (MCP). The MRA and police searched his offices in Lilongwe and Mzuzu last Friday and took files and computers from five lawyers.

Kadzipatike says the arrest is about tax. He says he has paid his taxes every year for 17 years of work as a lawyer. He says the MRA has given him Tax Clearance Certificates each year. Magistrate Bracious Kondowe said the case must move fast. The MRA asked for more time to give papers to the defence. The court set a new date later.

The MCP says the arrest is political. The party says the timing is bad because Kadzipatike helps the MCP in court cases against the government. The party says this looks like the government is using the law to silence them. The MCP asked the Human Rights Commission and other groups to watch what the government does.

After he left the police station, Kadzipatike said thank you to three lawyers who helped him: Jimion Nyanda, Khwima Mchizi and Jefferson Luwa. He told his clients that he is still a lawyer and his law office will work as normal. He also said he will give free law help to three men he met in the police cell, including a man arrested for stealing a car.

ny.title: Loya Kadzipatike wamasulidwa pa belo atamangidwa
ny.body: Khothi ku Lilongwe lamasula loya George Jivason Kadzipatike pa belo Lachitatu. Kadzipatike anapita ku ofesi ya apolisi Lachiwiri atatha kufufuza maofesi ake a zamalamulo ndi a Malawi Revenue Authority. Woweruza milandu adamuuza kuti alipire K2.5 miliyoni ndikupeza munthu m'modzi woti amulonjeze K5 miliyoni.
ny.body_more:
Kawirikawiri ndi loya komanso membala wa nyumba yamalamulo ya Dowa Kasangadzi. Iyenso ndi mkulu wa nkhani zamalamulo wa Malawi Congress Party (MCP). Apolisi ndi MRA adafufuza maofesi ake ku Lilongwe ndi Mzuzu Lachisanu lapitali ndipo adatenga mafayilo ndi makompyuta kuchokera kwa maloya asanu.


Kadzipatike akuti kumangidwa kwake ndi nkhani ya msonkho. Akuti amalipira misonkho yake chaka chilichonse kwa zaka 17 akugwira ntchito ngati loya. Akuti MRA imamupatsa Zikalata Zochotsera Misonkho chaka chilichonse. Woweruza milandu Bracious Kondowe adati mlanduwu uyenera kuyendetsedwa mwachangu. Apolisi a MRA adapempha nthawi yochulukirapo kuti apereke mapepala kwa oteteza. Khothi linakhazikitsa tsiku latsopano pambuyo pake.


MCP ikuti kumangidwa kumeneku ndi kwandale. Chipanichi chikuti nthawi yake ndi yoipa chifukwa Kawirikawiri amathandiza MCP pamilandu yamilandu yotsutsana ndi boma. Chipanichi chikuti izi zikuwoneka ngati boma likugwiritsa ntchito lamulo kuti liwaletse. Apolisi a MCP adapempha Human Rights Commission ndi magulu ena kuti ayang'ane zomwe boma likuchita.



Atatuluka ku polisi, Kazipatike anathokoza maloya atatu omwe anamuthandiza: Jimion Nyanda, Khwima Mchizi ndi Jefferson Luwa. Anauza makasitomala ake kuti akadali loya ndipo ofesi yake ya zamalamulo igwira ntchito mwachizolowezi. Ananenanso kuti apereka thandizo laulere kwa amuna atatu omwe adakumana nawo m'chipinda cha apolisi, kuphatikizapo mwamuna yemwe adamangidwa chifukwa choba galimoto.

en.title: Malawi leader calls for peace in Zambia election
en.body: Malawi's President Peter Mutharika has called for calm and tolerance ahead of Zambia's general election on 13 August 2026. Mutharika chairs the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation. He said the vote is important for the region and asked all voters to vote peacefully.
en.body_more:
In a statement issued on 11 August, Mutharika urged Zambians to protect peace before, during and after voting day. He encouraged all eligible voters to use their right to vote and to choose their leaders through the ballot box. Mutharika stressed that elections must be regular, credible, free, fair and transparent. He called on political players and citizens to show tolerance and respect for peace.

The SADC Electoral Observation Mission will watch the election process. Election observers watch elections to check if they are fair and done well. More than 100 observers from SADC will monitor the voting across Zambia. Mutharika said this shows the region's promise to support free and fair elections. These elections help countries have stable political and economic change, he added.

Zambia's election comes during strong political competition. President Hakainde Hichilema seeks a second term. His government campaigns on economic reforms and debt restructuring. Debt is money a country must pay back. Opposition parties challenge the government on the cost of living and other problems at home. Millions of Zambians are expected to vote. The region watches to see if Zambia will again show strong democracy through a peaceful vote and peaceful transfer of power.

ny.title: Mtsogoleri wa dziko la Malawi apempha mtendere pa chisankho cha dziko la Zambia
ny.body: Purezidenti wa Malawi, Peter Mutharika, wapempha bata ndi kulekererana chisankho cha Zambia pa 13 Ogasiti 2026. Mutharika ndiye wapampando wa bungwe la SADC Organ on Politics, Defense and Security Cooperation. Iye anati kuvotako n'kofunika kwambiri m'chigawochi ndipo wapempha ovota onse kuti avote mwamtendere.
ny.body_more:
Mu chikalata chomwe chinaperekedwa pa 11 Ogasiti, Mutharika analimbikitsa anthu aku Zambia kuti ateteze mtendere tsiku lovota lisanafike, panthawi komanso pambuyo pake. Analimbikitsa ovota onse oyenerera kugwiritsa ntchito ufulu wawo wovota ndikusankha atsogoleri awo kudzera mu bokosi lovotera. Mutharika anagogomezera kuti zisankho ziyenera kukhala zokhazikika, zodalirika, zaufulu, zachilungamo komanso zowonekera bwino. Anapempha osewera andale ndi nzika kuti asonyeze kulekerera ndi kulemekeza mtendere.

Ntchito Yoyang'anira Zachisankho ya SADC idzayang'anira momwe zisankho zikuyendera. Oyang'anira zisankho amayang'anira zisankho kuti aone ngati zili zolungama komanso ngati zachitika bwino. Oyang'anira oposa 100 ochokera ku SADC adzayang'anira kuvota ku Zambia konse. Mutharika anati izi zikusonyeza lonjezo la chigawochi lothandizira zisankho zaulere komanso zachilungamo. Zisankhozi zimathandiza mayiko kukhala ndi kusintha kwa ndale ndi zachuma kokhazikika, anawonjezera.

Chisankho cha Zambia chikubwera panthawi ya mpikisano wamphamvu wandale. Purezidenti Hakainde Hichilema akufuna nthawi yachiwiri. Boma lake likuchita kampeni yokhudza kusintha kwachuma ndi kukonzanso ngongole. Ngongole ndi ndalama zomwe dziko liyenera kubweza. Zipani zotsutsa zimatsutsa boma pamitengo ya moyo ndi mavuto ena m'nyumba. Anthu mamiliyoni ambiri aku Zambia akuyembekezeka kuvota. Chigawochi chikuyang'ana ngati Zambia idzawonetsanso demokalase yolimba kudzera mu voti yamtendere komanso kusamutsa mphamvu mwamtendere.

en.title: Rice farmers told to add value and sell abroad
en.body: Malawi's Ministry of Industrialisation, Business, Trade and Tourism has told rice farmers to add value to their rice and sell it to other countries. Deputy Agriculture Minister Edgar Tembo made this call after visiting a rice processing plant. The plant costs K750.4 million. Kajikhomele Investments Limited is building it. This company works for Karonga Catholic Diocese.
en.body_more:
The rice plant will change raw rice into packed rice ready to sell. This will help Malawi sell more rice and create jobs for local people. The government wants to buy less rice from other countries and grow local business instead.

Value addition means processing raw rice into finished products before selling. The Ministry will give money and help to farmers who do this. Farmers need to use new ways to farm, buy good seeds, and work with processors who will buy their rice. The goal is to create a chain where every person — from farmer to seller — makes money.

The rice processing plant is just one project. The Ministry has also started a value chain plan for other crops like tobacco, tea, and cassava. Farmers can add value to these crops too before selling them locally or to other countries. The government wants all business people to embrace value addition and reach international markets. This will help Malawi's economy grow and reduce how much the country buys from abroad. The Ministry says value addition is the way forward for the country's future.

ny.title: Alimi a mpunga auzidwa kuti awonjezere phindu ndikugulitsa kunja
ny.body: Unduna wa Zamalonda, Malonda ndi Zokopa alendo ku Malawi wauza alimi a mpunga kuti awonjezere phindu pa mpunga wawo ndikugulitsa kumayiko ena. Wachiwiri kwa Nduna ya Zaulimi Edgar Tembo adapempha izi atapita ku fakitale yokonza mpunga. Fakitaleyi imadula K750.4 miliyoni. Kajikhomele Investments Limited ikumanga. Kampaniyi imagwira ntchito ku Karonga Catholic Diocese.
ny.body_more:
Chomera cha mpunga chidzasintha mpunga wosaphika kukhala mpunga wokonzeka kugulitsidwa. Izi zithandiza Malawi kugulitsa mpunga wambiri ndikupanga ntchito kwa anthu am'deralo. Boma likufuna kugula mpunga wochepa kuchokera kumayiko ena ndikukulitsa mabizinesi am'deralo m'malo mwake.

Kuwonjezera phindu kumatanthauza kukonza mpunga wosaphika kukhala zinthu zomalizidwa musanagulitse. Unduna upereka ndalama ndikuthandizira alimi omwe amachita izi. Alimi ayenera kugwiritsa ntchito njira zatsopano zolima, kugula mbewu zabwino, ndikugwira ntchito ndi opanga omwe adzagula mpunga wawo. Cholinga chake ndikupanga unyolo komwe munthu aliyense - kuyambira mlimi mpaka wogulitsa - amapeza ndalama.

Chomera chopangira mpunga ndi pulojekiti imodzi yokha. Unduna wayambanso dongosolo la unyolo wamtengo wapatali wa mbewu zina monga fodya, tiyi, ndi chinangwa. Alimi amathanso kuwonjezera phindu ku mbewu izi asanazigulitse m'deralo kapena kumayiko ena. Boma likufuna kuti amalonda onse avomereze kuwonjezera phindu ndikufika pamisika yapadziko lonse. Izi zithandiza chuma cha Malawi kukula ndikuchepetsa kuchuluka kwa ndalama zomwe dzikolo limagula kuchokera kunja. Undunawu ukunena kuti kuwonjezera phindu ndiye njira yopitira patsogolo mtsogolo mwa dzikolo.

en.title: Twenty-seven fired reporters claim K688.5 million from MBC
en.body: Twenty-seven reporters fired by the Malawi Broadcasting Corporation (MBC) have gone to court. They want K688.5 million in money. They say MBC fired them in an unfair way. The reporters were hired for three years. They started on April 1 2025. MBC sent them letters on May 28 saying they must leave their jobs.
en.body_more:
The reporters say MBC hired them to cover the 2025 General Elections. The elections took place on September 16 2025. When the elections ended, MBC said the reporters' work was done and fired them. But the reporters say their contracts did not allow MBC to fire them just because the elections were over. The reporters' lawyer is Dominic Makawa. He told the Industrial Relations Court in Zomba that MBC acted unfairly.

Each reporter was earning K250,000 every month. They had 22 months left on their contracts. The reporters say they should be paid for these 22 months. That money is K148.5 million. They also want K540 million for the unfair and unsafe way MBC treated them. The total claim is K688.5 million. Reinstatement is not practical, they say, so they want money instead.

Another group of 16 journalists was also fired. They were hired between October and September 2025. MBC fired them on July 24. MBC said they did not work well enough during their probationary period. A probationary period is a time when a new worker is tested before being made permanent. MBC spokesperson Chisomo Mwamadi did not answer questions about defending the court case. He said MBC was mourning the death of Director General Brian Banda. Banda was buried on Monday.

ny.title: Atolankhani makumi awiri mphambu asanu ndi awiri omwe achotsedwa ntchito apempha MBC kuti ipereke K688.5 miliyoni
ny.body: Atolankhani 27 omwe achotsedwa ntchito ndi Malawi Broadcasting Corporation (MBC) apita kukhothi. Akufuna ndalama zokwana K688.5 miliyoni. Akuti MBC idawachotsa ntchito mopanda chilungamo. Atolankhaniwo adalembedwa ntchito kwa zaka zitatu. Anayamba pa Epulo 1, 2025. MBC idawatumizira makalata pa Meyi 28 akuti ayenera kusiya ntchito zawo.
ny.body_more:
Atolankhani akuti MBC idawalemba ntchito kuti alembe nkhani za Chisankho Chachikulu cha 2025. Chisankhocho chidachitika pa Seputembala 16 2025. Chisankhocho chitatha, MBC idati ntchito ya atolankhani yatha ndipo idawachotsa ntchito. Koma atolankhaniwo akuti mapangano awo sanalole MBC kuwachotsa ntchito chifukwa choti zisankhozo zidatha. Loya wa atolankhani ndi Dominic Makawa. Adauza Khothi Loona za Ubale wa Antchito ku Zomba kuti MBC idachita zinthu mopanda chilungamo.

Mtolankhani aliyense ankalandira K250,000 mwezi uliwonse. Anali ndi miyezi 22 yotsala pa mapangano awo. Atolankhaniwo akuti ayenera kulipidwa miyezi 22 iyi. Ndalamazo ndi K148.5 miliyoni. Akufunanso K540 miliyoni chifukwa cha momwe MBC idawachitira zinthu mopanda chilungamo komanso mosatetezeka. Ndalama zonse zomwe adapempha ndi K688.5 miliyoni. Kubwezeretsedwa ntchito sikothandiza, akutero, kotero akufuna ndalama m'malo mwake.

Gulu lina la atolankhani 16 lidachotsedwanso ntchito. Analembedwa ntchito pakati pa Okutobala ndi Seputembala 2025. MBC inawachotsa ntchito pa Julayi 24. MBC inati sanagwire ntchito mokwanira panthawi yawo yoyeserera. Nthawi yoyeserera ndi nthawi yomwe wantchito watsopano amayesedwa asanakhazikitsidwe kukhala wokhazikika. Wolankhulira MBC Chisomo Mwamadi sanayankhe mafunso okhudza kuteteza mlanduwo kukhothi. Anati MBC inali kulira imfa ya Director General Brian Banda. Banda anaikidwa m'manda Lolemba.

en.title: Super El Niño threatens Malawi's farming and economy
en.body: A big storm called Super El Niño will hurt Malawi's farms and economy. The African Development Bank says this storm will cost the world between 10 billion and 20 billion dollars. Southern Africa will be hit the hardest. Malawi's economy depends on farming, so farmers and businesses must prepare.
en.body_more:
Super El Niño is a climate event. Climate means the weather patterns of a place. This storm brings too much rain in some areas and dry spells in others. Malawi's farms will produce less food and crops. The cost of seeds and tools will go up. This makes life harder for farmers who grow rice, maize, and other crops.

The storm will also break roads, bridges, and power lines. When roads break, trucks cannot move goods to markets. When power lines break, factories stop work. Businesses that sell things will lose money. Companies that need farm products, like food makers, will find it hard to get what they need.

But some businesses may do well. Companies that process crops—turning corn into flour or maize into porridge—may grow. Insurance companies can help farmers by giving them money when crops fail. Insurance means a company pays you money if something bad happens. New farms that use less water and smart seeds may also do well.

The government, businesses, and aid groups must work together. They must build better roads and water pipes for farms. They must help farmers plant new crops that need less rain. They must teach farmers how to store food so less is wasted. When people work as one team, Malawi can face this big storm and come through strong.

ny.title: Super El Niño ikuopseza ulimi ndi chuma cha Malawi
ny.body: Mphepo yamkuntho yotchedwa Super El Niño idzawononga minda ndi chuma cha Malawi. Banki Yachitukuko ku Africa yati mphepo yamkunthoyi idzawononga dziko lonse lapansi pakati pa madola 10 biliyoni ndi 20 biliyoni. Kumwera kwa Africa kudzakhudzidwa kwambiri. Chuma cha Malawi chimadalira ulimi, kotero alimi ndi mabizinesi ayenera kukonzekera.
ny.body_more:
Super El Niño ndi chochitika cha nyengo. Nyengo imatanthauza momwe nyengo ilili. Mphepo yamkunthoyi imabweretsa mvula yambiri m'madera ena ndipo nyengo youma m'madera ena. Mafamu aku Malawi adzabala chakudya ndi mbewu zochepa. Mtengo wa mbewu ndi zida udzakwera. Izi zimapangitsa moyo kukhala wovuta kwa alimi omwe amalima mpunga, chimanga, ndi mbewu zina.

Mphepo yamkunthoyi idzaphwanyanso misewu, milatho, ndi zingwe zamagetsi. Misewu ikasweka, magalimoto akuluakulu sangathe kusuntha katundu kumsika. Zingwe zamagetsi zikasweka, mafakitale amasiya kugwira ntchito. Mabizinesi ogulitsa zinthu adzataya ndalama. Makampani omwe amafunikira zinthu zaulimi, monga opanga chakudya, adzavutika kupeza zomwe akufuna.

Koma mabizinesi ena angachite bwino. Makampani omwe amakonza mbewu—osandutsa chimanga kukhala ufa kapena chimanga kukhala phala—angakule. Makampani a inshuwaransi angathandize alimi powapatsa ndalama pamene mbewu zalephera. Inshuwaransi imatanthauza kuti kampani imakulipirani ndalama ngati chinachake choipa chichitika. Mafamu atsopano omwe amagwiritsa ntchito madzi ochepa ndi mbewu zanzeru nawonso angachite bwino.

Boma, mabizinesi, ndi magulu othandizira ayenera kugwira ntchito limodzi. Ayenera kumanga misewu yabwino ndi mapaipi amadzi a minda. Ayenera kuthandiza alimi kubzala mbewu zatsopano zomwe zimafuna mvula yochepa. Ayenera kuphunzitsa alimi momwe angasungire chakudya kuti zinthu zochepa zisawonongeke. Anthu akamagwira ntchito limodzi, dziko la Malawi likhoza kukumana ndi chimphepo chachikuluchi ndikudutsa mwamphamvu.

en.title: Parliament conference meets in Lilongwe this week
en.body: Malawi's Speaker of Parliament, Sameer Suleman, opened the 55th Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) Africa Region Conference on Wednesday in Lilongwe. The conference brings together parliament leaders from 17 African countries. Suleman warned that people are losing trust in government institutions. He said parliaments must listen more to citizens and act on their concerns.
en.body_more:
Suleman, who leads the CPA Africa Region, spoke at the Bingu International Convention Centre. He told delegates that many people feel far from political decision-making. Young people especially want more say in government choices. Suleman said the connection between people and parliament is crumbling.

The social contract is a promise between people and their government. Suleman explained this is not just words in a constitution. It is a real bond that must be lived each day. When parliaments do not listen to citizens, people lose faith in democracy. Suleman warned that this anger can damage Africa's governments.

The conference runs for several days under the theme "Renewing the Social Contract: Parliaments as Catalysts for Inclusive Growth and Citizen Trust." Speakers, presiding officers and other parliament staff from across Africa are attending. They will talk about how to make legislatures work better. They will discuss how to help citizens trust government again. Suleman said this meeting must be more than words. It must be a turning point for African democracy.

NBS Bank gave K300 million to help pay for the conference. The bank is part of Nico Group. Nico's chief executive, Vizenge Kumwenda, said the money will help make the meeting successful. Kumwenda also asked Parliament to use the event to show investors that Malawi is a good place to do business.

ny.title: Msonkhano wa Nyumba Yamalamulo ukumana ku Lilongwe sabata ino
ny.body: Sipikala wa Nyumba Yamalamulo ku Malawi, Sameer Suleman, adatsegula Msonkhano wa 55th Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) Africa Region Conference Lachitatu ku Lilongwe. Msonkhanowu umabweretsa pamodzi atsogoleri a nyumba yamalamulo ochokera m'maiko 17 aku Africa. Suleman adachenjeza kuti anthu akutaya chidaliro m'mabungwe aboma. Iye adati nyumba yamalamulo iyenera kumvetsera kwambiri nzika ndikuchitapo kanthu pa nkhawa zawo.
ny.body_more:
Suleman, yemwe akutsogolera CPA Africa Region, adalankhula ku Bingu International Convention Centre. Adauza nthumwi kuti anthu ambiri akumva kuti sakufuna kupanga zisankho zandale. Achinyamata makamaka amafuna mawu ambiri pazosankha za boma. Suleman adati mgwirizano pakati pa anthu ndi nyumba yamalamulo ukutha.

Mgwirizano wa anthu ndi lonjezo pakati pa anthu ndi boma lawo. Suleman adafotokoza kuti izi si mawu okha omwe ali mu malamulo. Ndi mgwirizano weniweni womwe uyenera kukhalapo tsiku lililonse. Nyumba zamalamulo zikamakana kumvera nzika, anthu amataya chikhulupiriro mu demokalase. Suleman adachenjeza kuti mkwiyo uwu ukhoza kuwononga maboma aku Africa.

Msonkhanowu ukuchitika kwa masiku angapo pansi pa mutu wakuti "Kukonzanso Mgwirizano wa Anthu: Nyumba zamalamulo monga Zothandizira Kukula Konse ndi Citizen Trust." Oyankhula, oyang'anira ndi antchito ena a nyumba yamalamulo ochokera ku Africa konse akupezekapo. Adzakambirana za momwe angapangire nyumba zamalamulo kugwira ntchito bwino. Adzakambirana momwe angathandizire nzika kudalira boma kachiwiri. Suleman adati msonkhanowu uyenera kukhala woposa mawu. Uyenera kukhala posinthira demokalase ya ku Africa.

NBS Bank idapereka K300 miliyoni kuti ithandize kulipira msonkhano. Bankiyi ndi gawo la Nico Group. Mkulu wa bungwe la Nico, Vizenge Kumwenda, anati ndalamazo zithandiza kuti msonkhanowu ukhale wopambana. Kumwenda adapemphanso Nyumba Yamalamulo kuti igwiritse ntchito mwambowu kuwonetsa osunga ndalama kuti Malawi ndi malo abwino ochitira bizinesi.

en.title: Stock exchanges want SMEs to list for capital growth
en.body: The Botswana Stock Exchange wants more small and medium businesses to list on stock markets. BSE official Kgotla Segwe said many companies do not know about this chance. He spoke to Malawi business journalists visiting Botswana last week. National Bank of Malawi paid for the visit.
en.body_more:
Segwe said many businesses in the region do not know how stock exchanges work. He said this limits their ability to grow. "We need to teach businesses about capital markets," Segwe said. "Stock exchanges help companies grow, expand and last a long time."

Segwe said the Botswana Stock Exchange and Malawi Stock Exchange should work together. If they do, companies could list on both exchanges at the same time. This would help businesses raise money from more investors. "We can help companies find capital outside their own country," Segwe said.

Ten business journalists from Malawi came to Botswana to learn. They visited business and financial institutions. Jane Kaonga, a journalist from Capital Radio, said the visit was helpful. "I saw how the Botswana Stock Exchange brings in companies and investors," Kaonga said. She said Malawi can learn from what Botswana does. "This visit gives us new ideas to write better stories about money and business," she said. "It shows what Malawi Stock Exchange can do."

National Bank of Malawi (NBM) plc paid for the visit. NBM said the tour helps journalists understand business and financial markets. The tour is part of NBM's work to teach journalists about money, investment and how economies grow. The journalists saw how Botswana's practices work. They will bring these ideas back to Malawi.

ny.title: Makampani ogulitsa masheya akufuna kuti makampani ang'onoang'ono ndi apakatikati alembedwe pamndandanda wa omwe akufuna kukula kwa ndalama zawo
ny.body: Bungwe la Botswana Stock Exchange likufuna kuti mabizinesi ang'onoang'ono ndi apakatikati alembedwe m'misika yamasheya. Mkulu wa BSE Kgotla Segwe adati makampani ambiri sakudziwa za mwayiwu. Adalankhula ndi atolankhani amalonda aku Malawi omwe adapita ku Botswana sabata yatha. National Bank of Malawi idalipira ulendowu.
ny.body_more:
Segwe anati mabizinesi ambiri m'derali sakudziwa momwe misika yamasheya imagwirira ntchito. Anati izi zimawalepheretsa kukula. "Tiyenera kuphunzitsa mabizinesi za misika yamakampani," adatero Segwe. "Misika yamasheya imathandiza makampani kukula, kukulitsa komanso kukhala nthawi yayitali."

Segwe anati Botswana Stock Exchange ndi Malawi Stock Exchange ziyenera kugwirira ntchito limodzi. Ngati atero, makampani akhoza kulemba mndandanda m'misika yonse iwiri nthawi imodzi. Izi zingathandize mabizinesi kupeza ndalama kuchokera kwa osunga ndalama ambiri. "Tingathandize makampani kupeza ndalama kunja kwa dziko lawo," adatero Segwe.

Atolankhani khumi amalonda ochokera ku Malawi anabwera ku Botswana kudzaphunzira. Anapita ku mabungwe amalonda ndi azachuma. Jane Kaonga, mtolankhani wochokera ku Capital Radio, anati ulendowu unali wothandiza. "Ndaona momwe Botswana Stock Exchange imabweretsera makampani ndi osunga ndalama," adatero Kaonga. Anati Malawi ikhoza kuphunzira kuchokera ku zomwe Botswana imachita. "Ulendowu umatipatsa malingaliro atsopano olembera nkhani zabwino zokhudza ndalama ndi bizinesi," adatero. "Zikuwonetsa zomwe Malawi Stock Exchange ingachite."

National Bank of Malawi (NBM) plc idalipira ulendowu. NBM idati ulendowu umathandiza atolankhani kumvetsetsa misika yamalonda ndi zachuma. Ulendowu ndi gawo la ntchito ya NBM yophunzitsa atolankhani za ndalama, ndalama zomwe zayikidwa komanso momwe chuma chikukulira. Atolankhani adawona momwe machitidwe aku Botswana amagwirira ntchito. Adzabweretsa malingaliro awa ku Malawi.

en.title: MCP party split deepens over Chakwera leadership
en.body: A group called MCP Veterans tried to seal the offices of Malawi Congress Party president Lazarus Chakwera on Tuesday. The group also targeted offices of party secretary general Richard Chimwendo Banda. This move shows the party has deep problems over who should lead it.
en.body_more:
Some MCP members want Chakwera to step down as leader. They are asking for a party convention — a big meeting where members choose new leaders. Chakwera's spokesperson Gift Nankhuni said he did not know about any plan to remove Chakwera. Nankhuni is also an MCP MP and a lawyer.

Alex Major is an MCP politician who has said he wants to be party leader. Major said he would win if the party holds a convention to choose a new leader. But Major said he did not help seal the offices on Tuesday. He called the office sealing a small matter done by people who think badly. Major said the party should solve its problems using proper party rules, not by blocking offices.

Richard Chimwendo Banda, the party secretary general, took a softer approach. He said he would listen to what party members want. He said he would try to fix the disagreement inside the party. The MCP lost the general election in September 2025. Now the party is in opposition — it is not the government. The party faces big pressure to fix its problems and work as one group again. If the party stays divided, it cannot work well or show the public a strong opposition.

ny.title: Kugawikana kwa chipani cha MCP kwakula chifukwa cha utsogoleri wa Chakwera
ny.body: Gulu lotchedwa MCP Veterans linayesa kutseka maofesi a pulezidenti wa chipani cha Malawi Congress Party Lazarus Chakwera Lachiwiri. Gululo linalimbananso ndi maofesi a mlembi wamkulu wa chipani Richard Chimwendo Banda. Izi zikusonyeza kuti chipanichi chili ndi mavuto akulu pankhani ya yemwe ayenera kuchitsogolera.
ny.body_more:
Mamembala ena a MCP akufuna kuti Chakwera achoke paudindo monga mtsogoleri. Akupempha msonkhano waukulu wa chipani - msonkhano waukulu womwe mamembala amasankha atsogoleri atsopano. Mneneri wa Chakwera, Gift Nankhuni, adati sakudziwa za dongosolo lililonse lochotsa Chakwera. Nankhuni nayenso ndi MP wa MCP komanso loya.

Alex Major ndi wandale wa MCP yemwe wanena kuti akufuna kukhala mtsogoleri wa chipani. Major adati angapambane ngati chipani chichita msonkhano wosankha mtsogoleri watsopano. Koma Major adati sanathandize kutseka maofesi Lachiwiri. Adati kutseka ofesiyo ndi nkhani yaying'ono yochitidwa ndi anthu omwe amaganiza molakwika. Major adati chipanichi chiyenera kuthetsa mavuto ake pogwiritsa ntchito malamulo oyenera a chipani, osati kuletsa maofesi.

Richard Chimwendo Banda, mlembi wamkulu wa chipanichi, adatenga njira yofewa. Adati adzamvera zomwe mamembala a chipani akufuna. Adati adzayesa kukonza kusamvana mkati mwa chipanichi. MCP idataya chisankho chachikulu mu Seputembala 2025. Tsopano chipanichi chikutsutsa - si boma. Chipanichi chikukumana ndi kukakamizidwa kwakukulu kuti chikonze mavuto ake ndikugwiranso ntchito ngati gulu limodzi kachiwiri. Ngati chipanichi chikapitirizabe kugawanika, sichingagwire ntchito bwino kapena kuwonetsa anthu kuti ndi otsutsa amphamvu.

en.title: Tobacco Farmers Earn Less Money This Year
en.body: Malawi's tobacco farmers are making much less money this season. After 16 weeks of sales, the country sold 130.2 million kilogrammes of tobacco. The price fell from $2.55 per kilogramme last year to $2 per kilogramme now. Farmers earned $260.8 million (K456.6 billion) so far, down from $412.5 million last year.
en.body_more:
The price drop is very big. It fell by about 21 per cent. Abiel Kalima Banda is the leader of Tama Farmers Trust. He said this season is bad for farmers. The price of $2 per kilogramme does not cover what it costs to grow tobacco. Farmers cannot make enough money to feed their families or prepare for next year.

AHL Tobacco Sales Limited gave the numbers. Last year, farmers sold 161.9 million kilogrammes. This year, they sold only 130.2 million kilogrammes. The final amount of tobacco to grow this year is 154.9 million kilogrammes. About 24.7 million kilogrammes still need to be sold. Buyers are not buying much tobacco. This is why the price is low.

The Tobacco Commission said Malawi would make 197 million kilogrammes. But that did not happen. Banda said the problem is not too much tobacco. The problem is that buyers do not want to buy. He said the old reason about too much supply does not fit what is happening now.

Tobacco is very important for Malawi. It brings in much foreign money. But this year, Malawi will earn much less than last year. Last year, tobacco sales made $542 million. Now the money is much smaller. This hurts poor farmers and their families. It also hurts the whole country.

ny.title: Alimi a Fodya Amapeza Ndalama Zochepa Chaka Chino
ny.body: Alimi a fodya ku Malawi akupeza ndalama zochepa kwambiri nyengo ino. Pambuyo pa masabata 16 ogulitsa, dzikolo linagulitsa makilogalamu 130.2 miliyoni a fodya. Mtengo unatsika kuchoka pa $2.55 pa kilogalamu chaka chatha kufika pa $2 pa kilogalamu tsopano. Alimi adapeza $260.8 miliyoni (K456.6 biliyoni) mpaka pano, kuchoka pa $412.5 miliyoni chaka chatha.
ny.body_more:
Kutsika kwa mtengo ndi kwakukulu kwambiri. Kwatsika ndi pafupifupi 21 peresenti. Abiel Kalima Banda ndi mtsogoleri wa Tama Farmers Trust. Iye anati nyengo ino ndi yoipa kwa alimi. Mtengo wa $2 pa kilogalamu imodzi suphimba ndalama zomwe zimafunika kulima fodya. Alimi sangathe kupeza ndalama zokwanira kudyetsa mabanja awo kapena kukonzekera chaka chamawa.

AHL Tobacco Sales Limited inapereka manambala. Chaka chatha, alimi adagulitsa makilogalamu 161.9 miliyoni. Chaka chino, adagulitsa makilogalamu 130.2 miliyoni okha. Kuchuluka komaliza kwa fodya chaka chino ndi makilogalamu 154.9 miliyoni. Makilogalamu pafupifupi 24.7 miliyoni akufunikabe kugulitsidwa. Ogula sakugula fodya wambiri. Ichi ndichifukwa chake mtengo wake ndi wotsika.

Bungwe la Tobacco Commission linati Malawi ipanga makilogalamu 197 miliyoni. Koma sizinachitike. Banda anati vuto si fodya wochuluka kwambiri. Vuto ndilakuti ogula sakufuna kugula. Iye anati chifukwa chakale chopezera fodya wochuluka sichikugwirizana ndi zomwe zikuchitika pano.

Fodya ndi wofunika kwambiri ku Malawi. Zimabweretsa ndalama zambiri zakunja. Koma chaka chino, Malawi ipeza ndalama zochepa kwambiri kuposa chaka chatha. Chaka chatha, malonda a fodya adapeza $542 miliyoni. Tsopano ndalamazo ndi zochepa kwambiri. Izi zimavulaza alimi osauka ndi mabanja awo. Zimavulazanso dziko lonse.

en.title: Women's Football Chief Left Morocco After Group Stage
en.body: Adelaide Migogo, chair of women's football in Malawi, left Morocco during the Women's Africa Cup of Nations. The Football Association of Malawi says this was planned. Migogo went to watch the group stage matches. She left when the group stage ended, as agreed before the trip.
en.body_more:
The Football Association of Malawi put out a statement to clear up talk about Migogo's departure. The statement said FAM president Fleetwood Haiya told the executive committee before the trip that the group would stay in Morocco only until the group stage finished. All executive members agreed to this plan.

Migogo traveled to Morocco with other FAM leaders, including Chimango Munthali. They all left after the group stage ended. Felistus Dossi, a FAM executive member and Competitions Chairperson, was named as the official leader of the delegation for the rest of the tournament. Only Haiya, Dossi, and FAM secretariat staff stayed in Morocco after the other executive members went home.

The statement also explained the roles of different football bodies in Malawi. The Football Association of Malawi is in charge of all national teams, including the Flames and the Scorchers. The National Women's Football Association runs the women's domestic league. The FAM secured the Scorchers' sponsorship deal with National Bank of Malawi, not the women's football body. The Scorchers qualified for the Women's World Cup after Migogo and the other executive members had already returned to Malawi.

Some football people have questioned whether Migogo gets enough credit for her work with the Scorchers. Pundit Cliff Kawanga raised questions about this. The FAM statement was made to answer these questions and set out the facts about who did what during the tournament.

ny.title: Mtsogoleri wa mpira wa azimayi wachoka ku Morocco pambuyo pa gawo la magulu
ny.body: Adelaide Migogo, wapampando wa mpira wa azimayi ku Malawi, adachoka ku Morocco pa nthawi ya mpikisano wa Women's Africa Cup of Nations. Bungwe la Football Association of Malawi likuti izi zidakonzedwa. Migogo adapita kukaonera masewera a gulu. Adachoka gawo la gulu litatha, monga momwe adavomerezera ulendo usanachitike.
ny.body_more:
Bungwe la Football Association of Malawi lapereka chikalata chofotokozera momveka bwino za kuchoka kwa Migogo. Chikalatacho chinati purezidenti wa FAM, Fleetwood Haiya, adauza komiti yayikulu ulendo usanachitike kuti gululi likhala ku Morocco mpaka gawo la gulu litatha. Mamembala onse akuluakulu adagwirizana ndi dongosololi.

Migogo adapita ku Morocco ndi atsogoleri ena a FAM, kuphatikiza Chimango Munthali. Onse adachoka gawo la gulu litatha. Felistus Dossi, membala wamkulu wa FAM komanso Wapampando wa Mpikisano, adasankhidwa kukhala mtsogoleri wovomerezeka wa nthumwi yonse ya mpikisano. Haiya, Dossi, ndi antchito a secretariat a FAM okha ndi omwe adatsala ku Morocco mamembala ena akuluakulu atapita kwawo.

Chikalatacho chinafotokozanso ntchito za mabungwe osiyanasiyana a mpira ku Malawi. Bungwe la Football Association of Malawi ndilo limayang'anira magulu onse adziko, kuphatikiza Flames ndi Scorchers. Bungwe la National Women's Football Association limayendetsa ligi ya akazi. FAM idapeza mgwirizano wothandizira wa Scorchers ndi National Bank of Malawi, osati bungwe la mpira wa azimayi. A Scorchers adayenerera mpikisano wa Women's World Cup Migogo ndi akuluakulu ena atabwerera kale ku Malawi.

Anthu ena a mpira adakayikira ngati Migogo adapeza ulemu wokwanira chifukwa cha ntchito yake ndi a Scorchers. Pundit Cliff Kawanga adafunsa mafunso okhudza izi. Mawu a FAM adaperekedwa kuti ayankhe mafunso awa ndikuwonetsa zenizeni za omwe adachita chiyani panthawi ya mpikisano.

en.title: Police get electric car and bike to save fuel
en.body: Tsuyoshi Motors Limited gave Central Region Police an electric patrol car and an electric motorcycle. The donation helps police save money on fuel and reach crime scenes faster. Police Commissioner Mabvuto M'bobo said the vehicles are good for busy city areas.
en.body_more:
Tsuyoshi Motors Managing Director Trevor William Kandoje said the company gave this gift to help the police. The police face big problems. Fuel costs are high. Vehicles break down often. Money for repairs is not enough. Kandoje said electric vehicles cost much less to use. Charging an electric vehicle costs about 70 percent less per kilometre than fuel. Electric vehicles have fewer parts inside. They break down less often. They do not produce dirty air from engines.

M'bobo said the electric motorcycle will help police move faster in busy city areas. Police can reach crime scenes more quickly. The new vehicles will save money the police can spend on other work. M'bobo said this is a big step forward for the Police Service.

Kandoje said Tsuyoshi Motors wants to work with the government to give more electric vehicles to other government offices. Many people and offices can use this new idea. The country has problems getting fuel and money to buy fuel. Electric vehicles can help fix this problem. However, the country needs charging stations for electric vehicles. The electricity supply must be strong and steady. Police need people who know how to fix electric vehicles.

The donation lets the police test if electric vehicles work well for police work. The vehicles must be fast and reliable for emergency calls. If this works well, other police units and government offices may get electric vehicles too.

ny.title: Apolisi apatsidwa galimoto yamagetsi ndi njinga kuti asunge mafuta
ny.body: Kampani ya Tsuyoshi Motors Limited yapatsa apolisi a Central Region galimoto yoyendera yamagetsi ndi njinga yamoto yamagetsi. Choperekachi chimathandiza apolisi kusunga ndalama zogulira mafuta ndikufikira mwachangu pamalo ochitira umbanda. Commissioner wa apolisi Mabvuto M'bobo adati magalimotowa ndi abwino m'madera otanganidwa a m'mizinda.
ny.body_more:
Mtsogoleri Wamkulu wa Tsuyoshi Motors, Trevor William Kandoje, anati kampaniyo yapereka mphatsoyi kuti ithandize apolisi. Apolisi amakumana ndi mavuto akuluakulu. Mitengo ya mafuta ndi yokwera. Magalimoto amawonongeka nthawi zambiri. Ndalama zokonzera sizikwanira. Kandoje anati magalimoto amagetsi amawononga ndalama zochepa kwambiri kuti agwiritse ntchito. Kulipiritsa galimoto yamagetsi kumawononga pafupifupi 70 peresenti pa kilomita imodzi kuposa mafuta. Magalimoto amagetsi ali ndi zigawo zochepa mkati. Amawonongeka kawirikawiri. Sapanga mpweya wonyansa kuchokera ku injini.

M'bobo anati njinga yamoto yamagetsi ithandiza apolisi kuyenda mwachangu m'madera otanganidwa mumzinda. Apolisi amatha kufika pamalo ochitira umbanda mwachangu. Magalimoto atsopanowa adzasunga ndalama zomwe apolisi angagwiritse ntchito pantchito zina. M'bobo anati iyi ndi sitepe yayikulu yopita patsogolo kwa Apolisi.

Kandoje anati Tsuyoshi Motors ikufuna kugwira ntchito ndi boma kuti ipereke magalimoto ambiri amagetsi ku maofesi ena aboma. Anthu ambiri ndi maofesi angagwiritse ntchito lingaliro latsopanoli. Dzikoli lili ndi mavuto opeza mafuta ndi ndalama zogulira mafuta. Magalimoto amagetsi angathandize kukonza vutoli. Komabe, dzikolo likufunika malo ochapira magalimoto amagetsi. Magetsi ayenera kukhala olimba komanso okhazikika. Apolisi akufunika anthu odziwa kukonza magalimoto amagetsi.

Mphatsoyi imalola apolisi kuyesa ngati magalimoto amagetsi amagwira ntchito bwino ndi apolisi. Magalimoto ayenera kukhala achangu komanso odalirika pa mafoni adzidzidzi. Ngati izi zikugwira ntchito bwino, magulu ena a apolisi ndi maofesi aboma nawonso angapeze magalimoto amagetsi.

en.title: Malawi women's team plays Algeria in World Cup semi-final
en.body: Malawi's women's football team, the Scorchers, will play Algeria in the semi-final of the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations. The match is on Wednesday in Rabat, Morocco. Malawi beat Ghana 2-1 in the quarter-final. Algeria are ranked 74th in the world. Malawi are ranked 153rd. The winner will go to the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil.
en.body_more:
The Scorchers have already qualified for the World Cup after beating Ghana. Coach Lovemore Fazili said the team is ready. "We are in the semi-finals and if we win, we will be in the finals," he said. "I am confident that what we have been preparing will work." Fazili also said players are not relaxed. They know the Algeria match is very important.

Algeria are strong. They beat Cameroon 3-1, Kenya 2-0, Senegal 2-0 and Ivory Coast 2-1. They lost only 1-0 to Morocco. Algeria coach Farid Benstiti said his team must play good defence. He said they must keep working hard and not think about the final yet. Some of Algeria's players play in Europe. Inés Boutaleb plays for Auxerre Women. Captain Marine Dafeur plays for Bristol City. Lynda Bendris plays for AS Cannes.

Malawi have good players too. Captain Tabitha Chawinga leads the team. Her sister Temwa helps in attack. Faith Chimzimu, Rose Kabzere, Leticia Chinyamula and Ireen Khumalo also play. Goalkeeper Mercy Sikelo and defenders Benadetta Mkandawire and Chimwemwe Madise protect the goal. Malawi beat Nigeria and Egypt to win their group. This is Malawi's first time at the Women's Africa Cup of Nations.

If Malawi win, they get the final. The winner of the tournament gets about K3.5 billion. The second place team gets about K1.3 billion. But Tabitha said money is not the main thing. She said young players want to be seen by big teams from around the world. Malawi players want to play at the World Cup because it is the biggest stage in football.

ny.title: Timu ya azimayi ya Malawi isewera ndi Algeria mu semi-final ya World Cup
ny.body: Gulu la mpira wa azimayi la Malawi, Scorchers, lidzasewera ndi Algeria mu semi-final ya Women's Africa Cup of Nations ya 2026. Masewerawa adzachitika Lachitatu ku Rabat, Morocco. Malawi idagonjetsa Ghana 2-1 mu kotala-final. Algeria ili pa nambala 74 padziko lonse lapansi. Malawi ili pa nambala 153. Wopambana adzapita ku Women's World Cup ya 2027 ku Brazil.
ny.body_more:
A Scorchers afika kale pa World Cup atagonjetsa Ghana. Mphunzitsi Lovemore Fazili anati timuyi yakonzeka. "Tili mu semi-finals ndipo ngati tipambana, tidzakhala mu finals," adatero. "Ndili ndi chidaliro kuti zomwe takhala tikukonzekera zigwira ntchito." Fazili adatinso osewera sakumasuka. Akudziwa kuti masewera a Algeria ndi ofunikira kwambiri.

Algeria ndi olimba. Adagonjetsa Cameroon 3-1, Kenya 2-0, Senegal 2-0 ndi Ivory Coast 2-1. Adataya 1-0 yokha kwa Morocco. Mphunzitsi wa Algeria Farid Benstiti adati timu yake iyenera kusewera bwino poteteza. Anati ayenera kupitiriza kugwira ntchito mwakhama osaganizira za masewera omaliza. Ena mwa osewera a Algeria amasewera ku Europe. Inés Boutaleb amasewera ku Auxerre Women. Captain Marine Dafeur amasewera ku Bristol City. Lynda Bendris amasewera ku AS Cannes.

Malawi nawonso ali ndi osewera abwino. Captain Tabitha Chawinga akutsogolera timuyi. Mlongo wake Temwa amathandiza pakuukira. Faith Chimzimu, Rose Kabzere, Leticia Chinyamula ndi Ireen Khumalo nawonso amasewera. Woyang'anira zigoli Mercy Sikelo ndi oteteza Benadetta Mkandawire ndi Chimwemwe Madise ateteza zigoli. Malawi yagonjetsa Nigeria ndi Egypt kuti ipambane gulu lawo. Iyi ndi nthawi yoyamba ku Malawi ku Women's Africa Cup of Nations.

Ngati Malawi ipambana, ipeza mpikisano womaliza. Wopambana mpikisanowu amapeza pafupifupi K3.5 biliyoni. Gulu lachiwiri limapeza pafupifupi K1.3 biliyoni. Koma Tabitha adati ndalama si chinthu chachikulu. Iye anati osewera achichepere akufuna kuwonedwa ndi magulu akuluakulu ochokera padziko lonse lapansi. Osewera aku Malawi akufuna kusewera pa World Cup chifukwa ndi gawo lalikulu kwambiri mu mpira.

en.title: Scorchers Coach Says Team Ready for Algeria Semi-Final
en.body: Malawi's Scorchers women's football team play Algeria on Wednesday in a WAFCON semi-final in Morocco. Head Coach Lovemore Fazili said his players are focused and ready. He said they will not relax before this big match. The Scorchers beat Ghana 2-1 in the quarter-final to reach the semi-finals.
en.body_more:
Fazili told reporters that his team has worked hard to improve all parts of the game. He said they checked the goalkeeper, defenders, and attack. He said the team made mistakes in past matches and must fix them now. "We have to work on all the problems," Fazili said.

Malawi reached the semi-finals for the first time ever at WAFCON. This is their first time at the tournament. Algeria also won their quarter-final match, beating Côte d'Ivoire 2-1. The other semi-final will be Morocco against Cameroon, also on Wednesday. Fazili said his players know what Algeria will do. He said they must stay focused and not make mistakes when they play.

The Scorchers need two more wins to take the title. No team in the semi-finals has won WAFCON before, so there will be a new champion. Fazili said his players are hungry and confident. He said reaching the final would be a very big moment for women's football in Malawi. The team has shown strong desire and unity through the tournament so far.

ny.title: Mphunzitsi wa Scorchers Ati Gulu Lakonzeka Kusewera Semi-Final ku Algeria
ny.body: Timu ya mpira wa azimayi ya ku Malawi ya Scorchers isewera ndi Algeria Lachitatu pa semi-final ya WAFCON ku Morocco. Mphunzitsi wamkulu Lovemore Fazili adati osewera ake ali odzipereka komanso okonzeka. Iye anati sadzapumula masewerawa asanafike. Scorchers adagonjetsa Ghana 2-1 mu kotala-fainali kuti afike mu semi-final.
ny.body_more:
Fazili adauza atolankhani kuti gulu lake lagwira ntchito molimbika kuti liwongolere magawo onse a masewerawa. Anati adayang'ana osewera a zigoli, oteteza, ndi kuukira. Anati gululo lidalakwitsa m'masewera am'mbuyomu ndipo liyenera kukonza tsopano. "Tiyenera kugwira ntchito pamavuto onse," adatero Fazili.

Malawi idafika mu semi-finals koyamba ku WAFCON. Iyi ndi nthawi yawo yoyamba pa mpikisanowu. Algeria idapambananso masewera awo a kotala fainali, ndikugonjetsa Côte d'Ivoire 2-1. Semi-finals ina idzakhala Morocco motsutsana ndi Cameroon, komanso Lachitatu. Fazili adati osewera ake amadziwa zomwe Algeria ichita. Anati ayenera kukhala olunjika komanso osalakwitsa akamasewera.

Scorchers ikufunika kupambana kawiri kuti itenge chikho. Palibe gulu mu semi-finals lomwe lapambana WAFCON kale, kotero padzakhala ngwazi yatsopano. Fazili adati osewera ake ali ndi njala komanso chidaliro. Anati kufika pa fainali kudzakhala nthawi yayikulu kwambiri kwa mpira wa azimayi ku Malawi. Gululi lawonetsa chikhumbo champhamvu komanso mgwirizano kudzera mu mpikisanowu mpaka pano.

en.title: Doll Mabel plans K120 million birthday party in Lilongwe
en.body: Mabel Khonje, known as Doll Mabel, will spend K120 million on her birthday party. The party will be at the Bingu International Convention Centre in Lilongwe on Friday, 14 August. Guests must wear masks. Doll Mabel finished third in Miss Malawi in 2004.
en.body_more:
Doll Mabel lives in the Netherlands but will fly home to Malawi for the party. She said: "This is a party I hold every year to celebrate my birthday. This year the party is happening right here at home in Malawi."

The party is called "A Love Song by Doll Mabel". Doll Mabel has asked many famous Malawian celebrities and important people from different jobs to come. She says this will be one of the biggest parties in Malawi in 2026. All guests will wear masks as part of a special theme. Doll Mabel says the masks have a special message for the party.

Doll Mabel has hosted the Miss Malawi pageant for many years after she finished third in the 2004 competition. She plans this party every year to mark her birthday. This year she chose to bring the party home to Malawi. The masks are not usual for parties, but Doll Mabel wants them to be part of what makes this party different.

The K120 million cost is very big. Many Malawians find it hard to pay for food and other needs. The country has money problems and people do not have enough foreign money to buy things from other countries. This party shows how different life can be for different people in Malawi.

ny.title: Doll Mabel akukonzekera phwando la kubadwa kwa K120 miliyoni ku Lilongwe
ny.body: Mabel Khonje, wodziwika kuti Doll Mabel, adzagwiritsa ntchito K120 miliyoni pa phwando lake lobadwa. Phwandoli lidzachitikira ku Bingu International Convention Centre ku Lilongwe Lachisanu, pa 14 Ogasiti. Alendo ayenera kuvala zophimba nkhope. Doll Mabel adamaliza pa nambala 3 pa Miss Malawi mu 2004.
ny.body_more:
Doll Mabel amakhala ku Netherlands koma adzapita ku Malawi kukachita phwandoli pandege. Iye anati: "Ili ndi phwando lomwe ndimachita chaka chilichonse kuti ndikondwerere tsiku langa lobadwa. Chaka chino phwandoli likuchitika kuno kwathu ku Malawi."

Phwandoli limatchedwa "Nyimbo Yachikondi ya Doll Mabel". Doll Mabel wapempha anthu otchuka ambiri aku Malawi ndi anthu ofunikira ochokera ku ntchito zosiyanasiyana kuti abwere. Iye akuti ili lidzakhala limodzi mwa maphwando akuluakulu ku Malawi mu 2026. Alendo onse adzavala zophimba nkhope ngati gawo la mutu wapadera. Doll Mabel akuti zophimba nkhope zili ndi uthenga wapadera ku phwandoli.

Doll Mabel wakhala akuchita mpikisano wa Miss Malawi kwa zaka zambiri atamaliza pa nambala 3 pa mpikisano wa 2004. Amakonzekera phwandoli chaka chilichonse kuti akumbukire tsiku lake lobadwa. Chaka chino adasankha kubweretsa phwandoli ku Malawi. Zophimba nkhope sizimachitika kawirikawiri pamaphwando, koma Doll Mabel akufuna kuti zikhale gawo la zomwe zimapangitsa phwandoli kukhala losiyana.

Ndalama ya K120 miliyoni ndi yayikulu kwambiri. Anthu ambiri aku Malawi amavutika kulipira chakudya ndi zosowa zina. Dzikoli lili ndi mavuto azachuma ndipo anthu alibe ndalama zokwanira zakunja zogulira zinthu kuchokera kumayiko ena. Phwando ili likuwonetsa momwe moyo ungakhalire wosiyana kwa anthu osiyanasiyana ku Malawi.

en.title: Continental Holdings shares start trading on stock market
en.body: Continental Holdings (CHL) began trading on the Malawi Stock Exchange yesterday. Share prices rose sharply on the first day. CHL is the 17th company to list on the exchange. The shares closed at K342.17, up from the offer price of K195.
en.body_more:
The listing ceremony took place in Blantyre. Reserve Bank of Malawi Deputy Governor Henry Mathanga spoke at the event. He said the listing is important for Malawi's economic growth. Mathanga said the country needs more capital from inside and outside Malawi. He praised retail and institutional investors for their strong response to the offering.

Mathanga told investors that the financial sector has led the way in building Malawi's capital market. He said this sector has pushed for honesty, good management, and proper risk control. Malawi Stock Exchange Board Chairperson Professor James Kamwachale Khomba said CHL's listing shows people have faith in Malawi's economy and its capital market.

CHL Group Chief Executive Officer Robert Abbey said the listing lets more Malawians invest and create wealth. Abbey said more than 10,000 new shareholders have joined the company. Exchange Chief Executive Officer John Robson Kamanga said CHL's listing meets a key goal the Exchange has had since 2021: to bring new companies to the market. Kamanga added that many ordinary Malawians now want to invest in the capital market to build wealth. The listing is expected to give more Malawians a chance to invest in financial services. It also gives CHL access to long-term capital to help the company grow.

ny.title: Magawo a Continental Holdings ayamba kugulitsa pamsika wamasheya
ny.body: Kampani ya Continental Holdings (CHL) inayamba kugulitsa pa Malawi Stock Exchange dzulo. Mitengo ya magawo inakwera kwambiri tsiku loyamba. CHL ndi kampani ya 17 kulembedwa pamndandanda wa magawo. Magawowa anatseka pa K342.17, kuchokera pa mtengo woperekedwa wa K195.
ny.body_more:
Mwambo wolembetsa mabizinesi unachitikira ku Blantyre. Wachiwiri kwa Bwanamkubwa wa Reserve Bank of Malawi, Henry Mathanga, analankhula pamwambowu. Anati kulembetsa mabizinesi ndikofunikira pakukula kwachuma cha Malawi. Mathanga anati dzikolo likufunika ndalama zambiri kuchokera mkati ndi kunja kwa Malawi. Anayamika amalonda ogulitsa ndi mabungwe chifukwa cha kuyankha kwawo mwamphamvu ku zomwe apereka.

Mathanga anauza amalonda kuti gawo lazachuma latsogolera pakumanga msika wachuma ku Malawi. Anati gawoli lalimbikitsa kuwona mtima, kasamalidwe kabwino, komanso kuwongolera zoopsa moyenera. Wapampando wa bungwe la Malawi Stock Exchange, Pulofesa James Kamwachale Khomba, anati kulembetsa kwa CHL kukuwonetsa kuti anthu ali ndi chikhulupiriro mu chuma cha Malawi ndi msika wake wachuma.

Mkulu wa bungwe la CHL Group, Robert Abbey, anati kulembetsaku kumalola anthu ambiri aku Malawi kuti aike ndalama ndikupanga chuma. Abbey anati anthu opitilira 10,000 atsopano alowa nawo kampaniyo. Mkulu wa bungwe la Exchange, John Robson Kamanga, anati kulembetsa kwa CHL kukukwaniritsa cholinga chachikulu chomwe Exchange yakhala nacho kuyambira 2021: kubweretsa makampani atsopano pamsika. Kamanga anawonjezera kuti anthu ambiri aku Malawi tsopano akufuna kuyika ndalama pamsika wachuma kuti apange chuma. Mndandandawu ukuyembekezeka kupatsa mwayi anthu ambiri aku Malawi kuti azigwiritsa ntchito ndalama mu ntchito zachuma. Umaperekanso mwayi kwa CHL wopeza ndalama zogulira kampaniyi kwa nthawi yayitali.

en.title: MCP Lawyer Kadzipatike Hands Himself to Police Over Tax Issues
en.body: George Kadzipatike, a lawyer and MP for Dowa Kasangazi, went to Area 30 police station in Lilongwe. He handed himself to police over a tax warrant. Kadzipatike is the director of legal affairs for the Malawi Congress Party. He said he learned police wanted to arrest him on tax matters.
en.body_more:
Kadzipatike decided to go to police by himself rather than wait to be caught. He said he has never missed paying taxes in 17 years of work as a lawyer. He said the Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA) gave him tax papers each year that said he paid all his taxes. He asked why the MRA now says he owes money when they gave him these papers.

The arrest came after a raid on his law offices. More than 20 police and MRA officers went to his offices in Lilongwe and Mzuzu on Friday. They took files and computers from five lawyers. Kadzipatike said the MRA was being used as a tool to hurt him because of his politics, not because he really owed tax money.

Senior members of the MCP went to the police station to show support. Party secretary-general Richard Chimwendo Banda came. MPs Moses Kunkuyu, Joshua Malango and Anthony Masamba also came. They wanted to check on Kadzipatike and show the party stood with him. Kadzipatike worried that if police held him too long, he would miss meetings for a committee looking into a plane crash at Chikangawa.

Police and the MRA have not given any official statement about the case. Opposition parties and groups that watch the government say it is using state bodies to arrest people who speak against it.

ny.title: Loya wa MCP Kadzipatike Wadzipereka Kwa Apolisi Chifukwa cha Nkhani Za Misonkho
ny.body: George Kadzipatike, loya komanso MP wa Dowa Kasangazi, adapita ku siteshoni ya apolisi ku Area 30 ku Lilongwe. Anadzipereka yekha kwa apolisi chifukwa cha chikalata cholipira msonkho. Kadzipatike ndi director wa zamalamulo wa Malawi Congress Party. Anati adamva kuti apolisi akufuna kumugwira pa nkhani za misonkho.
ny.body_more:
Kadzipatike anaganiza zopita kupolisi yekha m'malo moyembekezera kuti agwidwe. Anati sanaphonyepo kulipira misonkho kwa zaka 17 akugwira ntchito ngati loya. Anati bungwe la Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA) limamupatsa mapepala amisonkho chaka chilichonse omwe amanena kuti amalipira misonkho yake yonse. Anafunsa chifukwa chake bungwe la MRA tsopano limati ali ndi ngongole pamene linamupatsa mapepalawa.

Kumangidwa kumeneku kunachitika pambuyo poti apolisi ndi apolisi a MRA oposa 20 adapita ku maofesi ake ku Lilongwe ndi Mzuzu Lachisanu. Adatenga mafayilo ndi makompyuta kuchokera kwa maloya asanu. Kadzipatike adati bungwe la MRA likugwiritsidwa ntchito ngati chida chomupweteka chifukwa cha ndale zake, osati chifukwa choti ali ndi ngongole yamisonkho.

Akuluakulu a MCP adapita ku polisi kukawonetsa chithandizo. Mlembi wamkulu wa chipani Richard Chimwendo Banda adabwera. Aphungu a Nyumba Yamalamulo Moses Kunkuyu, Joshua Malango ndi Anthony Masamba nawonso adabwera. Ankafuna kukawona Kadzipatike ndikuwonetsa kuti chipanicho chili naye limodzi. Kadzipatike anali ndi nkhawa kuti ngati apolisi atamusunga kwa nthawi yayitali, sadzapezeka pamisonkhano ya komiti yofufuza za ngozi ya ndege ku Chikangawa.

Apolisi ndi MRA sanapereke chikalata chilichonse chovomerezeka chokhudza nkhaniyi. Zipani zotsutsa ndi magulu omwe akuyang'ana boma akunena kuti likugwiritsa ntchito mabungwe aboma kumanga anthu omwe amalankhula motsutsana nalo.

en.title: Hotel cleaner arrested for stealing K2.7 million from US tourist
en.body: Police in Mangochi have arrested a 30-year-old hotel cleaner. Rabbeca Selemani worked at Liwonde Sun Hotel. She took K2.7 million from an American tourist. The tourist, Monica Grant, was 47 years old. The theft happened on 10 August 2026. Police found all the money at Selemani's home.
en.body_more:
Monica Grant had booked a room at Liwonde Sun Hotel at Mangochi Turn Off. She left her money in the room while Selemani cleaned it. That evening at about 10 p.m., Grant found the money was gone. She told police right away at Mangochi Turn Off Police Unit.

The stolen money had two parts. Grant lost K1,878,500 in Malawi Kwacha. She also lost US$502 in dollars. Together, this was worth K2,754,100. Police searched Selemani's home and found all of it. Liwonde Police Station Public Relations Officer Sergeant Ngwashape Msumme told the story to news people.

Selemani comes from Mtila Village. This is in the area of Traditional Authority Sitola in Machinga District. She worked as a cleaner at the hotel. Now she must go to court. The court will decide if she is guilty of theft. A theft is when a person takes something that does not belong to them.

ny.title: Woyeretsa hoteloyo wamangidwa chifukwa choba K2.7 miliyoni kwa alendo aku America
ny.body: Apolisi ku Mangochi amanga munthu wazaka 30 woyeretsa hotelo. Rabbeca Selemani ankagwira ntchito ku Liwonde Sun Hotel. Iye anatenga K2.7 miliyoni kuchokera kwa mlendo waku America. Mlendoyo, Monica Grant, anali ndi zaka 47. Kuba kumeneku kunachitika pa 10 Ogasiti 2026. Apolisi adapeza ndalama zonse kunyumba kwa Selemani.
ny.body_more:
Monica Grant anali atasungitsa chipinda ku Liwonde Sun Hotel ku Mangochi Turn Off. Anasiya ndalama zake mchipindamo pamene Selemani ankaziyeretsa. Madzulo amenewo pafupifupi 10 koloko madzulo, Grant anapeza kuti ndalamazo zatha. Anauza apolisi nthawi yomweyo ku Mangochi Turn Off Police Unit.

Ndalama zomwe zinabedwazo zinali ndi magawo awiri. Grant anataya K1,878,500 ku Malawi Kwacha. Anatayanso US$502 m'madola. Zonsezi zinali za K2,754,100. Apolisi anafufuza nyumba ya Selemani ndipo anapeza zonse. Woyang'anira Ubale wa Apolisi ku Liwonde Sergeant Ngwashape Msumme anauza nkhaniyo kwa atolankhani.

Selemani amachokera ku Mudzi wa Mtila. Apa ndi m'dera la Traditional Authority Sitola m'boma la Machinga. Ankagwira ntchito yoyeretsa ku hoteloyo. Tsopano ayenera kupita kukhoti. Khoti lidzasankha ngati ali ndi mlandu wakuba. Kuba ndi pamene munthu atenga chinthu chomwe sichili chake.

en.title: Malawi women beat Ghana, go to World Cup
en.body: Malawi's women's football team, the Scorchers, won 2-1 against Ghana on Sunday night. The match was a quarter-final of the Women's Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco. This win means Malawi will go to the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup for the first time. The Scorchers also move to the semi-finals of the tournament.
en.body_more:
Ghana scored first after seven minutes. But Malawi hit back five minutes later. Star player Temwa Chawinga scored with a strong shot from the edge of the box. The shot took a deflection and went in. At half-time the score was 1-1.

In the second half both teams played hard and even. Malawi got the winning goal in the 79th minute. Again it came from Chawinga, who passed to Rose Kadzere. The 20-year-old Kadzere shot past the Ghanaian goalkeeper to make it 2-1. Ghana tried to score again but Malawi's defence held firm until the end.

Malawi came to the tournament as the lowest-ranked of the 16 teams. No one thought they would do well. But they have shocked everyone. They beat defending champions Nigeria 3-2 in their first game and Egypt 3-1 in their second game. Now they have gone all the way to the semi-finals. They will face Algeria on Wednesday at the Stade Olympique de Rabat at 7 p.m.

After the match, Football Association of Malawi president Fleetwood Haiya said the team's success shows that Malawi's football is changing for the better. Adelladie Migogo, the president of the National Women's Football Committee, said she was moved to tears. She said the team has made all 20 million Malawians proud. She also noted that this year the team won the COSAFA Cup earlier in the season. The Scorchers' success means Malawi will compete with 31 other nations at the World Cup in Brazil.

ny.title: Azimayi aku Malawi apambana Ghana, apita ku World Cup
ny.body: Gulu la mpira wa azimayi la Malawi, Scorchers, linapambana 2-1 motsutsana ndi Ghana Lamlungu usiku. Masewerawa anali kotala-fainali ya Women's Africa Cup of Nations ku Morocco. Kupambana kumeneku kukutanthauza kuti Malawi ipita ku FIFA Women's World Cup ya 2027 koyamba. Scorchers nawonso apita ku semi-fainali ya mpikisanowu.
ny.body_more:
Ghana idagoletsa chigoli choyamba patatha mphindi zisanu ndi ziwiri. Koma Malawi idabwezanso patatha mphindi zisanu. Wosewera nyenyezi Temwa Chawinga adagoletsa ndi chigoli champhamvu kuchokera m'mphepete mwa bokosi. Chigolicho chidalowa m'malo mwake ndipo chinalowa. Pakati pa nthawi yopuma, zigolizo zinali 1-1.

Mu theka lachiwiri, magulu onse awiri adasewera mwamphamvu komanso mofanana. Malawi idapeza chigoli chopambana mu mphindi ya 79. Apanso chinachokera kwa Chawinga, yemwe adapereka kwa Rose Kadzere.
